description.value: This small wooden or ivory box holds a piece of a saint. While it is on your person, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You have Advantage on saving throws caused by Undead creatures.
You can use each of your Channel Divinity class features one additional time.
When you use Turn Undead, you may choose for the targets to have Disadvantage on their saving throws. This can be used once. You regain its use after a Long Rest.

description.value: A Blessed Stake is a necessary tool in the arsenal of vampire hunters everywhere. This wooden spike, roughly a foot in length, has been blessed by a servant of an Arch Seraph in a special ceremony.

As an Attack action, a wielder can make a melee attack using Strength. Against most foes, this deals **1d4** Piercing damage. Against a Vampire that has the Stunned or Incapacitated condition, a successful attack with the Blessed Stake kills the Vampire.

If the Vampire is CR 10 or lower, the Vampire instantly crumbles to dust. If the Vampire is more powerful, its form remains whole for one year before crumbling to dust. If the Blessed Stake is removed before then, the Vampire rises with 1 Hit Point.
The magical drug comes in the form of a small, round pellet of white powder. If ingested by a Humanoid, that creature is filled with feelings of calm and happiness.
Upon ingestion, you have the following effects for 1d4 hours:

entries: You have Immunity to the Frightened condition.
You gain 3d10 Temporary Hit Points.
Your Speed is reduced by 15 feet.
You have Disadvantage on D20 Tests.
If you cause another creature to make a saving throw, it has Advantage on that save.

description.value: After the effects wear off, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, or you gain 1 Exhaustion level.

This glass sphere contains a raging blizzard inside. It's cold to the touch and vibrates with the gusts of wind trapped within. As a Magic action, you can throw the orb at a creature or object you can see within 30 feet of you, shattering it on impact. When the orb shatters, the blizzard erupts from the glass in a 20-foot-radius Emanation of swirling ice and snow originating from the target. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **4d8** Cold damage, and its Speed is halved until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

The blizzard remains for 1d4 rounds or until targeted by __Dispel Magic__ (as if the effect were a level 5 spell). Any surface within the area is covered in slick ice and sleet, turning the ground within the sphere into Difficult Terrain that remains for the effect's duration. While the blizzard persists, the area is Heavily Obscured.
This cylindrical flask is etched with arcane runes.
Humanoid blood stored in the blood capsule remains fresh for up to one year. The flask stores enough blood to sustain a vampire for one day.

These iron pendants come in pairs and are connected by a powerful bond of self-sacrifice. In order to create this bond, you and an ally with whom you are close perform a brief, 1-minute ritual to connect your destinies and forge a blood pact. When you create this blood pact, you must each agree on a number of Hit Points to permanently sacrifice, reducing your Hit Point maximum by that amount (minimum 1). Once a pact has been forged, trickles of the bound creatures' blood are absorbed into the normally clear gems adorning the faces of these pendants. While the gem is filled in this way, it seems to gently swirl and pulse in time with your heartbeat.

While the bound creatures are wearing their respective pendants and are on the same plane of existence, they're protected by this pact as long as one of the creatures is still conscious. When a bound creature dies, it's immediately revived with 2d10 Hit Points plus twice the number of Hit Points it had sacrificed. When a creature is revived in this way, the other bound creature immediately drops to 0 Hit Points and has the Unconscious condition, ending the blood pact and restoring both creatures' Hit Point maximums to normal; this property ignores any effect that would normally prevent a creature from being reduced to 0 Hit Points. Once the pact is ended in this way, the gems and pendants crack and are no longer magical.

name: Bloodmage Dagger
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Spellcaster)

description.value: This roughly hewn obsidian Dagger is razor sharp and can be used as a Spellcasting Focus. Its handle is covered in small holes that drink in whatever blood runs down the blade. There's a small reservoir for blood at the Dagger's pommel that seems to never completely fill. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Dagger has 5 charges and regains 1d3 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the Dagger, you can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to make a melee spell attack, using your spell attack bonus, against a living creature you can see within 5 feet of you. When you do, an illusory crimson dagger sweeps out toward the creature. On a hit, the target takes Necrotic damage equal to 3d6 plus your spellcasting ability modifier, and you regain Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. If the target is a Construct, Plant, or Undead creature, you don't regain any Hit Points in this way.

Alternatively, while holding the Dagger, you can expend 1 or more charges when you cast a spell using a level 1, 2, or 3 spell slot that targets either yourself or a single creature. The spell slot you use to cast this spell counts as one level higher for each charge you expend in this way. You can't increase a spell slot level beyond level 5 in this way. When you use this property of the Dagger, you also expend 1 Hit Point Die for each charge you expend in this way. Roll a number of Hit Point Dice equal to the number of expended charges and take Necrotic damage equal to the total. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity. If expending charges in this way causes you to drop to 0 Hit Points, the spell fails and you have the Unconscious condition.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

These red goggles have a second set of lenses that magically adjust their distance from your eyes to magnify and focus on targets. While you're attuned to the goggles, you are unaffected by visual obscurity, such as fog or smoke, and can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness—both magical and nonmagical—within 60 feet of yourself. If you already have Darkvision, wearing the goggles increases its range by 60 feet. Additionally, you have Advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on sight.

These lenses are also imbued with several innate spells. While wearing the goggles, you can cast one of the following spells from them, using your spell save DC, but can only target creatures whose blood you can see: __Hunter's Mark__ (level 3 version), __Locate Creature__, or __Scrying__. Casting a spell in this way doesn't require your *Concentration*. Once the goggles are used to cast a spell in this way, they can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

name: Bloody Fiddle

description.value: This scarlet-lacquered fiddle is warm to the touch, like the heat of fresh blood. Though it looks like it has seen better days, its sound is clear and strong.
While you hold the fiddle, you gain a +2 bonus to Charisma (*Performance*) checks, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Song of Stirred Blood
description.value: As a Magic action, you can play a lively or stirring tune on the fiddle. Up to six creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d10 + your Proficiency Bonus, and if you have Bardic Inspiration dice, you can expend and roll one to add it to the total. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Sanguine Curse
description.value: The first time that you play the fiddle after finishing a Long Rest, you take 1 Slashing damage that ignores Resistance. When you use the Song of Stirred Blood property, this Slashing damage increases by 1.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

name: Blunderbuss

description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.value: Cumbersome weapons are difficult to wield but are effective ranged tools for those strong enough to wield them. When making an attack with a Cumbersome weapon, you must use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Scatter weapons can devastate multiple enemies at once. When you take the Attack action and hit a creature with a Scatter weapon, measure the weapon's scatter range from the target's space (or one square the creature occupies if it is Large or larger). Creatures other than the original target that fall within the weapon's scatter range take damage equal to your 1 + your Dexterity modifier (minimum 2). This damage is of the same type you dealt to the original target.

description.value: This distinctive short-range firearm features a dramatically flared muzzle designed to launch shot in a wide spray. Most effective at close range, the Blunderbuss can be considered a precursor to the modern shotgun.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls with this weapon.

name: Blunderbuss of the Grinning Sinner (Legendary)

description.value: This dark, ornate blunderbuss has a brass barrel and a wooden handle etched with arcane symbols. It was the Grinning Sinner's weapon of choice, who imbued it with the power to shoot jinxes and hexes.

The blunderbuss functions as a Musket that ignores Loading, and it can make its own ammunition that deals Necrotic damage on a hit. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it determined by the blunderbuss's rarity. While holding the blunderbuss, you can use the blunderbuss as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Jinxshot (Rare+)
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a blast from the blunderbuss that forces each creature within a 30-foot Cone to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus), taking **2d4** Necrotic damage (Rare) or **3d6** Necrotic damage (Very Rare+) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Sinner's Jinx (Very Rare+)
description.value: Once during your turn when you damage a creature with the blunderbuss, the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus) or be cursed for 1 minute. When it makes a D20 Test while cursed, it subtracts 1d4 from the total. The curse ends if this property is used on another creature.

description.name: Luck Taker (Legendary)
description.value: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that is cursed by this weapon makes a D20 Test and rolls a 19 or 20 on the d20, you can take a Reaction to mimic their luck. The next time you make a D20 Test within 1 minute, change the number you roll on the d20 to the triggering number.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

name: Blunderbuss of the Grinning Sinner (Very Rare)

description.value: This dark, ornate blunderbuss has a brass barrel and a wooden handle etched with arcane symbols. It was the Grinning Sinner's weapon of choice, who imbued it with the power to shoot jinxes and hexes.

The blunderbuss functions as a Musket that ignores Loading, and it can make its own ammunition that deals Necrotic damage on a hit. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it determined by the blunderbuss's rarity. While holding the blunderbuss, you can use the blunderbuss as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Jinxshot (Rare+)
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a blast from the blunderbuss that forces each creature within a 30-foot Cone to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus), taking **2d4** Necrotic damage (Rare) or **3d6** Necrotic damage (Very Rare+) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Sinner's Jinx (Very Rare+)
description.value: Once during your turn when you damage a creature with the blunderbuss, the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus) or be cursed for 1 minute. When it makes a D20 Test while cursed, it subtracts 1d4 from the total. The curse ends if this property is used on another creature.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Blackpowder
description.value: Blackpowder weapons fire projectiles with ear-splitting noise, shredding armor with deadly force. When fired, Blackpowder weapons emit a deafening crack audible 300 feet away. A Blackpowder weapon exposed to heavy rain, submerged, or similarly drenched in water, can't fire until dried for 1 hour. These weapons use paper cartridge bullets as ammunition.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Scatter weapons can devastate multiple enemies at once. When you take the Attack action and hit a creature with a Scatter weapon, measure the weapon's scatter range from the target's space (or one square the creature occupies if it is Large or larger). Creatures other than the original target that fall within the weapon's scatter range take damage equal to your 1 + your Dexterity modifier (minimum 2). This damage is of the same type you dealt to the original target.

description.value: This Heavy Crossbow is made of metal and fires small bolts of electricity instead of normal ammunition. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you pull the string back to load the crossbow, the string crackles with energy and loads a small bolt of lightning ammunition instead. Attacks made with this crossbow deal **1d12** Lightning damage instead of 1d10 Piercing. In addition, whenever you make a ranged attack with this weapon against a metal target or a creature wearing metal armor, you make the attack roll with Advantage.

This crossbow acts as a small lightning rod. If another creature within 10 feet of you takes Lightning damage while you're holding the crossbow, you take **1d6** Lightning damage for every 10 Lightning damage the other creature took.

Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.value: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.

When you hit with Blessed ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Radiant. Also, if the target is Fiend, Fey, or Undead, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.
Designed to open wide wounds, such as with a broad-bladed arrowhead, Brutal ammunition works like a __Brutal__ Melee weapon.

When you hit with Desecrated ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Necrotic. Also, if the target is Celestial, Humanoid, or Plant, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

description.value: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.
When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional **1d4** Fire damage.
Advanced Ammunition that has the Ranging property is lighter and better made than common counterparts. When you fire Ranging ammo, you can increase your weapon's normal range by 50 percent.

A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.

Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.name: War Oil
description.value: A target hit by a piece of Alchemical Ammunition packed with War Oil takes damage as normal for the ammunition, then becomes coated in War Oil for up to 1 minute. Alternatively, you can target a point, such as the ground or a wall, and on an attack roll against AC 10, cause the War Oil to spill out of the ammunition, creating a circular patch of the viscous substance with a 10-foot radius.

War Oil is slick and highly flammable. An area coated in War Oil counts as Difficult Terrain, and a creature that starting its turn in a coated area or enters the coated area for the first time on a turn must succeed a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or gain the Prone condition and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the end of its turn. Additionally, if a creature or area coated with War

Oil is exposed to an open flame or some other source of Fire damage, the oil ignites. The ignited oil burns for two rounds, dealing **2d4** Fire damage to any creature or object who comes in contact with it, and an additional **2d4** Fire damage to any creature that ends its turn while in contact with it. An ignited creature can douse the flames by using an action.
After burning for two rounds, being doused, or remaining unlit for 1 minute, War Oil dries up and ceases to be slippery or flammable.

Ammunition with the Whistling property creates a high-pitched sound after firing. This sound is audible out to 300 feet from the ammo as it flies. Whistling ammo isn't heavier, but it catches the air with intricate baffles to create its sound, so its maximum range is half normal. Whistling ammo deals Bludgeoning damage.
These unremarkable brass knuckles appear well used if not well loved. They are covered in dings and scratches accompanied by the odd stain.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can attempt to maim them. When you do so, the creature must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or be maimed in one of the following ways of your choice. The creature remains maimed until it is targeted by a __Greater Restoration__ spell or similar magic. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Broken Arm
description.value: The creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes.

description.name: Broken Leg
description.value: The creature's Speed is halved.

description.name: Broken Ribs
description.value: The creature has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks and saving throws.

description.name: Broken Skull
description.value: The creature has Disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom ability checks and saving throws.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This strange tome is reputed to have been originally penned by the first human civilization that long ago disappeared beneath the rising seas. It grants its bearer insights needed to peer into secretive realms, at the cost of a growing suspicion of others.

description.name: Language:
description.value: Celestial (XPHB).

description.name: Attunement Check:
description.value: Intelligence (*Arcana*) DC 20. To end your attunement to the Book of Dzyan, a demon or devil must cast __Remove Curse__ on you. The book then disappears in a flash of light.

description.name: Benefits:
description.value: While attuned to the Book of Dzyan, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You can see Invisible creatures and objects within 30 feet of you.
You can read and write Abyssal (XPHB) and Infernal (XPHB).
If you can cast spells, you always have __Guidance__, __Detect Magic__, __Locate Object__, __Fly__, __Divination__, __Contact Deity__, and __Call Deity__ prepared.
Simply touching a wall or object allows you to detect secret doors or similar hidden compartments built into that object within 5 feet of you.
You have Advantage on all Wisdom (*Insight*) checks. If your check result is a 20 or higher, you learn a secret about a creature. This benefit applies only once for a given creature.
The save DC of your spells gains a +1 bonus.

description.name: Drawbacks:
description.value: When you encounter a creature you have never seen before, roll a d20 at the start of each of your turns. On a 10 or higher, you can only use your action that turn to Study it and learn about it. Once you do so, you no longer need to make this roll when that creature is present. This drawback applies to a general type of creature. If you encountered a __Hydra__ this drawback would apply, but it would not affect you when encountering different __Hydras__ in the future.

description.name: Insight-Insatiable Curiosity (+15):
description.value: You cannot bear to think that there are secrets out there that are beyond your grasp. A closed door, a parchment covered with strange runes, or anything else that holds a secret is an irresistible lure to you.

description.name: Lore:
description.value: The Book of Dzyan allows you to automatically succeed all DC 25 or lower checks made to learn about creatures of the planes.

These dark, fleshy boots grant marvelous powers and enhance your normal movement. While wearing the boots, you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover. You can hover up to 20 feet off the ground in this way, leaving behind a thin trail of shadow when you move. In addition, when you take the Dash action while wearing the boots, you can move an extra 10 feet.

The boots have 4 charges and regain 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the boots, you can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to cast either the Expeditious Retreat or __Misty Step__ spell from them. When you cast __Misty Step__ in this way, the silvery mist that surrounds you is instead dark and ominous.

description.name: Curse
description.value: When you pull these cursed boots over your feet for the first time, make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the boots before they extend the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the boots' muscly sinews dig into your legs and feet, interlocking with your own flesh; you take **4d8** Necrotic damage, and you can't remove the boots unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

While wearing the boots, your feet sometimes move in unexpected ways. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) checks and Dexterity saving throws, and when you have the Prone condition, it costs you an extra 10 feet of movement to right yourself. When you remove the boots after being cursed by them, you take another **4d8** Necrotic damage as they painfully tear themselves from your body.
A pair of brown, fur-lined boots that have been finely crafted. The boots are quilted, and have ceramic soles that emit a colourful magical energy.
While wearing these boots, you always land on your feet and cannot be knocked Prone. Additionally, your fall speed is capped at 60 ft per round, and you take no damage from falling.

While wearing these boots, you can jump while in the air as if you'd leapt from solid ground. You can't jump farther than your remaining movement would allow, and you treat all jumps made in this way as if they were standing jumps. When you make a midair jump, faint clouds fly out from under your feet. The boots allow you to jump in this way once before they need to make contact with a solid surface again. Jumping in this way while falling before landing on solid ground allows you to subtract up to 20 feet when calculating damage from the fall.

This crystalline, prismatic wand can channel the illustrative intent of its wielder. While holding the wand, you can magically create a stroke of color in the air, allowing you to draw in midair or on any surface the wand touches. The effect is illusory, visibly magical, radiates Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, and dissipates after 1 hour.
If you attempt to draw on an object that is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw in order to avoid it.

This enlarged, floating snowflake is magically held in place and changes its shape as temperatures fluctuate. While attuned to the pendant you have Resistance to Cold damage and give off an aura of cheeriness. The snowflake has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: __Charm Person__ (1 charge), __Color Spray__ (1 charge), __Hypnotic Pattern__ (3 charges), or __Ice Storm__ (4 charges).
If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the snowflake melts into a puddle of water. After 1 year, the pendant reforms around the magical golden brackets that hold it in place.

This magic item is a glass bottle with a blank label on its front. When a potion or other liquid is poured into the bottle, the contents and effects of the liquid will appear, written in Common, on the label. This writing fades when the bottle is emptied of its contents.

This small vial has a single dose of a fuming, pitch-black poison inside it. When a creature consumes the poison, it takes **4d6** Psychic damage and must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has the Blinded condition and becomes unable to benefit from a Long Rest. While the affected creature sleeps, its dreams are plagued with terrible nightmares. The creature repeats the save every 24 hours. The poison lasts until the creature succeeds on a save against it or is cured by the __Greater Restoration__, Heal, or __Wish__ spell.

This wondrous item has 5 charges. When you reach inside this box, you can expend a charge to pull out a treat. A Beast that eats the snack regains 3d4 + 3 Hit Points and removes one level of Exhaustion or ends one condition on it: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, or Paralyzed.
The box regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn.

This Spear has a hollow metal head filled with a spring-loaded Net. Attacks made with this weapon deal Bludgeoning damage instead of Piercing. When you hit a target with a melee attack using the weapon, you can press a button on the handle as a Bonus Action to deploy the spring-loaded Net. When you do, the target of the attack has the Restrained condition if it's Large or smaller. Once the Net is deployed, you can retract and reset it as a Utilize action. When you do, anything held by the Net is released. Attacks with the Spear are made with Disadvantage while the Net is deployed. If something is Restrained by the Net, you can't use the Spear to make weapon attacks.
You can take a Bonus Action to prime the Net to trigger upon impact, allowing it to deploy the next time the Spear hits a target when it's thrown or swung as part of an attack.
This Net follows the Net's normal rules but is destroyed if it's detached from the Spear. You can replace the Net with a new one by spending 1 minute attaching it to the Spear.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
This white wooden bow is set with four gemstones: a ruby, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

When you hold this bow, as a Bonus Action you can summon a magical arrow composed of one of the four elements. You must still make an attack roll to hit a creature with the magical arrow, and it does only the damage listed.

When you take the Attack action, you can attack with this summoned arrow. If you have a feature that lets you fire more than one arrow on a turn, you can fire other arrows as part of the Attack action.
Each time you summon a magical arrow, you must choose one of the four options below. If you do not fire the arrow within 1 minute of summoning it, it dissolves.

entries: **Arrow of Air**: On a hit, the arrow of air deals **4d8** Lightning damage.
**Arrow of Earth**: On a hit, the arrow of earth deals **4d8** Bludgeoning damage.
**Arrow of Fire**: On a hit, the arrow of fire deals **4d8** Fire damage.
**Arrow of Water**: On a hit, the arrow of water deals **4d8** Cold damage.

When you hit a Humanoid with an Arrow fired from the bow, you can force it to make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is subjected to the effects of a __Dominate Person__ spell for up to 1 minute, as if it were cast by you. This effect doesn't require *Concentration*. In addition, you can take a Bonus Action to magically see through the target's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses the target has. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

These bracers are crafted with fine leathers decorated with magical scales, washed in elemental fluids, elemental dust, and contaminated ichor. The animus used must be from a creature that deals Lightning damage, allowing the bracers to channel the element.
While wearing these magic bracers you gain Resistance to Lightning damage and Immunity to the Shocked condition.

These magic bracers have six charges, and regain all expended charges each day at dawn. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack, you can expend one charge from the bracers to deal an extra **3d6** Lightning damage to the target. A target which takes this damage has the Shocked condition until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Bracers of Arc Lightning requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a creature that deals Lightning damage (such as a Blue Dragon)
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
**[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
**[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
**[Hide]**: Skin
**[Hide]**: Scales

description.value: This magic Quarterstaff is made of a tightly knit length of braided rope. As a Bonus Action, you can use a command word to magically release its knotted form and loosen it into a 50-foot length of Rope. Repeating the command word as a Bonus Action causes the Rope to tighten back up into a Quarterstaff. If a creature has the Restrained condition from the Rope when you use the command word, the Rope tightens around the creature but doesn't crush it. To escape once tightened in this way, the Restrained creature or another creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 15 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success.

Tying an object no larger than 6 inches in any dimension to the end of the Rope doesn't prevent the Rope from reforming into the Quarterstaff. The Rope can only be broken by magical means. If broken, it becomes nonmagical and can't be transformed back into a Quarterstaff.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

name: Brambleheart Quiver
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Druid or Ranger)

description.value: This wooden Quiver can carry your Arrows as well as provide some of its own. The Quiver has 4 magic Arrows grown on it and regrows 1d3 + 1 picked Arrows daily at dawn. These magic Arrows are thorned and remain attached to the Quiver until picked for use (no action required). While you're attuned to the Quiver, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with these magic Arrows. An Arrow grown in this way is no longer magical after 1 minute has passed since it was first picked from the Quiver.

When you hit a target with one of these magic Arrows, you can take a Bonus Action to use a command word. When you do, the target takes **2d4** Piercing damage and the Arrow transforms into a thick field of thorns, duplicating the effect of a __Spike Growth__ spell centered on a point within 5 feet of the target. This effect doesn't require *Concentration* and lasts until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This armor, fashioned from the body of an Empyrean brazen bull, gleams brightly in direct sunlight. While wearing this armor, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class. In addition, you have Resistance to Fire and Radiant damage.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
This adamantine Breastplate of ancient Dhaakan belonged to a hobgoblin hero known as a mighty slayer of Aberrations.
While wearing this armor, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class, any Critical Hit against you becomes a normal hit, and you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Additionally, if you succeed on a saving throw against the Mind Blast ability of a Mind Flayer or other Aberration, you are unaffected, and the effect is reflected back toward the Aberration as if the cone originated from you, including the Aberration in its area of effect.

name: Breastplate of the Morning Light
type: rare (requires attunement by a Cleric or Paladin)

description.value: While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. You can also take a Magic action to cause the armor to emit a flash of blinding, radiant light. When you do, all other creatures within 30 feet of you must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Undead creatures have Disadvantage on this save and take **2d8** Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Named after the Arch Daemon of Fear, this poison creates an extremely powerful hallucinogenic effect that evokes a victim's worst fears. The poison is airborne, and victims need only breathe it in to suffer its effects. On the rare occasions it has been used, people in crammed rooms have jumped out of windows or even killed each other out of abject fear.

Rumors say that the poison has been forbidden even by the Ebon Syndicate, deeming it too dangerous, too extravagant, and too conspicuous. Chances are that such a powerful substance wasn't simply abandoned, however, and other rumors say the Ebon Syndicate still uses a milder version during interrogation.

description.name: Breath of Beleth (Inhaled)
description.value: A creature who breathes and is in the same space as an open container of the substance must succeed at a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

While Poisoned in this way, a creature has the Frightened condition, and it is Hostile to all creatures it can see. If a creature moves within 5 feet of a creature Poisoned in this way, the Poisoned creature must use the Dash action on its turn to move away. If it cannot move away, it must instead use the Attack action against the adjacent creature.

Arcane artillery requires a powerful surge of magical energy to fuel the attack. Wizards and other spellcasters can prime arcane artillery by expending a spell slot, but bombardiers don't have spell slots. Instead, a bombardier charges the weapon by using the Breath of Siberys—a small globe containing a highly refined solution of dragonshards held in a suspended state. While priming arcane artillery, the operator crushes the Breath of Siberys against an engraved brass plate; the sphere dissolves and the weapon is charged.

House Cannith has been developing traditional staffs that can be charged using Breath of Siberys. It takes a Magic action to dissolve the breath on the charging plate, restoring 1d4 charges to the staff. Cannith artificers are working to adapt other charged items to use Breath of Siberys.

This metal brooch features a rotatable dial and can be used to secure a cape or adorn a piece of clothing. While wearing the brooch, you can cast the __Enlarge/Reduce__ spell on yourself by turning the dial toward either the larger or smaller figure adorning the sides of the brooch. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

While under the effects of this spell, you can take a Bonus Action to overload the brooch by forcibly twisting the dial beyond its normal limits. When you do, your size magically changes by an additional category: you either grow a second size larger if you have the "enlarge" effect or shrink a second size smaller if you have the "reduce" effect. Your size can't be larger than Huge or smaller than Tiny by overloading the brooch, and your damage and weight are increased or decreased as if you were affected by a second instance of the __Enlarge/Reduce__ spell.

When you return to your original size after overloading the brooch, you have the Incapacitated condition and a Speed of 0 until the end of your next turn. Once the brooch has been overloaded, its properties can't be used again until 7 days have passed.
This small shield is worn on the forearm. While worn, it gives you +1 to AC, and it can be used as a Martial Melee weapon with Light that deals **1d4** Bludgeoning damage.

This grotesque pair of gloves are made using the barbed exoskeleton and harvested remains of a giant centipede. Immediately after you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made using an Unarmed Strike with the gloves, the target takes **2d6** Poison damage and must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition until the start of your next turn. Unarmed Strikes using these gloves deal either Bludgeoning or Piercing damage (your choice).
Ammunition is required by a weapon that has Ammunition. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

This magic weapon's head is an enchanted cactus that rapidly regrows its missing needles. The first target hit by the weapon on each of your turns takes an extra **1d4** Piercing damage from the attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

These antique quills and writing pads were originally owned by siblings. When the family set up four different branches of their toy-making business across the continent, they developed the magical pads as an easy way to communicate orders and stock levels with one another.
When something is written on one of the four parchment pads, it is visible on all the other parchment pads. Messages are visible for 12 hours, at which point the pads magically absorb the ink.

While burning, this dark candle sheds magical Darkness in a 10-foot radius. It can be lit for up to 1 hour before it's consumed and can be snuffed out or relit like a normal candle as a Bonus Action. Completely covering the candle with something opaque blocks the Darkness. Darkvision can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

name: Cane of Phillip Druskenvald (Legendary)

description.value: This ornate cane is made from polished black wood and is topped with a silver goat-skull ornament. Even a glance at it sparks greed and envy in all but the truly humble.

While holding the cane, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the cane's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Eldritch Glutton (Rare+)
description.value: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that targets only you, you can take a Reaction to consume the spell and store its energy in the cane. The spell has no effect on you. You can take a Magic action to absorb the stored energy to either regain an expended spell slot that is at least one level lower than the triggering spell or gain Temporary Hit Points equal to three times the spell's level. If you absorb a new spell while the cane holds spell energy, the previous energy is lost. Once the cane absorbs a spell, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Allure of Sin (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Dominate Person__ (save DC = 16 + the cane's bonus) from the cane. Once a creature is Charmed by the spell, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Sin-Binder's Call (Legendary)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can summon three Hell Hounds, one Incubus, or one Succubus. They appear in unoccupied spaces you can see within 30 feet of you, obey your commands, and take their turns immediately after yours on your Initiative count. After 10 minutes, they no longer obey you, but if you treated them well, they are Indifferent or Friendly toward you. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: (Requires the __Mark of Making__)
This object looks like a feather.

You can take a Magic action to toss the token 5 feet into the air. The token disappears and an enormous, multicolored bird takes its place. The bird has the statistics of a __Roc__, but it can't attack. It obeys your simple commands and can carry up to 500 pounds while flying at its maximum speed (16 miles per hour for a maximum of 144 miles per day, with a 1-hour rest for every 3 hours of flying) or 1,000 pounds at half that speed. The bird disappears after flying its maximum distance for a day or if it drops to 0 Hit Points. You can dismiss the bird as a Magic action.

name: Cannon

description.value: Smoothbore, muzzleloading Cannons are common fixtures on pirate ships and defensive fortifications, capable of splintering wood and reducing stone to gravel with a thunderous boom. Larger siege weapons of this type exist, and require entire teams of operators to position, load, and fire.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Explode
description.value: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with an explosion from this weapon's projectile. This explosion is a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within the weapon's normal range. Each creature within the Sphere makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. You can create this explosion only once per turn.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.value: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has Ammunition. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

Woven from the remains of an old snarite, this cap provides the wearer with a sense of magical peace and calm that emanates from them. While wearing this cap, you radiate an aura in a 30-foot Emanation. You and allies in this aura have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end effects that include the Frightened condition

This red-tinged armor made from carvaloth scales automatically shifts its color to camouflage you. When you wear this armor, Wisdom (*Perception*) checks made to perceive you have Disadvantage, and you have Advantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

name: Catchpole

description.name: Hafted
description.value: A Hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. After you use the Attack action to attack with a Hafted weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to make a melee attack with the haft. The haft deals **1d6** Bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Entangling
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with an Entangling weapon, you can use a Bonus Action later on the same turn to entangle the target. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10 plus your Proficiency Bonus) or have the Grappled condition until it escapes or until you release the weapon. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target must use an action to make a Strength (*Athletics*) or Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check against the same DC. On a success, the target no longer has the Grappled condition. While a creature is Grappled by this weapon, you can't use it to attack a different creature.

properties: a hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. after you use the attack action to attack with a hafted weapon, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the haft. the haft deals **1d6** bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.value: This gold and jade amulet seems to draw domestic cats to it. While wearing the necklace, you have Advantage on ability checks made to find or call Tiny domestic cats (if there are any) and on Wisdom (*Animal Handling*) checks you make to interact with them.

name: Cauldron of the Vermintoll Coven (Legendary)

description.value: The tarnished cauldron bubbles with a strange, dark liquid. Even in transport, the liquid stays within the rune-emblazoned rim of the cauldron.

While you hold the cauldron, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus determined by the cauldron's rarity to all saving throws, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Size Change (Rare+)
description.value: You can perform a 1-minute ritual to change the cauldron's size from Tiny to Medium, or from Medium to Tiny. It weighs 1 lb. when Tiny and 80 lb. when Medium. As a Medium object, its feet can move. It has a Speed of 20 feet and moves when you command it during your turn (no action required).

description.name: Cookpot (Rare+)
description.value: As part of a Short or Long Rest, you can use the Medium cauldron to prepare food for up to ten creatures. At the end of the rest, each creature that eats gains 2d6 Temporary Hit Points.

description.name: Vermincall (Rare+)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can spill liquid from the cauldron to cast __Conjure Animals__ with it. The conjured spirits take the form of grotesque insects or rats. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Fortifying Gorge (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you use the Cookpot property, one creature of your choice who eats gains a +2 bonus to AC until you finish a Short or Long Rest. During this time, the creature's skin is hardened and monstrous.

description.name: Coven Abomination (Legendary)
description.value: As a Bonus Action, you can drink from the cauldron or administer a draught from it to a creature within 5 feet. For 1 hour, the drinker of the thick, sickly-sweet liquid becomes Large if it is currently smaller than that, its reach increases by 5 feet, and its melee attacks deal an extra **1d8** damage. When the effect ends, the creature has the Incapacitated condition for 1 minute from the agony of its bones shrinking slower than its flesh.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: This strange weapon is fashioned from the mandible of a hivewolf. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon. When you roll a 19 or 20 on your attack roll with this weapon, that attack does an additional **2d6** Acid damage. In addition, you have Immunity to Acid damage while wielding the weapon.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

description.name: Momentum
description.value: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

description.name: Swift
description.value: Swift weapons help you recover quickly from missed attacks. When you miss with a Swift weapon, you have Advantage on the first attack roll you make with the weapon against the same target before the end of your next turn. If that attack hits, it also deals an extra **1d4** damage of the weapon's normal damage type.

name: Cavalry Hammer

description.name: Armor-Piercing
description.value: An Armor-Piercing weapon is a Melee weapon designed to punch through armor or thick hide. When you make an attack roll using an Armor-Piercing weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll if your target is wearing armor or has an Armor Class of 18 or higher.

description.name: Momentum
description.value: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

properties: an armor-piercing weapon is a melee weapon designed to punch through armor or thick hide. when you make an attack roll using an armor-piercing weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll if your target is wearing armor or has an armor class of 18 or higher.
