description.name: Master
description.value: While at the Master tier of Attunement, you have the following additional benefits:

entries: When you hit a creature with the sword, you can attempt to slay it instantly if it has 100 Hit Points or less. The creature makes a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save it dies, and on a success it takes normal damage from the attack. After using this effect, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Your body has atrophied and is slow to heal. After you hit with Dämglesvir, you can't regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn. Instead, any effect that causes you to regain Hit Points during that time grants you an equal number of Temporary Hit Points instead.

description.value: This dark, sea-soaked suit of armor smells of brine and is covered in eldritch runes. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and can breathe underwater.

In addition, while wearing the armor, you can cast the __Evard's Black Tentacles__ spell (save DC 15) from it. When cast in this way, the spell targets a 15-foot square centered on you; it doesn't follow you when you move. This version of the spell doesn't require your *Concentration*, and you are immune to its effects. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

This bronze mask lets out a deep, sonorous ring when struck. When you're reduced to 0 Hit Points or fail a Death Saving Throw while wearing the mask, the three enemies nearest to you within 30 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or take **2d12** Necrotic damage. Targets automatically succeed on this save if they aren't missing any Hit Points or have the Deafened condition. If you're healed or stabilized after dropping to 0 Hit Points, this property of the mask can't be used again until the next dusk.

This dark metal weapon is grimly ornate. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Once per turn when you reduce a Small or larger creature to 0 Hit Points with this weapon, a foreboding, gonglike sound emanates from the blade. Each enemy within 15 feet of the target that's missing any of its Hit Points must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw, taking **1d8** Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
(Requires the __Mark of Sentinel__)
While holding this Shield, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Wisdom (*Perception*) checks. The Shield is emblazoned with a symbol of an eye.

name: Detection Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Detection__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Detection__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Detection Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Detection__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Detection__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Detection Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Detection__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Detection__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

This well-worn leather eyepatch is enchanted with the illusion of an embroidered eye on the front. While wearing the eyepatch over an eye, whether you're missing one or not, you can magically see from the patch as if it were a working eye. The embroidered eye adorning the front of the patch swivels and moves as you look around while wearing it.

In addition, while wearing the eyepatch over an eye, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to magically gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet for 1 hour. If you already have Darkvision, this effect increases its range by 60 feet. For the duration, you can see through magical Darkness as if it were nonmagical Darkness. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Devilbone Button

description.value: This bone button is found on an article of clothing, such as a shirt or coat, and is carved with the tiny image of a devil. It must be attached to clothing that you wear to attune to it. You gain a +1 bonus to saving throws, and it has the following properties.

description.name: Improbable Luck
description.value: When you fail a saving throw while wearing the button, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Protective Bone
description.value: While wearing the button, your Hit Point maximum increases by 5 + your Constitution modifier.

description.name: Diabolic Curse
description.value: When you finish a Long Rest, there is a 1 percent chance the button is mysteriously missing and your Attunement to it ends. A devil with a CR of your level + 3 or CR 20 (whichever is lower) then becomes your enemy and seeks to destroy you. The GM determines the devil's details. When you use the Improbable Luck property, the chance the button disappears increases by 1.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

description.value: This old, weathered War Pick is able to effortlessly break and mold stone. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Creatures and objects made of stone that are hit by the War Pick take an extra **1d8** Piercing damage from the attack. In addition, the weapon has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend 1 charge to cast the __Meld into Stone__ or __Stone Shape__ spell from the weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This thin, hollow Quarterstaff reverberates when it strikes a target. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Finesse property. When you hit a target with the weapon and roll the maximum number on its damage die, the hollow staff shudders and emits a deep, thunderous sound. Roll the weapon's damage die again and add it to the total damage of the attack. This extra damage is Thunder damage.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This magic wooden ring is always covered in splotches of charcoal, ink, or paint, regardless of how well or often it's cleaned. While wearing the ring on a finger, you can touch that finger to a solid surface and begin to draw. The drawing uses your finger to make marks as if it were a piece of charcoal, an ink quill, or a paintbrush (your choice). The marks you make can be in any color. Any drawing made by the ring can be easily smudged or washed away without leaving any marks behind. The ring can have up to a total of 5 square feet covered with drawings in this way at any time. Drawing more than that begins to erase the previous marks, and any mark it makes is magically erased after 24 hours.

This black sugarpaste cookie is made using a grim recipe passed down through generations of Clerics devoted to gods of death. Inside this hollow cookie is a blank strip of enchanted paper whose writing only appears when you break open the cookie. The paper's writing vaguely predicts the manner in which you'll die. When you open this cookie, roll 1d20 and use the table below to determine the paper's prediction.

Once a creature's death has been predicted in this way, all future Doomsday Cookie papers will predict the same outcome for that creature. If a creature dies in a way foretold by the cookie (at the GM's discretion), the cookie's paper transforms into a Spell Scroll of __Revivify__. This scroll can only be used on the creature whose passing it foretold. If the scroll is unused within 1 minute, it crumbles into flour.
Regardless of its grim foretellings, the cookie itself is a delicious snack that is sweet, salty, and smoky.

table.title: Doomsday Cookie Predictions
rows: Your fiery passions burn too hot.
The light of the full moon casts the deepest shadows.
Vainglorious you stumble, entranced by your own reflection.
Great heights bring low all who reach them.
Betrayal strikes deeper than any blade.
Hasty hands make for quick lives.
Getting ahead of yourself may separate you both.
The crushing weight of the world is too much.
Your demise is met with revelry, gnashing jaws, and gluttony.
Beware the viridian, in color and emotion.
Mortality is shed as quickly as skin or clothing.
Hold onto each breath. Savor it as your last.
70 percent of accidents happen in the home.
Stars die as new ones rise.
The stench of failure burns your nostrils.

name: Double Blade

description.name: Double
description.value: A Double weapon functions as two Light weapons, one in each hand, for the purposes of two-weapon fighting. If a Double weapon has Reach, you can use only one of these properties per turn.

description.name: Momentum
description.value: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Set
description.value: Weapons with the Set property allow you to prepare for an oncoming attack. If a target enters your reach while you wield a weapon with this property, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack with the weapon against that target.

properties: a double weapon functions as two light weapons, one in each hand, for the purposes of two-weapon fighting. if a double weapon has reach, you can use only one of these properties per turn.

name: Double-Barrel Shotgun

description.value: A classic design with two loaded barrels, the Double-Barrel Shotgun trades ammo capacity and range for reliability and firepower.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Recoil
description.value: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls with this weapon.

description.name: Blackpowder
description.value: Blackpowder weapons fire projectiles with ear-splitting noise, shredding armor with deadly force. When fired, Blackpowder weapons emit a deafening crack audible 300 feet away. A Blackpowder weapon exposed to heavy rain, submerged, or similarly drenched in water, can't fire until dried for 1 hour. These weapons use paper cartridge bullets as ammunition.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Scatter weapons can devastate multiple enemies at once. When you take the Attack action and hit a creature with a Scatter weapon, measure the weapon's scatter range from the target's space (or one square the creature occupies if it is Large or larger). Creatures other than the original target that fall within the weapon's scatter range take damage equal to your 1 + your Dexterity modifier (minimum 2). This damage is of the same type you dealt to the original target.

description.value: This slender, iridescent Lance is covered in an enchanted finish that resembles the hardened scales of many dragons. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While attuned to the weapon, you know Draconic (XPHB).

This Lance has 8 charges and regains 1d4 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with the Lance, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra **3d6** Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice) to the target. If you expend a charge in this way when you hit a Dragon, it must also succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn.

Whenever you expend a charge in this way, you can expend a second charge to deal an additional **1d6** damage of the same type to the target, and the target can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

description.name: Wyrmling Steed
description.value: In addition, while holding the Lance, you can cast the __Find Steed__ spell from it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. When you cast the spell in this way, you can choose to summon a dragon wyrmling instead of a normal mount by expending a number of charges equal to its Challenge Rating (maximum 2). You determine the kind of dragon summoned, but its alignment toward Good or Evil must be the same as your own; if your alignment is Neutral, you can summon a wyrmling of either alignment. The wyrmling counts as one size larger when used as a mount and can't use its breath weapons.

description.name: Forceful Impact
description.value: If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a Medium or smaller target immediately before making a melee attack roll with the Lance while within 5 feet of the target, you make the attack roll with Advantage. On a hit, you can immediately make an additional melee attack roll with the Lance as part of the initial attack. This additional attack roll must be made against a different target directly behind the first that is within 5 feet of it and isn't behind Total Cover.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This Shield is made from a piece of reclaimed dragon turtle shell. The dragon turtle head sculpture adorning its front is made of brass, and it magically creates and heats a small reservoir of water that replenishes daily at dawn. When you take Fire damage while holding the Shield, you can take a Reaction to use a command word. When you do, the water inside it is superheated, reducing the Fire damage you take by half. The superheated water is released as a dense cloud of steam, causing the area in a 45-foot-diameter Emanation originating from you to be Heavily Obscured. The cloud remains stationary and lasts for 1 minute or until a strong wind (like that created by __Gust of Wind__) disperses it.
Once this property is used, the Shield's reservoir is empty and can't be used again in this way until the next dawn when it replenishes or until it's submerged in nonmagical salt water for 1 hour.

This magnificent blade is crafted from the remains of an ancient dragon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon deals an extra **2d6** damage on a hit if the target is a Dragon. In addition, while you're attuned to this weapon, you know Draconic (XPHB).

description.name: Kindled Cleave
description.value: When you're affected by a Hostile dragon's breath weapon, you can take a Reaction to hold the blade in front of you. When you do, the sword splits the breath weapon's area of effect, leaving you and any creature in a 30-foot Cone behind you unaffected by it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

When you use this property to split a breath weapon that deals damage, the sword gives off an elemental haze corresponding to the dragon's breath weapon. The haze lasts for 1 minute, and it sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. The first target you hit with an attack roll using the sword while it has this haze takes an extra **6d6** damage of the breath weapon's damage type. This extra damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

description.name: Lesser Draconic Resistance
description.value: If you fail a saving throw by 4 or less, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This ear cuff imparts a deeper understanding of draconic history and language upon its wearer. While wearing the ear cuff, you know Draconic. In addition, you gain a +1 bonus to any Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma check you make that involves dragon-related lore.

When you drink this potion, you gain a ravenous thirst for blood and gain the effect of the __Vampiric Touch__ spell (level 6 version, no *Concentration* required) for 1 minute. You can repeat the attack on subsequent turns as a Bonus Action instead of a Magic action.
This liquid is a shimmering red deeper and more intense than natural blood.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: For the duration, as a Magic action, you can gain the effects of the __Gaseous Form__ spell (no *Concentration* required) while you aren't in sunlight. You can also revert to your normal form as a Magic action.

This short purple cape is vaguely iridescent and is difficult to look at from afar. The cape creates illusions of faraway places that are visible only to creatures that are at least 30 feet away from it. While wearing the mantle, creatures more than 30 feet away from you have Disadvantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on sight to perceive you, and they make ranged attack rolls against you with Disadvantage. This property is suppressed while you have the Incapacitated or Restrained condition or are otherwise unable to move.

In addition, you can cast the __Dream__ spell (save DC 16) from the mantle over the course of 1 minute, using yourself as the messenger within the dream. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

Made from a mysterious, magically grown plant, this popular new drug induces vivid hallucinations in which the user's dreams appear to be fulfilled. Some users even see visions of branching possibilities that their life could take.
Upon consuming Dreams Leaves, you can choose to fall into a blissful, trance-like state for 1 hour, during which time you have the Unconscious condition. Taking damage ends the trance early.

If you remain in the trance for the full hour, you awaken with a faint insight into your future. Once before you finish your next Long Rest, you can take a Reaction to reroll a D20 Test and use the new result.

Using this Reaction creates an addiction to Dreams Leaves. While addicted, you have Disadvantage on saving throws. Consuming another dose of Dreams Leaves negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest.
The addiction lasts until you receive a __Greater Restoration__ spell, or until you have not consumed Dreams Leaves for 30 days.

name: Druidic Throwing Club
type: rare (requires attunement by a Druid or Ranger)

description.value: This magic wooden Club has the Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While attuned to the Club, you know the __Shillelagh__ cantrip. If the Club is affected by __Shillelagh__, the spell doesn't end when the weapon is thrown. The Club flies back to your hand immediately after making a ranged attack roll with it.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This magic plant only grows at the base of trees that are often stepped through by dryads. Its leaves continuously shift as if by a breeze. Touching the plant, even gently, causes its leaves to stop their gentle swaying for 1 minute.

Dryadleaf plants only grow up to four leaves at a time and are found in the wild with 1d4 matured leaves. Leaves are fully matured once they have a thin yellow rim. You can take a Magic action to eat a mature Dryadleaf. When you do, you can speak to Beasts, Plant creatures, and nonmagical plants for 1 minute as if you shared a language. Once it's been picked, a Dryadleaf retains this property for 7 days before it wilts.

You can move the plant to a pot over the course of 1 minute. When you do, make a DC 15 Intelligence (*Nature*) or Wisdom (*Survival*) check. On a success, the delicate plant survives the transfer to a new pot. On a failure, the plant is irreversibly damaged and dies.

The plant can survive with surprisingly little air, allowing it to survive in an extradimensional space such as a Bag of Holding or Portable Hole. As long as it's watered lightly each day and given a moderate amount of sunlight (weather and environment permitting), the plant grows 1d4 missing mature leaves every 7 days.

While holding or wearing this item, you can take a Magic action to summon or dismiss a dome of energy that manifests just above your head. This energy repels moderate quantities of frozen and liquid water, such as rain, snow, bird droppings, or other similar nuisances, but can't be used to protect against harsh environmental hazards or attacks. The energy field is typically silvery and translucent. More expensive models have illusions woven into the field; one popular version creates the image of a sunny blue sky overhead.

While holding this wand, you can take a Magic action to instantly clean an area within 10 feet of you that is no larger than 1 cubic foot, removing dirt and grime. There are many variations of the Duster; the two-handed Staff of Cleansing covers a five-foot cube with a single Magic action, while the Bright Basin cleans clothing and cloth objects placed within it.

This thick glove is ornamented with eagle feathers and fitted with an enchanted silk lining. You can use the glove to cast the __Find Familiar__ spell as a Magic action instead of its normal casting time. When you do, the familiar takes the form of an Eagle. The familiar disappears if you are no longer attuned to the glove. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Summon Giant Eagle
description.value: You can focus on the glove for 1 hour to magically summon a __Giant Eagle__ that appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. It disappears when it drops to 0 Hit Points, after 12 hours, or if you dismiss it (no action required). Once the creature disappears, it can't be summoned again until 2 days have passed.

The creature is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your Initiative count, but it takes its turn immediaftely after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

The creature has a carrying capacity of 480 pounds and can travel at a rate of 8 miles per hour while flying. It must rest 1 hour for every 3 hours it flies, and it can't fly for more than 9 hours each time it's summoned.

name: Ear Cuff of the Vampire Bat

description.value: While wearing this ceramic bat ear cuff, you can mentally command the cuff (no action required) to enhance your hearing when you fail a Wisdom (*Perception*) check to that relies on hearing. When you do, the bat's eyes flash with a red glow as its ceramic fangs bite down on your ear, causing you to take **1d4 + 1** Necrotic damage and gain a bonus to the check equal to the amount of Necrotic damage you took, potentially turning the failure into a success. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

This weapon is made of silver spirit energy that phases in and out of reality, making it extremely difficult for living creatures to perceive. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Attack rolls made with the whip against non-Undead creatures have Advantage.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This tome of cooking recipes is enchanted to turn sheets of fine paper into delectable meals. You can write a simple recipe on one of the book's pages over the course of 1 minute. As you do, the paper becomes aromatic, smelling like the cuisine you're writing. The sheet of paper has the taste, texture, and smell of the food described on its page. Eating the sheet as a Magic action nourishes you as if you ate a meal.

If you add a more complex recipe to the book that takes at least 10 minutes to write—potentially using sensory language, descriptions of fine ingredients, or illustrations of the dish—eating the delicious sheet of paper provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day. When a creature eats a sheet detailing one of these complex recipes, its Hit Point maximum increases by 1d10 + its Proficiency Bonus, and it gains the same number of Hit Points, until it finishes a Long Rest. In addition, if the creature has the Poisoned condition or is affected by a magical contagion, it can immediately repeat the save to end it. A creature can only gain the benefits of a complex recipe once every 24 hours.

In addition, you can use this book as a Spellcasting Focus when casting the __Create Food and Water__ spell if you have it prepared or can otherwise cast it. When you do, the food and drink you create can be aromatic and flavorful, recreating recipes of your choice from the book.
The book can hold up to 50 pages. A book found as treasure usually has 3d10 + 10 blank pages as well as 1d10 filled pages containing complex recipes.

When you remove the last page from the book or attempt to rebind the book, roll 1d20. On a 1, the tome bursts into flame, destroying the book and leaving the air in a 60-foot radius smelling like wine and fine cooking. The smell remains in the area for 30 days. After 1 minute, the book's tattered remains transform into a bountiful meal, duplicating the effect of the __Heroes' Feast__ spell. On any roll other than a 1, the book can be rebound using fine paper that costs at least 5 GP per page.

This dark scarf moves slowly on its own and is always wrinkled. The scarf hides an extradimensional space within its folds that can only be reached while its worn. The space can hold 60 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 6 cubic feet. The scarf always weighs 1 pound, regardless of its contents. When you place an object in this space (no action required), your hand vanishes into the scarf's loose folds.

You can't retrieve items placed within the scarf with your hands. Instead, retrieving an item requires you to take a Bonus Action to mentally control the scarf while wearing it, causing its frayed, handlike ends to reach into the space and retrieve a stored item of your choice. The hands can carry up to 10 pounds, and they drop any object weighing more than that on the ground at your feet.

If the scarf is ironed or otherwise flattened, the items stored inside are squeezed out, spilling forth unharmed from the ends of the scarf. If the scarf is destroyed, its contents are lost forever, although an Artifact always turns up again somewhere. A living creature can't be placed inside the scarf.

In addition, while wearing the scarf, you can take a Magic action to mentally control it, using the scarf's frayed hands instead of your own to perform a simple task within 5 feet of you, such as to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. The hands can't attack or activate magic items.

Placing the scarf inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Total Cover is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

This ring, composed of living lightning, is forged from elemental dust compressed into a gem around the lens eye of a construct, washed in the acidic glands of a monster before being set into an animus of an elemental.

When you cast a spell using a spell slot that deals Lightning damage, choose one target that failed its first saving throw against that spell. That creature is Shocked until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating an Electric Charge Ring requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from an Elemental
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
**[Organ]**: Eye from a Construct
**[Organ]**: Glands

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Swift
description.value: Swift weapons help you recover quickly from missed attacks. When you miss with a Swift weapon, you have Advantage on the first attack roll you make with the weapon against the same target before the end of your next turn. If that attack hits, it also deals an extra **1d4** damage of the weapon's normal damage type.

This foul-smelling liquid is made from the saliva of an elemental troll. For one minute after consuming the potion, you can take a Bonus Action to spit energy at a creature within 5 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take **2d6** damage of a type corresponding to the troll whose spittle was used to craft the potion. No damage is inflicted on a successful save.
If the target rolls a natural 20 on its saving throw, the potion explodes inside you. You take **6d6** damage of the type listed for it, and the potion's duration ends immediately.

When you drink this potion, your breath billows out in clouds of fog. For the next 10 minutes, fog and smoke don't hinder your vision, you can cast __Fog Cloud__ up to three times (no *Concentration* required), and you can cast __Misty Step__ up to three times as long as your teleportation begins or ends in an area of fog. This bottle has a base like cobblestone. The glass widens near the top before narrowing again into an iron cap, resembling a lantern. The liquid inside is a murky gray.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: The potion's duration becomes 1 hour, and when you use this potion to cast __Misty Step__, you also gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the start of your next turn.
After you drink this thick, chalky mixture, your Hit Point maximum cannot be reduced for 10 minutes.
This magical feather can sometimes be found growing from a rabenhex. While holding the feather, you can take an action to cast __Remove Curse__. Afterward, the feather becomes nonmagical.

This ring's tiny chains rotate slowly around your finger while worn. Whenever you are affected by a spell that restores Hit Points, such as Cure Wounds or Healing Word, you can take a Reaction to repeat the saving throw against an Enchantment spell that's currently affecting you.

description.name: Shatter Enchantment
description.value: When you fail a saving throw against an Enchantment spell, you can take a Reaction to weaken the spell's grip. You and your allies within 10 feet of you that were targeted by the spell can reroll the save, potentially turning the failure into a success. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 1d4 days have passed.

This swirling potion tastes like iron and bitter raisins. When you drink this potion, you enter a rage that lasts for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. This rage grants you the same effects as the level 1 Barbarian class feature with the following changes:

entries: You can enter and maintain this rage even if you're wearing Heavy armor.

If you end your turn and haven't made an attack roll against an enemy, forced an enemy to make a saving throw, or taken a Bonus Action to extend your rage, you take **1d4** Psychic damage, and the rage extends for another round.

description.value: A stick of Eternal Chalk never breaks or wears down with normal use. When using this chalk, you can choose the color of its marks and whether they emit a faint glow. Any marks you make with this chalk can't be erased for 7 days by anyone except you.

This Spear can slip through the Ethereal Plane to reach its destination. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Force damage instead of Piercing. When you take the Attack action while holding the Spear, you can choose a space you can see within 20 feet of you. The tip of the Spear vanishes and reappears in that space, allowing you to make melee attack rolls with the Spear against a target within 5 feet of that space until the end of the turn. These attacks ignore Half Cover and treat Three-Quarters Cover as if it were Half Cover instead.

description.name: Ethereal Sight
description.value: You can take a Bonus Action to magically see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane and vice versa. This effect lasts for 1 minute. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This large ceramic stein is decorated with dwarven glyphs and topped with a brass lid that can be opened by thumb lever. While the lid is closed and the stein is empty, you can name a nonmagical ale, beer, or mead as a Bonus Action and the stein fills with that liquid.

This cauldron is made using the plated iron from a construct infused with the ash of an elemental. The animus used must be from a dragon which adds both control and potency to the latent elemental magics. The spoon used to stir the cauldron is carved from the bone of a magical creature. This cauldron can heat to boiling temperatures without requiring fire simply by being filled and stirred, and the stews and soups it produces are always delicious and hearty.

During a Long Rest, you can cook enough stew to feed up to three creatures. All creatures who eat a stew from this pot gain 10 Temporary Hit Points. While a creature has these Temporary Hit Points, they gain Valor (1d4).

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating an Everhot Stew Pot requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a Dragon
**[Bones]**: Ribs from a Monstrosity
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
**[Hide]**: Plates

description.value: This large wooden box weighs 25 pounds and is 3 feet long, 2 feet deep, and 2 feet tall. It has rugged ropes on its left and right sides as well as on the top of its lid. The left and right sides of the box are covered by enchanted slabs of stone that magically keep the contents on the inside of the box at a consistent 40 degrees Fahrenheit. The box can hold up to 24 Rations (or an equivalent amount of food). For a creature stuck inside the box to escape, it or a creature within 5 feet of the box must make a DC 10 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing the trapped creature on a success.

While the box's lid is closed and its latch is shut, you can take a Magic action and use a command word to shrink it and its contents down to a more portable size. The weight of the box and anything inside it is halved while it's shrunk in this way, and the box measures a mere 1 foot long by 8 inches deep and tall. You can repeat the command word to return the box to its normal size. Opening the latch, whether by choice or by force, immediately returns the box and its contents to their full size and weight. A living creature can't be shrunk in this way, and the lid and latch are forced open if the box becomes too small for it.

This large sugarbomb is roughly two inches in diameter. Its flavors are a mix of bitter, salty, savory, spicy, sour, and sweet, but also refreshing. The sugarbomb is solid and slowly dissolves in your mouth, changing in flavor each time you reach a new layer. An Everlasting Sugarbomb provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day after 1 minute of letting it dissolve in your mouth. The sugarbomb fully dissolves after 30 uses. You can bite through to the center of the sugarbomb with a successful DC 25 Strength or Constitution check (your choice). If you succeed, make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute and suffer from painful nausea.
While you're attuned to this item, you can cast the __See Invisibility__ spell from it at will.

description.name: Curse
description.value: The Eye of Dendallen is cursed. When you attune to it, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw as you're suddenly overcome with the urge to see what it sees. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately end your attunement to the eye before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save or if you choose not to end your attunement to it, you are cursed until you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic. When you become cursed, you forcefully tear out one of your own eyes, taking **4d10** Necrotic damage, and allow the Eye of Dendallen to crawl into the now vacant socket. If you're already missing an eye, you simply let the eye crawl into that socket without taking the Necrotic damage.

You can see normally through the Eye of Dendallen while it's in your socket. In addition, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already had Darkvision, the eye increases its range by 30 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can focus on looking through the eye to see through magical Darkness for 1 minute as if it were nonmagical Darkness. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

If your attunement to the eye ends after being cursed by it, it pulls itself out of your socket and tries to escape. The eye uses the Spider stat block except its creature type is Undead; it has HP 5; and it doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep. Slaying the eye while it isn't attuned to a creature destroys the item.

description.name: Dendallen Familiar
description.value: The eye also doubles as a gruesome companion while you're attuned to it. As a Magic action, you can command the eye to crawl out of your socket and move independently of you. You control the eye as if you summoned it with the __Find Familiar__ spell, using the statistics above. If the eye drops to 0 Hit Points or you dismiss it, it reappears inside your open socket with a sickly sound. If it does so as a result of dropping to 0 Hit Points, it turns pitch black, and none of its magical properties can be used until the next dusk.
This small, glass sphere is enchanted with weak Divination magics to help you find specific words or phrases in writing. It has a stylized iris etched into the glass.

You can take a Bonus Action to use a command word and then speak the word or phrase you're searching for. The word or phrase magically appears and floats within the sphere. By holding the eye in a free hand, your vision becomes magically enhanced to subconsciously highlight the word or phrase you searched for in a green light wherever you see it. Once you've used the eye's ability for the first time, you can change the word or phrase as many times as you like for the next hour, after which the item can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Eye of the White Worm (Legendary)

description.value: This fist-sized eyeball is cold and clammy to the touch. It is milky-white with purple veins, and its pupil constantly searches for something.

While holding the eye, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the eye's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Thought Scour (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Detect Thoughts__ (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you probe deeper into a creature's mind, it takes **3d8** Psychic damage unless it is a willing target. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Mnemonic Siphon (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Modify Memory__ (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you do, you gain a version of the affected memory as if you experienced it yourself, though you still know the memory isn't yours. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Violation of the Real (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you cast a Conjuration spell using a spell slot that deals damage, or that summons a creature that can deal damage, the spell or creature deals an extra **1d10** Psychic damage to one target the first time it deals damage during a turn.

description.name: Enduring Violation (Legendary)
description.value: When you cast a Conjuration spell with a duration of 1 hour or more, you can extend the duration to 24 hours, and the spell no longer requires *Concentration*. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: (Requires the __Mark of Finding__)

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. While wearing them, you have Advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on sight. In conditions of clear visibility, you can make out details of even extremely distant creatures and objects as small as 2 feet across.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with Fable's End against a Large or smaller creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be banished to a harmless demiplane. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. If you make an attack roll against a Fey with this weapon, you score a Critical Hit and force the save against being banished on a roll of 19 or 20; Fey creatures have Disadvantage on this save. When a creature is banished in this way, the weapon's center emits a brilliant magenta flash of light.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
This crown is woven of aromatic flowers. When you first don the crown after attuning to it, 1d6 + 3 butterflies begin fluttering around it.
When you are hit by a melee attack, you can take a Reaction to release one of the butterflies. The attack misses you and destroys the butterfly instead.
Once all butterflies are destroyed, the crown withers and crumbles to dust.
Once per day as a Magic action, you can use this finely-carved figurine to cast __Find Familiar__.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Familiar Figurine requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any
**[Bones]**: Bones from a Giant
**[Dust]**: Dust from an Elemental or Fey

description.value: Legend has it these hand claws were crafted from the talons of a fabled feline. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

description.name: Darkvision
description.value: While you are holding this magic weapon, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

description.name: Feline Form
description.value: While you are holding this magic weapon, you can cast __Polymorph__ from it. When you do, the spell targets only yourself and the only form you can take is a Cat.

description.name: Nine Lives
description.value: The weapon has 9 charges. While holding it, when you fail a Death Saving Throw you can expend 1 charge (no action required) to succeed on it instead. The weapon loses this property if it has no charges.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
These tarnished copper coins are always found in pairs and bear the portrait of a horned man on one side (heads) and a rowboat on the other (tails).

You can take a Magic action to place the coins over the eyes of a Humanoid that is dead, willing, or has the Unconscious condition. When you do, the coins create an effect based on which side is facing up. You can remove one or both of them from the creature's eyes as a Magic action to end the effect early. If the coins aren't facing the same direction, they have no effect.

description.name: Heads
description.value: While the coins are heads up over the eyes of a creature that has the Unconscious condition, that creature is Stable. If placed over the eyes of a conscious creature, it enters a physical and mental state indistinguishable from death for 1 hour or until the coins are removed, and it has Immunity to Psychic damage for the duration. Once a living creature leaves this state, it can't enter it again for 24 hours.

description.name: Tails
description.value: While the coins are tails up over the eyes of a dead creature, that creature is under the effect of the __Gentle Repose__ spell. Its body can't be detected through magical means, and the soul of the creature can't be contacted.

This festerwood Shield is riddled with amber pustules that glow with a low, yellow light. While holding this magic Shield, the pustules emit Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 5 feet. In addition, while you're holding the Shield, you can take a Reaction when a creature that you can see within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll to attempt to bash that creature with the Shield. When you do, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take **1d4 + 1** Acid damage.

This heavy, dark wood is incredibly strong and forms part of the symbiotic relationship it shares with destructive beetles that live inside. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon, some of the sword's beetles leave the weapon and latch onto the target, biting and hindering it for its next 1d4 turns. While affected by the beetles in this way, the target takes **1d6** Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns and its Speed is halved. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to swat away the beetles, removing them and ending the effect early. If the target is a plant, a Plant creature, or an object made of wood, this effect deals maximum damage to it at the start of each of its turns and lasts for 4 turns unless ended early by a creature.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Graze
description.value: If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

name: Festerwood Fungal Stave
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Cleric, Druid, or Sorcerer)

description.value: This fungal staff has 25 charges and regains 1d10 + 15 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the staff, you can take a Magic action and expend 1 or more charges to cause clusters of noxious mushrooms to magically appear in a number of unoccupied spaces equal to the number of charges you expend. The spaces must be on solid ground within 60 feet of you. Each space becomes Difficult Terrain for the duration of the effect. When a creature moves into or within an area covered by these mushrooms, it takes **2d4** Poison damage for every 5 feet it travels. The mushrooms live for 1 minute or until you dismiss them as a Bonus Action.

In addition, while holding the staff, you can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it (regardless of the spell's normal casting time), using your spell save DC: __Cloudkill__ (5 charges), __Fog Cloud__ (1 charge), __Insect Plague__ (5 charges), or __Stinking Cloud__ (3 charges). A spell cast in this way doesn't require *Concentration*, but it ends at the end of your next turn and must target a point adjacent to a space occupied by your mushrooms.

If you expend the last charge from the staff, roll 1d20. On a 1, the fungi on the staff begin to overgrow, destroying the staff and forcing you to drop it in an unoccupied space adjacent to you. A Hostile Violet Fungus grows in its place.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This magic axe is a favorite among lumberjacks. The axe is made entirely of the magically hardened festerwood and sharpened to a menacing edge. The weapon's glimmering yellow pustules leech acid with each attack, causing any target hit by it to take an extra **1d4** Acid damage. This Acid damage is maximized if the target is a plant, a Plant creature, or an object made of wood.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
This dark wooden mask is strangely insect-like and magically conforms to fit your face. While wearing the mask, you have Blindsight with a range of 10 feet.

In addition, you can take a Magic action to cause beetles to fly out of the mask's mouth, which use the Swarm of Insects (Fly Speed) stat block. The swarm doesn't take its own turns, but you can command it to move and make one attack as part of the action to summon it and then again on each of your subsequent turns as a Bonus Action, using its statistics. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the swarm takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger. The swarm disappears when it drops to 0 Hit Points. If it goes 10 minutes without attacking a creature, it disperses harmlessly to seek food elsewhere. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

This festerwood Rapier's blade is inlaid with scrapings from the Lightspore, the radiant mushroom growing at the center of the Festerwood. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, attuned to the Rapier, you have Advantage on ability checks made to find locations within the Festerwood, and you are immune to magical contagions. While holding the sword, it sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

You can take a Magic action to raise the blade overhead and use a command word. When you do, all other creatures within 30 feet of you are dusted with a sudden wave of magical spores. An ally affected by the spores is suddenly invigorated, allowing it to immediately take a Reaction to either make one attack roll using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike or move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. An enemy affected by the spores must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.
The Rapier has 5 charges for the following properties. It regains 1d3 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk.

description.name: Spells
description.value: While holding the Rapier, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17, +9 attack bonus) from it: __Charm Person__ (level 4 version), __Compulsion__, __Confusion__, __Contagion__, __Faerie Fire__, __Locate Animals or Plants__, or __Moonbeam__ (level 4 version). In addition, you can cast the __Dancing Lights__ cantrip while holding the Rapier.

description.name: Spore Cleansing
description.value: As a Magic action, you can touch a willing creature with the Rapier and expend 1 charge to remove 1 Spore Counter from that creature.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This magical fife can be played as an instrument or wielded as a deadly weapon. You are proficient with the Fife of Dragonsong as both an instrument and Blowgun while you're attuned to it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d6** Thunder damage on a hit.

description.name: Dragonsong
description.value: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to play a powerful note that repels foes and empowers allies. The note is audible out to 100 feet. Enemies within a 15-foot Cone must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **2d6** Thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

Allies within the Cone that can hear the note are bolstered by it instead. Each ally affected by the note gains 2d6 Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

name: Fighting Chain

description.name: Double
description.value: A Double weapon functions as two Light weapons, one in each hand, for the purposes of two-weapon fighting. If a Double weapon has Reach, you can use only one of these properties per turn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Disarming
description.value: A Disarming weapon can catch a foe's weapon, allowing you to remove it from their grasp. When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with a Disarming weapon, you can use your Bonus Action later on the same turn to disarm the target. Both you and the attacker must make opposed attack rolls, ignoring any sources of Advantage and Disadvantage. If your result is higher and the weapon is something the target can drop, the weapon falls from the target's grasp, landing in its space.

If your winning result on the opposed attack roll was a Critical Hit, you can choose for the weapon either to land in a space of your choice up to 15 feet from the target, or to land in your hand if you have a free hand.

The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10 plus your Proficiency Bonus) or have the Grappled condition until it escapes or until you release the weapon. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target must use an action to make a Strength (*Athletics*) or Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check against the same DC. On a success, the target no longer has the Grappled condition. While a creature is Grappled by this weapon, you can't use it to attack a different creature.

description.value: This tendril of flesh, harvested from an Aberration, melds with the body of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your skin during the Attunement process. At the end of this time, the fin burrows into your body and bonds with your muscular system. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Fin Symbiote.
While attuned to the symbiote, you gain the following benefits:
**Symbiotic Health**: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.
**Immovable**: When you would be moved against your will, you can take a Reaction to subtract 10 feet from that movement.
**Aberrant Power**: If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, add +2 to the DC of save DCs for your Aberrant Horror Boons.

**Symbiote Link**: You cannot voluntarily end your Attunement to this magic item. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in 1d4 hours unless you receive a __Remove Curse__ spell before it grows back (which also ends your Attunement).
(Requires Use by a Warforged)

A delicate winged creature, this homunculus was designed to facilitate communication between warforged soldiers during the Last War. A __Final Messenger__ is a Tiny Construct with an AC of 20, 6 Hit Points, and a Fly Speed of 60 feet. It has Immunity to Poison damage and Psychic damage, and all conditions other than Unconscious. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). It has Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. It has no limbs and the only action it can take on its turn is the Dash action.

If you are a warforged, you can take a Magic action to integrate a Final Messenger into your body. While it is part of your body, the messenger cannot be targeted by any attack. You can only have one messenger attached to your body at a time. A messenger can only remain active for 8 hours after it detaches from a warforged body, after which time its energy dissipates and it gains the Unconscious condition. An Unconscious messenger must complete a Short or Long Rest while attached to a warforged, after which it regains its energy, as well as regaining all lost Hit Points.

A Final Messenger holds four pieces of data, accessible only to the warforged it is attached to. While the messenger is attached to you, you can take a Magic action to review the data currently stored within the messenger, and if you choose to, change any or all of these data points.

entries: A destination for the messenger. This can be very specific (a particular apartment in Sharn) or more general (an open marketplace).
A target individual. This could be a specific person or a category ("Any Karrnathi warforged").
A single image recorded through the eyes of a warforged attached to the messenger.
A message of up to 25 words.

description.value: You can release the messenger as a Bonus Action, at which point it flies to its destination by the most direct route possible. Once it reaches the destination it seeks the target individual; if no target has been set, it approaches the nearest warforged.

If you are reduced to 0 Hit Points while a Final Messenger is attached to you, it immediately detaches and seeks out its target. It retains its stored message, but replaces its stored image with the last thing you saw before dropping to 0 Hit Points.

name: Finding Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Finding__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Finding__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Finding Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Finding__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Finding__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Finding Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Finding__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Finding__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

entries: **Ability**: Intelligence
**Utilize**: Reveal the fingerprint left behind on an object and sketch a copy (DC 20), or match a copied fingerprint against a humanoid creature's (DC 15).

description.value: This item allows you to capture the details of a fingerprint that has been left on an object and match them against another creature. It consists of an inkpad, parchment, and talcum powder.

description.name: Tool
description.value: If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

You can throw a Fire Bomb by using an Attack action. Target one space you can see within 20 feet. A creature in this space must make on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature in that space takes **2d6** Slashing damage and **4d6** Fire damage and starts Burning. Creatures adjacent to the attacked space take half that damage and are not Burning.

This breathable cloak sounds like a crackling fire as it billows behind you and can create a small, fiery cyclone around you as you twirl in it. The cloak has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Once on each of your turns, you can expend 1, 2, or 3 charges from the cloak (no action required) and reduce your Speed by 10, 20, or 30 feet, respectively, until the end of the turn in order to spin in place instead. When you do, each creature within 5 feet of you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **1d8** Fire damage for each charge you expended, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the end of the turn.

This hollow metal crossbow was created by a team of kobolds and contains an enchanted ember at its core. The crossbow has 3 charges. While the crossbow has at least 1 charge, the inner ember burns brightly when you hold the weapon. While it burns, the crossbow emits Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet, and any nonmagical Bolt fired from the crossbow catches fire and deals an extra **1d6** Fire damage on a hit.

You can also expend 1 charge as a Magic action to cause the ember to spew forth devastating flames, sending out a wave of fire in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in the Cone must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking **4d6** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried start burning.
The crossbow regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the magical ember inside the crossbow dies out, and the weapon becomes nonmagical.
