name: Fire Wand of the Unbroken Circle

description.value: This wooden wand is carved out of ash and is always faintly warm to the touch. Whenever you grip the wand's handle and later look at your palm, it's strangely covered in a fine layer of charcoal. This wand has 7 charges.

While holding the wand, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast either __Flame Blade__ (2 charges) or __Produce Flame__ (0 charges, or 1 charge to cast at level 5) from it, using an attack bonus of +5. When you cast the __Flame Blade__ spell using this wand, the sword's fiery blade appears above the wand's haft instead of in a free hand.

Whenever you would fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain *Concentration* on a __Flame Blade__ spell cast in this way, you can expend 1 charge as a Reaction to succeed on the save instead. You can only take this Reaction if you're holding the wand.
The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

These multicolored crystals are usually purchased in small bags at festivals and holiday events. As a Magic action, you can throw one of the 1-inch crystals against a solid surface within 20 feet of you to crack it apart. When a crystal breaks, it releases the magic inside. The magic ends at the end of your turn and is entirely sensory.

A bag of Firecracker Crystals comes with 1d4 + 8 crystals inside. Roll 1d8 for each crystal in the bag and record each number rolled. Use these numbers to determine the kinds of crystals found in the bag, as shown on the table below.

rows: Releases a small flash of Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 5 feet, followed by the smell of spices and citrus
Releases small spiraling motes of energy that fizz and fly about in a 5-foot radius
Releases a cloud of bright, verdant smoke that fills a 5-foot-radius Sphere and smells both foul and sickly sweet
Releases a series of comically large bubbles that float outward from the point of impact in a 5-foot radius
Releases the sound of music; the song is random, and plays only enough to make it recognizable as music
Releases a dazzling display of sparkling glitter in a 5-foot radius
Releases a mystery effect; when used, roll on this table again to determine the effect, rerolling until you don't roll an 8

description.value: While wearing these fine golden gloves, you can cast the __Produce Flame__ cantrip from them (+5 to hit). You can hold this flame and other small nonmagical ones (such as that from a Candle or Torch) as if they were tangible objects and can sculpt them like clay. Once sculpted, a flame retains its form for 1 minute before returning to normal. A nonmagical flame carried in this way burns for 1 hour before dying. If you drop or throw a nonmagical flame, it immediately burns out.

When you cast __Produce Flame__ using the gloves, the spell has a duration of 1 hour, instead of 10 minutes. In addition, you can place the spell's conjured flame on the ground at your feet (no action required). The placed flame is harmless and burns out after 1 minute, ending the spell, unless you take a Magic action to pick it back up while within 5 feet of it. Until you pick up the flame, you can't hurl fire as described in the spell unless you cast it again.
In addition, when you take Fire damage while wearing these gloves, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d8 + 2, provided you have a free hand.

description.value: Cumbersome weapons are difficult to wield but are effective ranged tools for those strong enough to wield them. When making an attack with a Cumbersome weapon, you must use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

The weapon holds that amount and type of ammunition, which you can expend before needing to reload the weapon. As a Bonus Action, you may remove a Magazine and then reload it with a new Magazine. A Magazine weapon comes with two empty magazines included in the weapon's cost and weight. An additional empty magazine for a Magazine weapon costs 25 GP. Loading an empty Magazine with ammunition takes 1 minute.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Scatter weapons can devastate multiple enemies at once. When you take the Attack action and hit a creature with a Scatter weapon, measure the weapon's scatter range from the target's space (or one square the creature occupies if it is Large or larger). Creatures other than the original target that fall within the weapon's scatter range take damage equal to your 1 + your Dexterity modifier (minimum 2). This damage is of the same type you dealt to the original target.

description.value: This swirling mixture of red and white liquid is formed from the remains of a coldfire ooze. As an action, the vial of Flammable Tincture can be hurled up to 30 feet at a target, which must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be covered with the liquid. For 1 minute, the creature loses its Immunity or Resistance to Fire damage and has Vulnerability to Fire damage instead.
Ammunition is required by a weapon that has Ammunition. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Flare Gun

description.value: Less a firearm and more a survival tool, a Flare Gun fires a single white-hot flare, useful for distress signals and last-ditch-effort self defense.

description.value: This patchwork shirt is made of enchanted pieces of stitched-together flesh. The shirt has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the shirt, you can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to cast the __False Life__ spell. In addition, while you're *Bloodied*, you regain Hit Points equal to 1d4 plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns. You don't regain Hit Points in this way if you have the Unconscious condition or have taken Fire or Radiant damage since the start of your last turn.

description.name: Curse
description.value: When you put on this cursed shirt for the first time, make a DC 20 Strength saving throw as the fleshy fabric begins to bubble, hiss, and fuse to your skin. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the shirt before it extends the curse to you.On a failed save, you become cursed, and the shirt attaches to your flesh; you can't remove the shirt unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic. Any nonmagical clothing you were wearing under the shirt is destroyed, and magical objects worn beneath it rise to the surface as it seeps through them to attach to your skin.

As long as you remain cursed, you have the Undead creature type in addition to any other creature type you already have, and you have Vulnerability to Radiant damage. When you remove the shirt after being cursed by it, you take **4d10** Necrotic damage as the shirt is peeled from your skin.

This jeweled gauntlet has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with a melee attack roll using a weapon in the hand that's wearing this gauntlet or an Unarmed Strike with it, you can choose to expend 1 charge as part of the attack.

On a hit, the target takes an extra **2d6** Force damage and must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, you're pushed 10 feet away from it instead. Targets two or more sizes larger than you automatically succeed on the save.

This electrum coin has a smiling human woman's face on one side (heads) and a scowling fiendish woman's face on the other (tails). While you're within 30 feet of the coin, you can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to magically summon it to either your hand or pocket. Despite its unique appearance, this coin can be spent like a normal Electrum Piece.

description.name: Fate Flip
description.value: This coin has 2 charges. You can attempt to regain expended charges once every 24 hours by flipping a coin. The Fortune's Fivepence regains all expended charges if the coin is heads or 0 if it's tails.

When the coin is on your person and your total for a D20 Test is 10 or lower, you can expend 1 charge (no action required) to channel the coin's magic and forge your own luck. When you do, flip a coin. If it's heads, add 1d10 to the D20 Test; if it's tails, subtract 1d10 instead. The coin loses this property if using it reduces the total of your D20 Test to 0 or lower.

These bracers can summon another pair of spectral arms below your existing ones. These arms can be summoned as a Magic action and last for up to 1 minute before disappearing. While active, you can use the spectral arms to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.
Each arm can carry up to 10 pounds. The arms stay attached to your torso at all times and can't be moved to other parts of your body, but they can be turned around to face the opposite direction.

In addition, the gems adorning the bracers can amplify the arms' strength for short bursts. The gems have 5 charges and regain 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Bonus Action, you can use a command word and expend 1 charge to magically empower the arms and immediately make two Unarmed Strikes with them. The arms use a Strength modifier of +3 and use your Proficiency Bonus for their attack rolls. They use a damage die of 1d4 and deal Force damage on a hit.
Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge when you summon the arms to double the amount of weight they can carry and increase their duration to 5 minutes.
As an action, a creature in a Thin Place can create a gate to the Ethereal Plane for 1 minute, after which the key crumbles to dust

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating the Fractal Key requires a Rare forge and the following components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a __Fractal Lepidoptera__
**[Bones]**: Bones of any Rare creature

description.value: Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

description.name: Delerium Properties
description.value: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

entries: Immune to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
Resistant to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
Vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an __Antimagic Field__, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 Hit Points. However, delerium geodes release a random [Arcane Anomalies](https://5e.tools/tables.html#arcane%20anomalies_monstersofdrakkenheim) when destroyed.

description.name: Delerium Hazards
description.value: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take **1d6** Necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination.

description.name: Delerium Harvesting
description.value: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

description.name: Uses for Delerium
description.value: Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:

description.name: Spell Component
description.value: Delerium may be used as an Arcane Focus or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

description.name: Magic Items
description.value: Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

description.name: Stable Delerium
description.value: The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk Contamination when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

description.name: Delerium Dust
description.value: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an __Antimagic Field__. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. Improvised Weapons & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a Sling or fashioned into a makeshift Club. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Contamination. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.

This smooth, egg-shaped crystal is about 6 inches tall, weighs 3 pounds, and can shed Bright Light out to a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light is sunlight. As a Bonus Action, you can touch the crystal to mentally control the light's brightness, magically reducing or enlarging its area (out to its maximum range) or snuffing it out.

While holding the crystal, you can use a command word as a Magic action to cause it to release a brilliant wave of light. The light washes over each creature that isn't behind Total Cover in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the crystal. Undead creatures and Fiends in the area must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes **8d6** Radiant damage and has the Blinded condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. Allies of your choice in the area regain 4d6 Hit Points, provided they're living creatures.

Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn, and the crystal's light dims. While dimmed in this way, the crystal can only shed Bright Light out to a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

A pack of oozebeans comes with 4 inside it. When you open a pack, roll 4d8 and record each number. Use these numbers to determine the kinds of oozebeans found in the bag as shown in the table below. You can eat an oozebean as a Bonus Action. Each color has an effect that lasts for 1 minute.

description.name: Upset Stomach
description.value: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

rows: You have Resistance to Acid damage and can safely eat otherwise inedible and nonpoisonous organic materials.
Whenever you successfully grappled a creature or another creature successfully grapples you, that creature takes 1d8 Acid damage.
You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions.
You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.
You have Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on any ability check you make to end the Grappled and Restrained conditions.
You have Resistance to Lightning damage, and you have Immunity to damage from the Magic Missile spell.

name: Frefil's Tiny Tasty Tongue Twisty Sugarbombs

description.value: This small bag of marble-sized gumballs contains 12 enchanted candies. While the color and flavor of each gumball is different, each one's effect is the same. As a Magic action, you can start to chew one of these gumballs to release its magic. While you chewing the candy, you understand the literal meaning of any language that you hear or see signed. If you speak while chewing the gumball, your accent changes to match that of the creature to whom you're listening, allowing you to sound like a local with minimal effort. The candy's magic and flavor fade 5 minutes after you first start to chew it.

description.name: Upset Stomach
description.value: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

While holding this clay statuette of a frog, you can speak its command word and kiss it to cast the spell __Mandy's Feral Follower__, transforming the statuette into a __Commoner__. The commoner created by the statuette retains the memories of each time it is transformed, no matter what appearance you ascribe to it.
Once it has been used, the statuette can't transform again until the next dawn.

This massive utensil comes from the table of a frost giant. Latent jotun magic flows through this makeshift Trident and drives your hunger to nearly aggressive levels. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Immediately after you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using the Trident, you can attempt to bite the same target as a Bonus Action. Make a melee attack roll using your Proficiency Bonus and Strength modifier. It deals Piercing damage on a hit, and uses a damage die of 1d6 as your jaws and teeth are fortified to have the strength of a giant.

description.name: Curse
description.value: While you're attuned to this weapon, your hunger is almost insatiable. You're overwhelmingly compelled to eat twice the amount of food you normally would, and gain 1 Exhaustion level from malnutrition if you go a day without eating enough.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This icy Shield has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack roll, you can expend 1 charge as a Reaction to deal **2d4** Cold damage to the attacker. After the attack, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the Cold damage dealt.

Attacks made with this Dagger deal Cold damage instead of Piercing. When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this magic weapon, the target must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn as it's frozen in place. On a successful save, its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn instead, provided it doesn't have Immunity to the Paralyzed condition.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This potent powder is supposedly created by grinding up the dried organs of a werewolf. Despite the risks associated with its use, it is a favored drug of many wrestlers, boxers, and soldiers because of the raw strength it provides.

Consuming this potion enhances your physical prowess for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, your Strength score becomes 19 (unless it was already 19 or higher), and you have Advantage on Strength ability checks and saving throws.

Prolonged use of Full Moon Extract is risky. You can consume it safely a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Any further use results in painful addiction. While addicted, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.

Consuming another dose of Full Moon Extract negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest, but you must also make a DC 10 Charisma save. On a failure, you become overcome by violent urges for 1 minute. During that time, you cannot take Bonus Actions or Reactions. At the start of each of your turns, you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy. During that turn, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the Attack action, targeting the creature. If your movement doesn't bring you within reach, you must use your Dash action to continue moving toward it.
The addiction lasts until you receive a __Greater Restoration__ spell, or until you have not consumed Full Moon Extract for 30 days.

When you gain the Unconscious condition as a result of being reduced to 0 Hit Points while wearing these black leather boots, you can choose to not gain the Prone condition. While you have the Unconscious condition and are standing in this way, you can walk up to 10 feet on your turn after making a Death Saving Throw.

This delicate mask is made of thinly beaten copper that molds to the skin when worn. While wearing this mask, you can use an action to alter your appearance, including your height, weight, facial features, the sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and distinguishing characteristics for 8 hours. You can make yourself appear as a member of another species, though none of your statistics change. You also can't appear as a creature of a different size, and your basic shape stays the same; if you're bipedal, you can't use this item to become quadrupedal, for instance.
Creatures within 5 feet of you can use an action to make a DC 20 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check to discern your true appearance.
If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Lich Transformation, you also gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class while your appearance is disguised by the mask.
Once you use the mask, you cannot do so again until the following dawn.

This magical helmet once belonged to the Soulfire Phoenix Fara, a paragon to the citizens of the Elemental Plane of Fire who led her people to victory during the Savrayan Wars. While some believe that her ferocity and heroism were a result of phoenix blood running through her veins, others claim that a hero will always rise from the ashes when the time is right.

A spark of this heroism resides within the helmet, imparting its passion and phoenix-like properties to you. While wearing the helmet, you have Resistance to Fire damage, and while you're in combat, magical flames erupt from it. The fire is harmless and sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. If you die while attuned to the helmet, it vanishes in a cloud of embers and smoke and reappears somewhere on the Elemental Plane of Fire.

description.name: Fiery Spirit
description.value: While wearing the helm, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions, and if you roll a 19 or 20 on the d20 for a Death Saving Throw, you regain 1 Hit Points. These benefits also extend to your allies within the helmet's Bright Light.

description.name: Ignite
description.value: While wearing the helmet, you can take a Bonus Action to cast the __Fire Shield__ spell (warm shield only) from it. When you do, you also sprout a pair of flaming wings that last for the duration of the spell and give you a Fly Speed of 30 feet. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Call of the Phoenix
description.value: This helm has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the helmet, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18, +5 spellcasting ability modifier) from it: __Death Ward__ (3 charges), __Flame Strike__ (4 charges), or __Healing Word__ (level 2 version; 1 charge).

description.name: From the Ashes
description.value: If you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright while wearing the helmet, you can take a Reaction to call upon the spark of heroism that resides within the galea to drop to 1 Hit Point instead. When you do, you immediately regain 14 Hit Points, and each creature within 10 feet of you must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking **4d10** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, two flaming wings unfurl from your back, carrying you to an unoccupied space of your choice up to 60 feet away from you without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The wings then disappear. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: The Galea of the Soulfire Phoenix has the following random properties:

entries: 1 [major beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) property
2 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) properties
1 [major detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property

description.name: Destroying the Helmet
description.value: The only way to destroy the helmet is to feed it to an ancient phoenix. The phoenix dies and is immediately reborn as a result of the intense magic stored within the Artifact. When it's reborn, the phoenix has a pronounced crown of golden feathers upon its head. Regardless of how many times it's reborn, the phoenix retains this crown of feathers.

This magic Net is made with fine steel chains and has the Heavy property. Magic, leaden weights line the edge of the Net and send shocking pulses throughout the metal. A creature can't make more than one attack during its turn while it has the Restrained condition from this Net.

While a creature within 30 feet of you has the Restrained condition from the Net, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to cause the Net to magically release a painful wave of electricity, causing the target to take **1d6** Lightning damage. If the target is made of metal or wearing metal armor, it takes **2d6** Lightning damage instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the start of your next turn.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 15 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. A Small or smaller creature has Disadvantage on this check. Destroying the Net (AC 12; 15 HP; Resistance to Slashing damage; Immunity to all other damage) also frees the target, ending the effect. Once destroyed, the Net magically repairs itself over the course of 1d6 + 1 days.

name: Gatling Gun

description.value: Infamous for its rate of fire, the Gatling Gun rotates and fires six or more barrels in succession. This weapon is cumbersome, easily recognizable, and utterly terrifying.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Automatic
description.value: When you make an attack with this weapon, you can choose to make two attacks instead. These attacks are always made with Disadvantage, regardless of circumstance. You can't replace these attacks. If this weapon has Ammunition, these attacks use twice the normal amount of ammunition.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.value: Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

description.name: Delerium Properties
description.value: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

entries: Immune to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
Resistant to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
Vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an __Antimagic Field__, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 Hit Points. However, delerium geodes release a random [Arcane Anomalies](https://5e.tools/tables.html#arcane%20anomalies_monstersofdrakkenheim) when destroyed.

description.name: Delerium Hazards
description.value: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take **1d6** Necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination.

description.name: Delerium Harvesting
description.value: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

description.value: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an __Antimagic Field__. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. Improvised Weapons & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a Sling or fashioned into a makeshift Club. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Contamination. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.

This three-foot warhorn, a revered artifact of Dhakaan, is carved from the tip of a red dragon's horn, banded with adamantine, and covered with runes of power. An inscription in Goblin reads "A mighty dirge for the fallen foe." Ghaal'duur was crafted by Jhazaal Dhakaan, a legendary dirge singer who united the ancient warring clans. Any kech warlord who obtained it would gain great influence among the Heirs of Dhakaan—and any non-Dhakaani that possesses it bears a dangerous burden.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: The warhorn has the following random properties (see "Artifacts" in the Dungeon Master's Guide):

entries: 2 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) properties

1 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property; any goblinoid attuned to the warhorn is immune to the detrimental effects of this property.

description.name: Jhazaal's Presence
description.value: While you are attuned to the warhorn, your Charisma increases by 4, to a maximum of 24.

description.name: The Dragon's Song
description.value: When holding the warhorn in both hands, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells. Bard spells cast using the warhorn gain the following benefits:

entries: If the spell has a duration of 1 minute or longer, its duration is doubled, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
If the spell has a range of 5 feet or greater, its range is doubled.
If the spell is 1st level or higher, it is cast as if from a spell slot 1 level higher than the spell slot you expended.

description.name: The Sound of Victory
description.value: While holding the warhorn in both hands, you can take a Magic action to blow it, empowering your allies and intimidating your foes. For the next 10 minutes, any time an ally within 600 feet of you that can hear you makes an attack roll or a saving throw, it adds 1d4 to the attack roll or save. If the creature is a goblinoid, it adds 2d4 instead of 1d4. Additionally, every enemy within 600 feet of you that can hear you must make a Charisma saving throw against your Bard spell save DC. For the next 10 minutes, whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save. If the target is a goblinoid, it subtracts 2d4 instead of 1d4.
Once you use this property, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

description.name: Destroying the Horn
description.value: It's said that only the fire of Jharaashta, the dragon who sacrificed his horn for its creation, can destroy the horn. But after nine thousand years, most sages assume that the mighty dragon is long dead.
(Requires the __Mark of Hospitality__)
This ceramic jug appears to be able to hold a gallon of liquid and weighs 12 pounds whether full or empty. The jug sloshes when it is shaken, even if the jug is empty.

You can take a Magic action and name one liquid from the Alchemy Jug Liquids table to cause the jug to produce the chosen liquid. Afterward, you can uncork the jug as a Utilize action and pour that liquid out, up to 2 gallons per minute. The maximum amount of liquid the jug can produce depends on the liquid you named.
Once the jug starts producing a liquid, it can't produce a different one, or more of one that has reached its maximum, until the next dawn.

name: Ghallanda Cauldron
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__)

description.value: Engraved with arcane sigils and imbued with ground Siberys shards, this cauldron allows you to prepare food in the blink of an eye. While you have to provide the raw materials, a Ghallanda Cauldron can mystically heat, chill, or flavor contents, allowing precise control over temperature and replicating the flavor of spices or herbs you don't possess. While cooking food in the cauldron, you can reduce its cooking time by 90%, and you gain Advantage on ability checks made using Cook's Utensils.

This bow is hand-carved carefully from the bones of a dryad and stained in the undead blood of vampires. Strung with the hair of a banshee with a powerful wraith animus is placed within the handle. Once the bow's crafting is complete, it fades from its physical form into a semi-corporeal form.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic longbow.
The bow produces its own spectral ammunition which deals Force damage instead of Piercing damage. The ammunition disappears when it hits or misses a target.

While attuned to this weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to see into the Ethereal Plane and see all invisible creatures and objects until the end of your turn. Additionally, you can see through all walls and solid objects within 60 feet of you until the end of your turn. During this time, ammunition fired from this bow passes through solid objects, and you can target enemies within 60 feet of you with your ranged attacks, even if they are behind total cover. You can use this Bonus Action only if you haven't moved during your turn. After you use the Bonus Action, your Speed becomes 0 until the end of your turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Ghost Sight Bow requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Undead Animus from a Wraith
**[Bones]**: Skull from a Dryad
**[Dust]**: Undead Dust
**[Fluid]**: Ectoplasm
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from an Undead
**[Hair]**: Hair from a Banshee

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This club is made from the cleaned and polished femur of a giant, crafted finely into a usable two-handed club. Its tapered hilt is wrapped in stained leather. Fastened to the top of the club is a large troll skull with several monstrous teeth embedded into it like a bone morningstar, giving the weapon a grim appearance. The club is imbued with elemental power from the animus used to power the weapon, which causes it to crackle with elemental power.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic greatclub, and you have Advantage on attack rolls made against Giants.
While attuned to this club you deal an additional **2d6** damage of the type associated with the elemental dust infused into it.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Giant Femur Club requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Giant Animus from a Troll
**[Bone]**: Skull from a Troll
**[Bone]**: Bone from a Giant
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust from a Troll
**[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity
**[Natural Weapons]**: Teeth from a Giant, Beast, or Monstrosity

description.value: The dust component determines the additional damage the club deals. For example, dust from a __Storm Troll__ deals Lightning damage, and dust from an __Eldritch Troll__ causes the club to deal Necrotic damage.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This magic box is made of enamel and bits of bone that stick together with the gummy, red remains of a gibbering mouther. The box weighs 7 pounds and is 1 foot long and 6 inches wide and deep. You can open the box's wooden lid as a Magic action. When you do, the red paste inside the box swirls and forms a toothy mouth that starts incessantly babbling nonsense. A creature takes **1d6** Piercing damage if it touches the red paste and toothy mouth while the box is opened and babbling in this way.

Each creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the open box and can hear the babbling must make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn and rolls a d8 to determine what it does during the current turn. On a 1-4, the creature does nothing. On a 5-6, the creature takes no action or Bonus Action and uses all its movement to move in a random direction. On a 7-8, the creature makes a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

This effect lasts for 1 minute or until the box's lid is closed again as a Magic action. Once this property is used, it can't be used again for 24 hours. Opening the lid again while this property is inactive results in a droning, gurgling sound that turns silent after 1 minute of the box being open. The paste is extremely elastic and can't be removed or separated from the box.

This pair of mithral (Give) and obsidian (Take) Scimitars are connected by a sturdy chain. When you make an extra attack as a result of using the Scimitars' Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage.

The Scimitars have a collective 10 charges and regain 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at midday. When you hit a creature with one of these magic weapons, you can create an effect based on the blade used for the attack, as detailed below.

description.name: Give
description.value: When you hit a creature with Give and expend 1 charge, you and all other creatures within 5 feet of the target (other than the target) gain 2d6 Temporary Hit Points.

description.name: Take
description.value: When you hit a creature with Take and expend 1 charge, the target takes **2d6** Necrotic damage, and you and all other creatures within 5 feet of the target take half as much Necrotic damage.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Entangling
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with an Entangling weapon, you can use a Bonus Action later on the same turn to entangle the target. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10 plus your Proficiency Bonus) or have the Grappled condition until it escapes or until you release the weapon. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target must use an action to make a Strength (*Athletics*) or Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check against the same DC. On a success, the target no longer has the Grappled condition. While a creature is Grappled by this weapon, you can't use it to attack a different creature.

While wearing this armor, you have Resistance to Radiant damage. Whenever a creature hits or misses you with a melee attack, it takes **3** Piercing damage. An attacker can choose to have Disadvantage on its attack roll to avoid this damage.

This glove has 5 charges and regains 1d3 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. When a target that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend any number of the glove's charges. For each charge expended in this way, you gain a +2 bonus to AC for the attack, potentially causing it to miss instead.
The glove's power can't be used if you are already wielding a Shield.

You are proficient with all Musical Instruments while you wear this glove on your dominant hand. In addition, spectral musicians appear behind you to accompany your playing when you play an instrument for at least 1 minute. The musicians are obviously illusory and vanish after you stop playing for 1 minute. While accompanied by the spectral musicians, you have Advantage on Charisma (*Performance*) checks.
In addition, you gain a +2 bonus to your spell save DC for Enchantment spells you cast while performing with the spectral musicians if the target can hear your performance.
Your Dexterity score is 19 while you wear these ratling hide gloves. They have no effect on you if your Dexterity is 19 or higher without them.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Gloves of Ratling Agility requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Hair]**: Fur from any Ratling
**[Hide]**: Skin from any Ratling
**[Organ]**: Guts from any Monstrosity

description.value: These gloves come in pairs, each one tied to a small pocket dimension. The gloves' weight is negligible, regardless of their contents. While wearing the gloves, and holding an object that weighs no more than 20 pounds and can be held in one hand, you can take a Bonus Action to store that object inside the glove's extradimensional space. When an object is stored inside the extradimensional space, you can take a Bonus Action to summon it back into your empty hand. You can only store a single object in each glove's extradimensional space, for a total of two items between the pair.
If a glove is pierced or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane.

Placing the gloves inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Total Cover is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

The ring, made from the bristles of the gold mane boar, sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. This light shines even in areas where magic does not function, or where magical light would normally be suppressed.
These five ornate, golden rings once belonged to an evil monarch. Alone, each is simply an inert piece of dress jewellery. When they are brought together, they hum with dark and ominous energy.

The Gold Rings of Might have 5 charges, and regain 1 expended charge every day at dawn. If you expend the last charge, the item loses its enchantment and does not recharge. If a creature is wearing the Gold Rings of Might, they can innately cast the __Shocking Grasp__ spell as a Magic action.
The wearer can expend 1 charge to cast __Lightning Bolt__ (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.
Alternatively, the wearer can expend 3 charges to cast __Chain Lightning__ (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.
Whether this smooth, pearlescent egg was truly laid by a mythical golden goose is the subject of much debate. What is known for sure, however, is that the egg has remarkable healing powers.

Once per day as an Action, this item can be thrown into an unoccupied space up to 40 ft away and release a wave of healing energy. Creatures within a 30 ft radius Sphere from the point the Goose Egg Healing Grenade lands regain 2d8 + 4 Hit Points, or 5d8 + 4 if they are within a 10 ft radius Sphere. The item's magic heals up to six creatures at a time, starting with the creatures with the lowest Hit Points.
This item's magic has no effect on undead creatures or constructs.
A Grappling Gun can shoot a Grappling Hook attached to a rope up to 150 feet, and the hook catches with a successful DC 10 Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check.

Additionally, if you are falling, you can use a Reaction to shoot the Grappling Gun at an attachable surface to stop your fall. You still must succeed on the check to ensure the Grappling Hook catches on a solid object. On a successful check, you stop your fall.

This soft roll of turf is magically fertile. Its soil is 1 inch thick and allows plants of all kinds to grow well within it. Each roll of turf is 10 feet long and 5 feet wide. Its grass and soil are self-containing and will not grow beyond the size of the carpet. The carpet is so fertile that plants growing in its soil require only half the normal amount of sunlight and water they would normally need in order to grow.

For every 1 inch of the soil's depth, the carpet provides the same amount of nutrition as normal soil does with 1 foot, allowing plants whose roots are normally 1 foot in length to grow with only 1 inch of this soil. Folding the carpet over for added depth, or layering multiple Grass Carpets on top of one another, increases the soil depth to allow for larger plants to grow on the carpet.

The carpet weighs 30 pounds and takes 1 minute to roll up or out. While rolled up, it has a diameter of 1 foot. The carpet can be cut into smaller plots using a magical blade, with each plot measuring at least 1 foot long and wide.

This Dagger's blade is actually a large, enchanted blade of grass. As wind passes over the blade, it creates a soft, sweet note that magically begins to lull creatures to sleep. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Dagger has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using the Dagger, you can choose to forgo the attack's damage and expend 1 charge to attempt to put the creature to sleep. When you do, you swing the blade in a pattern around the creature that creates a magical lullaby. The target must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, at which point it must repeat the save. If the target fails the second save, it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. This effect ends on a target if it takes damage or someone within 5 feet of it takes an action to shake it out of the effect. If the target succeeds on the second save, it takes **3d8** Psychic damage instead.
Creatures that don't sleep, such as elves, or that have Immunity to the Exhaustion condition automatically succeed on saves against this spell.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.
