description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: You feel a sickening terror and Vulnerability when you're alone. If you can't see or hear any Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls and can't concentrate on spells. Creatures conjured or summoned by magic, such as the __Find Familiar__ spell, don't count for this effect.

description.value: While holding this Shield, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to cause it to become wreathed in harmless, magical flames. The flames shed Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The flames last until you repeat the command word as a Bonus Action or until you are no longer holding the Shield.

While holding the Shield, you have Resistance to Fire damage and a +1 bonus to Armor Class. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. In addition, the Shield has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. While the Shield is ablaze, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast __Fire Shield__ (2 charges, warm shield only) or Hellish Rebuke (1 charge, save DC 16) from it.

This 10-foot-long rope smells of sulfur and crackles with embers when moved. As a Magic action, you can lay the rope down in a line next to you on solid ground and use a command word to set it ablaze. When you do, the rope becomes a 15-foot-tall wall of fire along its length. The flames are visible, but not opaque, and are 1 inch thick. Creatures other than you within 5 feet of the wall when the rope is ignited must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take **2d4** Fire damage. A creature must also make this save when it enters the wall of fire for the first time on a turn or ends its turn inside the wall. The flames shed Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet, and they vanish after 1 minute.

The rope rematerializes at the base of the flames when they vanish. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. The rope can only be broken by magical means and becomes a nonmagical Rope once broken.

Designed to aid in the capture and interrogation of mages, this silver syrup is also an effective method of freeing oneself from a cursed item. After drinking this potion, you are incapable of attuning to magic items for 1 hour. During this duration, you can take an action to sever all your Attunements to magic items (even cursed items). At the end of this duration, if you are attuned to any magic items, you die.
(Requires Use by a Warforged)

This item attaches to the body of a warforged, and is designed to serve as one of the following tools that weighs 10 pounds or less: an Artisan's Tools, Forgery Kit, Herbalism Kit, Poisoner's Kit, Thieves' Tools, or a Musical Instrument.

You must incorporate the tool into your body before you can use it. Over the course of 1 hour, you can attach the tool or remove it from your body, remaining in contact with it for the whole hour; this can be done over a Short or Long Rest.

While you're alive, the tool can't be removed from your body against your will. Though the tool has become part of your body, you must still have a hand free to make use of it. You can only have one Integrated Tool attached to your body at a time.

*Eberron: Rising from the Last War introduces the Prosthetic Limb, a Common magic item requiring Attunement which predates the warforged. Prosthetic Limbs come in many forms; one might resemble an organic limb of animated wood, and another could be a metal shell or a construct of force. During the Last War, Karrnath made use of skeletal prosthetics, and more recently, Cannith and Jorasco have produced prosthetics that use the same semiorganic materials as the warforged.*
*Eberron: Rising from the Last War also includes two magic items designed to integrate into a Warforged's forearm: the Armblade and the Wand Sheath. At the DM's discretion, a character of a different species might be able to integrate one of these warforged items into their Prosthetic Limb; the question is if the two can logically work together, or if the style of your prosthetic makes it implausible that it could mesh with a warforged component. If the DM decides it's possible to integrate a component item with the prosthetic, the two could be counted as a single magic item for the purpose of determining the number of magic items you can attune to. If you remove the component from the prosthetic, you immediately lose your Attunement to the component.*

This bow was crafted by a powerful djinni in the Stormheart: a perpetual maelstrom of wind and electricity in the Elemental Plane of Air. Lost to time, it has remained in the storm for untold centuries absorbing the volatile magic that runs rampant there. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

description.name: A Storm Is Coming
description.value: Whenever you roll Initiative while the bow is on your person, you can roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the total.

description.name: Fast as Lightning
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one attack with the bow as a Bonus Action.

description.name: Discharge
description.value: Immediately after you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the bow on your turn, the target and other creatures within 5 feet of it each take **1d8** Lightning damage. Once a creature takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Chained Conduits
description.value: When you hit a target with a ranged attack using the bow, that target becomes a conduit for electricity for 1 minute. You can use a command word as a Bonus Action to cause all such conduits within 60 feet of you to magically electrify. When you do, 5-foot-wide Lines of electricity arc between all electrified conduits that are within 30 feet of each other. Each conduit takes **2d8** Lightning damage, and all other creatures that are in at least one of the Lines must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking **2d8** Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once a conduit has been electrified in this way, it is no longer a conduit. Once a creature or object takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Maelstrom Marksman
description.value: Once on each of your turns when you miss a target with a ranged attack using the bow, you can reroll the attack roll, making the attack against a different target you can see within 30 feet of the first one. You have Disadvantage on this attack roll.

description.name: Zephyr Step
description.value: While holding the bow, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover as long as you are within 20 feet of the ground.

description.name: Embrace the Storm
description.value: While you're attuned to the bow, you're subjected to the chaotic magic of the Stormheart whenever you take Lightning damage. When you do, roll 1d8, using the table below to determine the resulting effect.

rows: You have Vulnerability to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn.
You are thrown 20 feet in a random direction and have the Prone condition.
You have the Deafened condition for 1 hour.
You can't take Reactions for 1 minute.
You cast Fog Cloud centered on a point within 5 feet of you. The spell doesn't require Concentration and you can't end it early, instead lasting for 1d4 rounds.
Up to three random creatures within 10 feet of you take 1d8 Lightning damage.
Your Speed is doubled until the end of your next turn.
You have Immunity to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: Ionbreaker, the Tempest's Reach has the following random properties:

entries: 1 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) property
1 [major beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) property
1 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property
1 [major detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property

description.name: Destroying the Bow
description.value: The bow can be destroyed if it's struck by lightning in the Stormheart at the same time as it's hit by a hammer made of pure adamantine against a similarly adamantine anvil by a creature attuned to the bow. When it's destroyed, each creature within 60 feet of the bow takes **10d10** Lightning damage and **10d10** Force damage. If a creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage, it's immediately turned to ash and can only be revived by a __Wish__ spell.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.
This shimmering breastplate is forged from a giant dragonfly's carapace and adorned with a cape of gossamer fabric. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you wear this armor.
While wearing this armor, you can take an action to transform the cape into dragonfly wings for 1 hour. While this effect lasts, you have a Fly Speed of 30 feet.
If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Fey Transformation, the armor's effect lasts for 2 hours, during which time you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.
Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

These iron tooth caps are inscribed with magical runes. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Bite attacks, and your Bite attacks deal your choice of either force or Piercing damage.
This net is comprised of tiny interlocking iron rings. It acts as a normal Net, with the following changes:

entries: The Iron Net's range is 10 feet.
The DC of the Strength (*Athletics*) check to escape is 15.
The Iron Net has AC 13 and 15 HP.

description.value: Despite the head of this Maul being made from vines, it seems impossibly solid and carries with it a formidable heft. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The Maul has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Immediately after you hit a Medium or smaller target with the Maul, you can expend 1 charge to force the target to make a Strength saving throw; the save DC equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus. On a failed save, the target takes **1d6** Piercing damage and has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This reinforced wooden Shield is covered with ironleaf vines that grant you extra protection. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while holding it. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. In addition, the Shield reforms itself to fit you whenever you transform into a Beast while holding it. When you do, the ironleaf vines and wooden Shield latch onto your bestial form, granting you a +1 bonus to AC. When you revert to your normal form, the Shield also reverts, donning itself upon your arm again.

You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while wearing this suit of armor, which is lined with ironleaf vines. These vines seem to support and quiet the armor's normally loud movements; it doesn't impose Disadvantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks. In addition, the vines dampen the impact you receive from blunt force, granting you Resistance to Bludgeoning damage while you wear the armor.
If you take Fire damage while wearing the armor, the vines wither for 1 minute. For the duration, you gain none of their benefits.

description.name: Mantle of the Wild
description.value: While wearing this armor, you can cast the __Pass without Trace__ spell from it. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
These boots have iron horseshoes embedded in their soles. When you take the Dash action while wearing the boots, you can move an extra 10 feet.

You can click the boots together and cast the __Polymorph__ spell on yourself, transforming into a Riding Horse. When cast in this way, you also retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as your skill and saving throw proficiencies. Any bags you were carrying don't meld into the new form and are magically draped over your torso as saddlebags. Your other gear melds into the new form. You can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

This version of the spell has a duration of 8 hours. The spell ends early if you take any damage while transformed, causing you to take the damage in your normal form instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Jinxed Poker Chip

description.value: This ceramic poker chip is painted with a crocodile's skull on one side. Hoarse laughter sounds when it flips. While you hold the chip, it grants the following properties.

description.name: Jinxed Luck
description.value: When you fail a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to flip the chip. Roll 1d6. On a 4-6, you succeed on the D20 Test instead. After you use this property, roll 1d20. On a 1-5, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Sense Cheating
description.value: If you have proficiency with a Gaming Set, you automatically succeed on ability checks to know if someone in a game you are playing is cheating.

description.name: Cursed Coin
description.value: When you roll Initiative, you must succeed on a DC 0 Charisma saving throw or become cursed until you finish a Short or Long Rest. While cursed, you subtract 1d6 from D20 Tests. When you use the Jinxed Luck property, the saving throw DC increases by 1.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

description.value: When you drink this brightly colored rum, your luck takes a strange turn for 1 hour. For the duration, when you make a D20 Test, roll 1d4. On a 2-4, add the number to your roll. On a 1, roll an extra d20 and use the lowest roll for the test.
This potion is stored in a glass rum bottle marked with crossbones.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: Roll 1d6 instead of 1d4.

name: Jora Charm
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Healing__)

description.value: While wearing this pendant, you gain the following benefits.

description.name: Life Preservation
description.value: Whenever you make a Death Saving Throw, you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10, turning a failed save into a successful one.

description.name: Natural Healing Boost
description.value: Whenever you roll a Hit Point Die to regain Hit Points, double the number of Hit Points it restores.
While wearing these pants, you count as one size smaller while riding a non-Humanoid creature as a mount, provided you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

These infamous weapons, prized by assassins, have a Khyber dragonshard embedded into the pommel that channels the souls of victims, but doesn't itself trap them. There's much debate over the actual fate of the souls of those slain by a Keeper's Fang. Common myth says that the souls of victims are trapped in the Lair of the Keeper, and heroes can seek to reclaim a soul from the Sovereign of Death and Decay. Another myth maintains that these weapons channel souls to the overlord Katashka, and that one must deal with the Lords of Dust to restore a victim. Most Keeper's Fangs were created by the Shaarat'khesh assassins of the Empire of Dhakaan. Rather than ascribing the blade's power to the Keeper--whose existence the Dhakaani reject--they believe these blades utterly destroy the souls of their victims.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you use it to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, the creature is slain and its soul removed. A creature whose soul has been stolen in this way can be restored to life only by means of a __Wish__ spell.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This magic Longbow is adorned with a bear skull and claws. The bow can have up to 4 charges and gains 1 charge whenever you reduce a Small or larger creature to 0 Hit Points with it. For each charge the bow has, a small, etched line appears on the bear skull adorning the weapon. An etched line vanishes from the skull when its charge is expended.

When you hit a creature with a ranged attack roll using the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to cause the target to take an extra **1d8** Psychic damage and make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

When you eat this spicy chocolate sweet as a Magic action, you have Resistance to Fire damage for 1 hour, and you can tolerate temperatures as low as -50 degrees Fahrenheit without any additional protection for the duration.

description.name: Upset Stomach
description.value: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.
This cloak is made from the skin of twenty knifewings. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. If you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While wielding this Halberd, you radiate fervor and valor. When you or an ally within 10 feet of you makes a saving throw to avoid or end the Frightened condition, the creature can add its Proficiency Bonus to the save if it wouldn't already. In addition, when an ally starts their turn within 10 feet of you, their Speed increases by 5 feet until the end of the turn.
You can change the design and color of the weapon's flag by focusing on it over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a Short Rest.

description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While wielding this brass Pike, you radiate health and vitality. When you or an ally within 10 feet of you makes a saving throw to avoid or end the Poisoned condition, the creature can add its Proficiency Bonus to the save if it wouldn't already. In addition, when an affected ally regains Hit Points from a spell or potion while in combat, you can take a Reaction to cause that ally to regain an extra 1d6 + 2 Hit Points.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While wielding this decorated Glaive, you radiate righteousness. When you or an ally within 10 feet of you makes a saving throw to avoid or end the Charmed condition, the creature can add its Proficiency Bonus to the save if it wouldn't already. In addition, when an ally you can see within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction to magically reduce the damage they take by 5. When you do, you take Force damage equal to the amount of damage you reduced in this way.

description.value: If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

description.name: Momentum
description.value: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Set
description.value: Weapons with the Set property allow you to prepare for an oncoming attack. If a target enters your reach while you wield a weapon with this property, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack with the weapon against that target.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Defending
description.value: A Defending weapon is either made for parrying, has advanced techniques for use in parrying, or both. When wielding a Defending weapon, you may use your Reaction when you are hit by a melee attack roll. Roll 1d4 and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack.

These steel-toed boots of dwarven make are adorned with an embossed key on the toe. You can kick an object that contains a mundane or magical means of preventing access and cast the __Knock__ spell on it using the boots. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This Whip is made using the shrunken tentacle of a great sea creature. It still writhes slightly on its own. As a Magic action, you can use the Whip to force a Large or smaller creature you can see within 10 feet of you to make a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice).
On a failed save, the target has the Grappled condition and takes **1d4 + 2** Bludgeoning damage.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing the Grappled creature on a success. While Grappled, the creature takes **1d4 + 2** Bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns.

You can't use the Whip to attack while grappling a creature in this way. While holding the Whip, you can end the grapple at any time (no action required), and if you move more than 10 feet away from the Grappled creature, you drag it with you, but every foot of movement costs you 1 extra foot unless the creature is Tiny or two or more sizes smaller than you.

(Requires the __Mark of Warding__)

You can take a Utilize action to place these shackles on a creature that has the Incapacitated condition. The shackles adjust to fit a creature of Small to Large size. The shackles prevent a creature bound by them from using any method of extradimensional movement, including teleportation or travel to a different plane of existence. They don't prevent the creature from passing through an interdimensional portal.

You and any creature you designate when you use the shackles can take a Utilize action to remove them. Once every 30 days, the bound creature can make a DC 30 Strength (*Athletics*) check. On a successful check, the creature breaks free and destroys the shackles.
While you are holding this wand, you can take a Magic action to instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar source of flame within 10 feet of you.

This magical, gruesome Lance can drain the life force from another creature. The first time on each of your turns that you hit an enemy with a melee attack roll using the Lance, you deal an extra **1d12** Necrotic damage to it, provided the target is a living creature. You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half the Necrotic damage dealt (round up).

description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

name: Lantern of the Chained Reaper (Legendary)

description.value: This ornate Hooded Lantern was once a weapon in the hands of the Chained Reaper, filled with ghastly balefire. Able to pierce the veil, the lantern reveals a glimpse at things hidden from mortal eyes.

While you hold the lantern and it is lit, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence (*Investigation*) and Wisdom (*Perception*) checks determined by the lantern's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Ghostly Flame (Rare+)
description.value: The lantern doesn't require fuel, and it sheds blue-green light. It casts Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. You can snuff or ignite its light as a Bonus Action while you are within 30 feet of it.

description.name: Revealing Flame (Rare+)
description.value: Creatures in the Border Ethereal within the area of the lantern's Bright Light are visible to creatures on the Material Plane. When a creature within the lantern's Bright Light is possessed or affected by the __Magic Jar__ spell, the creature in control appears overlaid on the body in a spectral form.

description.name: Mystic Sight (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Detect Magic__ from the lantern. The spell ends early if you extinguish the light or aren't holding the lantern.

description.name: Summon Spirit (Very Rare+)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can summon a __Ghost__ that appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. The ghost obeys your commands, and it takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. The ghost vanishes after 1 minute, or when it dies. You can't use the lantern's properties, except for Ghostly Flame, during this time.

description.name: Balefire (Legendary)
description.value: You can cast __Scorching Ray__ (level 5 version, +11 to hit) from the lantern. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Warding Light (Legendary)
description.value: The lantern's area of Bright Light offers the protection of a __Magic Circle__ spell. This protection can't operate in the reverse direction, and it ends if you aren't holding the lantern or if you have the Incapacitated condition.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: When you drink this potion, you take **2d4** Necrotic damage. For 1 hour, you have Resistance to Radiant damage, and whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Necrotic damage or its normal damage type.
This potion is thin and gray. It smells vaguely unpleasant but tastes like nothing at all.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This Quarterstaff has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to siphon away some of the target's life force, causing it to take an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage. You regain Hit Points equal the Necrotic damage dealt in this way. This property has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This high-backed armchair made of oak and gold weighs 100 pounds. When you sit in it and speak its command word as a Magic action, it hovers beneath you and can fly through the air. The throne has a Fly Speed of 50 feet, can hover, and can carry up to 400 pounds. The throne stops hovering when you speak its command word again.
By speaking a second command word, you can cast __Unseen Servant__ using the throne. The servant can conjure a spectral trumpet to announce your arrival, in addition to its usual tasks.

Lastly, you can speak a third command word as a Magic action to magically create up to 10 pounds of delicious food of your choice and up to four bottles of wine. Only you can partake of this meal and drink; it instantly becomes stale and sickening in another creature's mouth. Once you have spoken this third command word, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

This magical lyre's strings reverberate with Enchantment magic when you tell lies, allowing you to deceive other creatures more easily. You have Advantage on Charisma (*Deception*) checks you make when you spend at least 1 minute attempting to convince a creature of a lie. In addition, when you cast the __Vicious Mockery__ cantrip while holding the lyre, you have a +1 bonus to your spell save DC. You are proficient with this lyre while you're attuned to it.

description.name: Tool (Musical Instrument)
description.value: If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

This sword's hilt and blade are forged from a single piece of black metal that absorbs the light around it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Cold damage instead of Slashing damage. While attuned to the sword, you gain darkvision to 60 feet and can see in magical darkness.
As a Bonus Action, you can cause the sword to emit magical darkness in a 20-foot radius, and illumination is limited to Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

While the darkness is active, you can use an action to expand or reduce its radius of darkness by 5 feet each, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet each. You can use this feature again at the end of a Short, or Long Rest.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

These 3-foot-long rods are made using a blend of magic and science and normally come in sets of three. The pylons are tipped with a fragment of a blue dragon's horn. A Lightning Pylon can extend electricity to any neighboring pylons to create an electrical barrier between them. Each pylon has an electrical charge. Once a charge has been lost, it takes 12 hours to recharge.

You can place a pylon upright in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you as a Magic action. If a pylon within 5 feet of you has an electrical charge, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to magically electrify it. When you do, the pylon is electrified for 1 minute, after which it loses its electrical charge. Any other pylon with an electrical charge placed within 20 feet of an electrified pylon also becomes electrified, creating a wall of lightning between them that is 10 feet tall and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. You can have up to six pylons connected in this way at a time. Electrified pylons are magically bound to the ground until they lose their charge.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw; creatures made of metal or wearing metal armor have Disadvantage on this save. On a failed save, a creature takes **5d8** Lightning damage, and its Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Lightning damage, and its Speed is halved instead. A creature must also make this save when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn within 5 feet of the wall.

Each magic pylon has AC 15, HP 20, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. A creature that touches an electrified pylon or hits it with a metal Melee weapon takes **1d8** Lightning damage for each pylon connected to it, including itself. When a pylon is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it falls over and loses its electrical charge, ending any connection it has to other pylons. A pylon reduced to 0 Hit Points can't be used again until 2 days have passed, at which point it regains all its Hit Points.
When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the __Polymorph__ spell (no *Concentration* required), turning you into a Frog.
This potion is found in a clay jar shaped and painted like a large frog, with a cork stopper in its back.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: The potion has six doses instead of one.

This terrible venom is extracted and distilled from the deadly lindwyrm. It can be delivered via ingestion or a wound. A creature exposed to the venom must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or take **8d8** Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned, the creature has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity skill checks and saving throws.

This net is made of wire and thread from a suture golem. It can be used in the same manner as a normal Net, but once it restrains a target it coils and twists as if alive. Escaping the Living Net requires a DC 15 Strength (*Athletics*) check.
The Living Net has AC 15 and 15 HP. If destroyed, the net repairs itself after 1 minute.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.
This set of six-sided dice is indistinguishable from nonmagical dice. While attuned to the dice, you gain the following benefits.

description.name: Luck
description.value: The dice have 6 charges and regain 1d6 charges daily at dawn. When you fail a D20 Test, you can expend 1 charge to reroll the test if you don't have the Incapacitated condition. You must use the new roll.

description.name: Loaded
description.value: When you use this magic item to play a dice game, you have Advantage on ability checks made to determine the winner of the game.

This silver lock pick twists and reorients itself to more easily open locks. You gain a +3 bonus on Dexterity (*Sleight of Hand*) checks you make with it to pick a lock. If you roll a 1 on such a check using the lock pick, it casts the __Knock__ spell on the lock before it turns to dust and is destroyed.
If you roll a 1 in this way and use an ability to reroll the die or otherwise change the result, the lock pick becomes nonmagical instead but doesn't cast the spell or turn to dust.

This plate armor is lined with magnetic lodestone harvested from a different plane of existence. While wearing the armor, you can take a Bonus Action to enhance its magnetic polarity for 1 minute. Loose stones, soil, and minerals are immediately attracted to the surface of the armor, granting you a +1 bonus to Armor Class and reducing your Speed by 5 feet.

Using this ability while it already active increases the AC bonus by 1 and reduces your Speed by an additional 5 feet (to a maximum bonus of +4 and a maximum reduction of 20 feet). Once you reach this maximum effect, you can't activate the armor again until the duration has ended.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon can be attuned to by two allies together over the course of a Long Rest. If two creatures are attuned to the weapon in this way, its bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls becomes +2 instead.

This Greatsword is made of two long Scimitars that are held together by a powerful, indeterminate magic. You can use a command word as a Bonus Action to magically separate it into a pair of Scimitars or recombine them into the Greatsword. If you are not already holding the Greatsword or at least one of the Scimitars when you use the command word and are on the same plane of existence as it, you can choose to summon the Greatsword to your free hand or summon one or both Scimitars as individual blades.
The Scimitars have the Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet when separated. They deal Piercing damage when thrown.

Each Scimitar also has its own elemental effect—either cold or fire—that deals an extra 1d6 Cold or **1d6** Fire damage on a hit, respectively. The Greatsword instead deals an extra 1d6 Cold and **1d6** Fire damage on a hit.
The weapon can be used to cast the __Fire Shield__ spell twice, and it regains all expended uses daily at dawn. An attuned creature can't cast the spell in this way more than once each day.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Graze
description.value: If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.
Made with fzeg blood, this silvery potion is dotted with swirling flecks of red. Drinking this liquid removes the curse of lycanthropy.

These brass knuckles are forged from a dull black ore that sparkles with a prism of colors when held to light. They feel heavier than they look like they should be, especially to creatures capable of casting spells.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature that can cast at least one spell, that creature takes an extra **1d6** Force damage. Additionally when you deal damage to a creature that is *Concentrating* using this weapon, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain *Concentration*.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
This bubbling liquid is distilled from the remains of a magebane ooze. You can throw the container at an enemy's weapon or armor, or at a spellcaster.

Make a ranged weapon attack. On a hit, the target takes **1d6** Acid damage. If the weapon was targeted, that weapon takes a -1 penalty to attacks and damage as well. If armor was targeted, that armor takes a -1 penalty to the Armor Class. Both effects end after the wielder or wearer completes a Long Rest.
A spellcaster hit with a Magebane Bomb has a -1 penalty to hit with spell attacks, and the DCs of saving throws against spells they cast decrease by 1 for 1 minute.

name: Mageplate Cap
type: rare (requires attunement by a Sorcerer or Wizard)

description.value: This pointed hat is fitted with chain and metal that have been enchanted with Abjuration magic. The cap has 2 charges and regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn. While wearing the cap, you can expend 1 charge to cast the __Mage Armor__ spell from it, targeting only yourself. When the spell is cast in this way, the magical force appears as platelike armor, and your base AC becomes 15 plus your Dexterity modifier instead of the AC the spell normally provides.

The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with Grievous Wounds, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through Prosthetics, which are covered in Chapter 5 of the Grim Hollow Player's Guide.

Magical versions of Prosthetics can be crafted with properties that mimic existing Wondrous Items or Rings. Typically, these Prosthetics replicate the body part that would wear that item. For example, a Magical Prosthetic leg could replicate the effect of Boots of Elvenkind, while a Magical Prosthetic hand might act as a Ring of Protection.

A Magical Prosthetic has the same rarity as the magic item it mimics. It counts as "wearing" an item of that kind, so if you have a Magical Prosthetic leg that mimics Boots of Elvenkind, you can't wear another pair of magic boots.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d4** Fire damage on a hit. This weapon has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target that is either made of metal or wearing metal armor using the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra **2d8** Fire damage to the target.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

name: Magnum

description.value: Chambered for large-caliber bullets, Magnum revolvers pack the most kick possible into a single shot.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Recoil
description.value: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.
after you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

name: Making Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Making__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Making__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Making Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Making__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Making__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Making Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Making__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Making__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Malleus Macabre
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Fighter or Barbarian)

description.value: This weapon is a blunt but jagged-edged bludgeon that is the object form of a kokela. You gain a +4 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon, and attack rolls made with this weapon score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20. If you have abilities that increase your critical range with melee attack rolls, this weapon scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 17-20.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This weapon is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you spend one year at least a mile away from the weapon. While you remain cursed, you're unwilling to part with the club, always keeping it within reach. You also have Disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.
Whenever you roll a Critical Hit with this weapon, after dealing damage there is a 25% chance the Malleus Macabre casts __Cloudkill__ at level 9 centered on you.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

These magic boots are as sturdy as the feet of a mammoth. While wearing the boots, your weight increases by 50 pounds (although you don't feel any different), and Difficult Terrain composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement. In addition, whenever you're pushed, pulled, or otherwise moved against your will, the distance you would be moved is reduced by 5 feet.
(Requires the __Mark of Hospitality__)

This long key, studded with tiny Siberys dragonshards, can only be used by a creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__. You can take a Magic action to trace the outline of a door in the air with the key and cast __Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion__ without requiring Material components. The spell ends after 24 hours or when you use the key to lock the door and dismiss the effect; at that time, any creatures within the mansion are expelled into an open space near its entrance. Once used, the key cannot be used again until the next dawn.
Structured from the fur and skin of a monstrosity and the horns of a fiend, and coated in the dust of fey creatures, this mantle is imbued with charming energies.
Your Charisma score is 19 while you wear this magic cape. It has no effect on you if your Charisma is 19 or higher without it.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Mantle of Otherworldly Charisma requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Hair]**: Fur from a Monstrosity
**[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity
**[Natural Weapons]**: Horns from a Fiend
**[Dust]**: Fey Dust

description.value: While wearing this enchanted pelt cloak, creatures don't have Advantage on an attack roll against you as a result of having an ally within 5 feet of you if they normally would, such as from the Pack Tactics trait.

name: Manual of Occult Anatomy +1
type: rare (requires attunement by an apothecary or warlock)

description.value: Filled with diagrams showing humans with alien features, this book of strange medical lore is written in monster-blood ink infused with draconic dust and then etched onto parchment pages made from aberration skin. The manuscript is bound in a scale-clad cover.

You can use this manual as a Spellcasting Focus for your Apothecary or Warlock spells. When you use the manual as a Spellcasting Focus, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs of your Apothecary or Warlock spells.

In addition, the book contains the knowledge of an Apothecary Esoteric Theory or Warlock Eldritch Invocation up to a level determined by the manual's rarity and chosen when the item is created, which you gain while you are attuned to it. This determines which class is required to attune to the item.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Manual of Occult Anatomy requires a Workshop and Components of equal rarity to the item created. The Components required are:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Dust]**: Any Dragon Dust
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Monstrosity
**[Hide]**: Scales
**[Hide]**: Skin from an Aberration

name: Marotte of the Lord of Fools (Legendary)

description.value: This wooden fool's scepter is painted with vibrant, unsettling colors that depict a grinning face. While no creature is attuned to the marotte, the face looks like the infamous Chuckles, the Lord of Fools.

While holding the marotte, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the marotte's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Coulrophobia (Rare+)
description.value: When you succeed on a saving throw to avoid the Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to force the creature that created the effect to make the same saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn.

description.name: Fortune's Fool (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Tasha's Hideous Laughter__ (save DC = 16 + the marotte's bonus) from the marotte. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk. You regain use of the spell early if you roll a 1 on the d20 for a D20 Test.

description.name: Fool's Motley (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __False Life__ from the marotte. Any clothing or armor you wear looks like a fool's motley for the duration of the spell.

description.name: Slapstick (Very Rare+)
description.value: When a creature is affected by a __Tasha's Hideous Laughter__ spell you cast, you can choose another creature. When that creature deals damage to the target of the spell, the target has Disadvantage rather than Advantage on its saving throw to end the spell.

description.name: Lord of Fools (Legendary)
description.value: You can cast __Mass Suggestion__ (save DC 19) from the marotte. The effect ends on a creature if it is behind Total Cover or more than 120 feet from you. A creature affected by your __Tasha's Hideous Laughter__ automatically fails its saving throw against this Mass Suggestion. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

properties: each fabled heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. the rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [heirloom rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. an heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. the heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: This skull mask covers the top of your face and offers several benefits while worn. The mask has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the mask, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 16) from it: __Bestow Curse__, __Fear__, __Speak with Dead__, or __Tongues__. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain *Concentration* on a spell you cast in this way. In addition, you understand any written language that you see.

description.name: Curse
description.value: When you place this cursed mask over your face for the first time, make a DC 16 Intelligence saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the mask before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the skin surrounding the mask is riddled with blackened veins and sickly gray skin; you take **5d10** Psychic damage, and you can't remove the mask unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

While wearing this mask, you can't smell or taste anything, and you automatically fail any Wisdom (*Perception*) check that relies on smell or taste. In addition, whenever you roll a 1 on D20 Test, you take **1d10** Psychic damage. When you remove the mask after being cursed by it, it takes 1d4 days for the veins and skin on your face to return to normal.
Your voice also changes. Use the table below to determine the new voice.

rows: Your voice deepens and does not echo.
Your voice becomes raspy and you overly enunciate consonant sounds.
Your voice becomes quiet, almost a whisper, but can still be heard as if spoken at a normal volume.
Your voice becomes high-pitched, and your laugh maniacal.
You slur your words, as if your tongue is suddenly too large for your mouth, and your spit releases a faint hiss as it escapes your mouth.
Your voice becomes that of another ally's and changes each time you complete a Long Rest.

name: Mask of Lethica Nightborne (Legendary)

description.value: This immaculate porcelain mask is painted with delicate violet filigree and once belonged to Lethica Nightborne—a priestess of a goddess of night and healing known as the Nightmother.
While wearing the mask, you gain a +3 bonus to Wisdom and Charisma saving throws determined by the mask's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Gift of the Night Goddess (Rare+)
description.value: You can see normally in magical and nonmagical Dim Light and Darkness.

description.name: Soothing Darkness (Rare+)
description.value: Creatures of your choice in the area of a __Darkness__ spell that you cast have Resistance to Psychic damage.

description.name: Whispers of Night (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Darkness__ from the mask. This property can be used twice (Very Rare+: four times), regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Balm of Midnight (Very Rare+)
description.value: At the start of your turn, a Frightened creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the condition ends, and if the creature is in an area of Darkness, it gains 2d10 Temporary Hit Points.

description.name: Offering of Burdens (Legendary)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can touch a willing creature with Exhaustion levels and transfer any number of Exhaustion levels to yourself, then remove up to two Exhaustion levels from yourself and regain one expended spell slot of level 5 or lower. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Surcease of Sorrows (Legendary)
description.value: You can cast __Modify Memory__ from the mask (save DC 19). If the target voluntarily fails the saving throw, you can choose a memory that happened at any time in its lifespan. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.
