description.value: This magic mask is made from the skull of a particular monstrosity (with a Challenge Rating of 6 or lower). The skull is carved into a mask, engraved with aberrant dust, and then boiled in a vat of mimic mucus, the flesh of a doppelganger, and acidic bile. Finally, a vessel containing the animus of any creature with the Shapechanger trait is placed upon the forehead of the mask, channeling its shapechanging magic.
While attuned to the mask, you can expend two uses of your Wild Shape feature to transform into the monstrosity associated with the mask, instead of a Beast.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Mask of Monstrous Forms requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a creature that has the Shapechanger trait
**[Bones]**: Skull of a Monstrosity*
**[Dust]**: Aberrant Dust
**[Fluid]**: Acidic Bile
**[Fluid]**: Mucus from a Mimic
**[Organ]**: Flesh from a Doppelganger

description.value: ** The Monstrosity used for this mask determines the form of the shapechange.*

Carved from yew, this mask is shaped in the likeness of a beast's visage and has 3 charges. While wearing the mask, you can expend 1 charge to cast __Polymorph__ on yourself, with a maximum duration of 1 minute.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This item is cursed. Wearing it curses you until you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic. While you remain cursed, you cannot remove the mask.

This mask looks like a normal wooden mask while no one is attuned to it. When you attune to the mask, your patron's lingering presence over you magically reshapes it to represent the visage of your patron. While wearing this mask, you can cast one spell from the table of spells shown in your level 3 Warlock subclass feature without expending a spell slot. The spell must be of a level equal to or less than your Warlock spell slot level. A spell cast in this way is always cast at its lowest level, regardless of your normal Warlock spell slot level. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

description.name: Delerium Properties
description.value: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

entries: Immune to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
Resistant to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
Vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an __Antimagic Field__, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 Hit Points. However, delerium geodes release a random [Arcane Anomalies](https://5e.tools/tables.html#arcane%20anomalies_monstersofdrakkenheim) when destroyed.

description.name: Delerium Hazards
description.value: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take **1d6** Necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination.

description.name: Delerium Harvesting
description.value: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

description.name: Uses for Delerium
description.value: Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:

description.name: Spell Component
description.value: Delerium may be used as an Arcane Focus or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

description.name: Magic Items
description.value: Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

description.name: Stable Delerium
description.value: The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk Contamination when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

description.name: Delerium Dust
description.value: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an __Antimagic Field__. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. Improvised Weapons & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a Sling or fashioned into a makeshift Club. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Contamination. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.
This immaculate silver hammer is polished to a mirror finish. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the hammer, you can expend 1 charge to cast the __Mending__ cantrip from it, touching the hammer to the object. Casting Mending in this way affects an area up to 5 feet on a side, instead of 1 foot. Alternatively, you can expend 3 charges as a Bonus Action and touch a creature's armor with the hammer to magically enchant it. The enchantment lasts for 1 minute and grants the armor's wearer a +1 bonus to Armor Class. A creature can only be affected by one of these enchantments at a time.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
These musical instruments are not just the work of the finest luthiers and artisans in Etharis, they have secret embellishments and innovations that can add to a musical performance.
If you are proficient in the instrument and have a Proficiency Bonus of at least +4, all Charisma (*Performance*) checks made using a Mastercraft Instrument have Advantage.

This red gemstone seems to glint with some sort of liquid inside. The gem is immune to all damage. It contains magic absorbed from countless other sources that it uses to overpower the attunement requirements of certain magic items. While holding this gem against an item with an attunement requirement you don't meet, you can ignore that requirement and attune to the item anyway; the item can't be a Legendary item or Artifact. The gem fuses to the surface of the item and encases the area around it in a crystalline shell.

You can end your attunement to the item as normal, even if the item is cursed. Ending your attunement to a cursed item in this way breaks the curse's effects on you. When you end your attunement to an item the gem is fused to, it detaches from the item, allowing you to use it on another one and leaving behind the crystalline shell. When it detaches in this way, it removes the item's magic with it, causing the item to become nonmagical.
This ostentatious medallion draws the eye of even casual onlookers. Whenever you gain Temporary Hit Points, you gain an additional 1d6 Temporary Hit Points.
(Requires the __Mark of Detection__)

This wand has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge, and if a secret door or trap is within 60 feet of you, the wand pulses and points at the one nearest to you.
(Requires the __Mark of Detection__)

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. While wearing them, your vision improves significantly out to a range of 1 foot, granting you Darkvision within that range and Advantage on Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks made to examine something within that range.

This sealed letter, infused with Chronomancy magic, contains a written description of how the creature that reads it shall die. The letter always contains specific descriptions, such as "The red-eyed orc drove its blade through Faizon the Blue's heart," but may also use cryptic or vague language. It never specifies an exact time. Once a creature has read the letter, it has Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and dies only after gaining five Death Saving Throw failures, instead of three. However, when the creature arrives at the moment of its death described in the letter, it dies without making Death Saving Throws if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points.
Once a Memento Mori is opened and read, it becomes an ordinary letter. Its effects end only if the creature that read it dies and is later restored to life.

This small fruit is highly sought after by cooks and sweet-lovers everywhere, both for its flavor as well as its unique sensory-enhancing properties. Eating a Merry Berry raw yields a taste and texture like that of a rich shortbread—the perfect way to end a day of adventure or travel.

Cooking the berry, whether it be in a cuisine or simply roasted over a campfire, brings out more magical effects. When properly cooked, a creature that eats the fruit has Advantage on Intelligence and Wisdom checks that rely on smell or taste for the next 24 hours, as well as on ability checks made using Cook's Utensils for the duration.
Overcooking the fruit not only cooks out the berry's benefits but also results in a soggy and overall bland dish.

This neatly painted drum is attached to a leather shoulder harness, so it can be struck at waist height. Local folklore suggests that this instrument can have an almost hypnotic effect on those in earshot, but only if played at the correct tempo.

You can play this drum as an Action. Once a day, up to three Humanoids within a 30 ft Emanation of the drum beat must succeed on a DC 14 saving throw or have the Charmed condition and become Friendly towards you. The targets make their saving throws with advantage if you or your allies are fighting them. The Charmed condition ends after 1 hour or when you stop playing the drum. When the Charmed condition ends, the targets know they were Charmed by you.

description.name: Tool (Musical Instrument)
description.value: If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

name: Midwife Shears

description.value: These scissors are shaped to resemble a stork. Their blades are forever wickedly sharp, and the threads they cut are more than merely physical.

description.name: Cut the Unseen Thread
description.value: While holding the scissors, you can cast __Dispel Magic__ (+4 bonus) or __Remove Curse__ from them. Once either spell is cast from the scissors, that spell can't be cast from them again until the next dusk.

description.name: Curse of the Severed Thread
description.value: When you make a saving throw to avoid being pushed or to avoid the Prone condition, you have a -1 penalty to the roll. This penalty increases by 1 each time you use the Cut the Unseen Thread property. If you fail such a save by 5 or more, you are pushed 1d6 x 5 feet straight away from the source of the save, in addition to any other distance pushed.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

name: Military Fork

description.name: Hafted
description.value: A Hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. After you use the Attack action to attack with a Hafted weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to make a melee attack with the haft. The haft deals **1d6** Bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Disarming
description.value: A Disarming weapon can catch a foe's weapon, allowing you to remove it from their grasp. When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with a Disarming weapon, you can use your Bonus Action later on the same turn to disarm the target. Both you and the attacker must make opposed attack rolls, ignoring any sources of Advantage and Disadvantage. If your result is higher and the weapon is something the target can drop, the weapon falls from the target's grasp, landing in its space.

If your winning result on the opposed attack roll was a Critical Hit, you can choose for the weapon either to land in a space of your choice up to 15 feet from the target, or to land in your hand if you have a free hand.

properties: a hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. after you use the attack action to attack with a hafted weapon, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the haft. the haft deals **1d6** bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.value: This roughly hewn crystal sword bends light in unexpected and dangerous ways. As a Magic action, you can use a command word to cause it to emit up to two ghostly projections of itself. The sword can have up to two of these projections at a time, which last until you dismiss them (no action required). When swung, the ghostly projections make the sword difficult to see. When you miss a target with an attack roll using the sword while it has at least one projection, you can dismiss one of its projections to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll.

When you hit a target with this weapon while it has at least one projection, the ghostly projections become razor sharp. Targets hit by the sword take an extra **1d4** Slashing damage for each projection it has.

The sword sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius while it has one projection or in a 20-foot radius while it has two. Sheathing the Scimitar contains the projections and their light without dismissing them.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This crystalline Spear bends the light it generates in such a way that it becomes tangible. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Light property.

While you hold the Spear in one hand and have another hand free, you can use a command word as a Magic action to create a ghostly projection of the Spear in your free hand. The projection uses the same weapon statistics as the Spear. When you create a projection in this way, you can make one attack roll with either the Spear or the projection as part of that action. If you make a ranged attack roll with the projection, it disappears after it hits or misses the target. If you're still holding the crystalline Spear when this happens, it magically recreates the projection in your free hand again (no action required).

The projection lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it as a Bonus Action, or until a creature other than you holds it. If you drop or stow the crystalline Spear, its projection disappears until you hold the Spear again. The Spear can only have one projection at a time. While it has a projection, both the Spear and its projection shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This magic sword helps you more effectively add insult to injury. You are proficient with the Mockingblade while you're attuned to it. The sword has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with this weapon on your turn, you can immediately take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to cast the __Vicious Mockery__ cantrip from it, using your spell save DC, against that creature. When you do, any words you use to insult the creature appear written along the blade for 1 minute or until replaced by a new insult.

When a creature rolls a 20 on its saving throw against a __Vicious Mockery__ spell cast in this way, the face adorning the sword's hilt screams insults at you instead until the end of your turn. The insults are audible out to 30 feet and are directed at your deepest insecurities and regrets. Any creature that hears these insults is made aware of your weaknesses, granting it Advantage on its next attack roll against you until the start of your next turn. Once the sword screams at you in this way, it can't be used to cast the __Vicious Mockery__ spell again until 1d4 days have passed.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This single lens has three filters that you can peer through. You can change the monocle's filter by rotating its outer ring. A small arrow along the edge of the frame indicates the monocle's selected filter. The monocle has 4 charges and regains 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the monocle, you can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to activate one of the following filters and gain the corresponding benefits. These effects last for up to 1 hour, ending early if you take off the monocle or you change its filter.

description.name: Filter of Comprehend Languages
description.value: When you peer through this filter, you can understand any written language you see, as if by the written language portion of the __Comprehend Languages__ spell.

description.name: Filter of Darkvision
description.value: While looking through this filter, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

description.name: Filter of See Invisibility
description.value: When gazing through this filter, you can see creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition as if they were visible.
This mithral Whip was once used by a powerful monster hunter. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d4** Slashing damage on a hit.

The Whip has seven runes on its handle that correspond to different damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using the weapon, you can channel one or more of the runes to deal an extra **2d4** damage of the corresponding type or types. For example, you can channel two runes to add 2d4 Acid and **2d4** Fire damage to an attack against a troll, or one rune to add **2d4** Thunder damage to an attack against a clay golem. Once you channel a rune in this way, that rune can't be channeled again until the next dawn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This opaque, grey eyepiece completely blocks normal vision for the eye wearing it. The only things you can see through it are grief eaters, and creatures experiencing significant pain, sorrow, or guilt. These creatures appear as white outlines, shining with an intensity that matches their emotional turmoil. The range of this unusual vision is 60 feet.
While wearing the monocle, you also have Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to gauge a creature's emotions.
This ring is composed of hundreds of rose gold wires woven to coil around the finger. It allows its wearer's spirit to resist the pull of the afterlife.

If you die while wearing this ring, your soul enters the ring and your body remains alive and Stable at 0 Hit Points. When you regain Hit Points, your soul reenters your body and the ring turns into a useless lump of lead.
These brass knuckles are plated with cheap faux gold that wouldn't fool even the most casual observer.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you score a Critical Hit against an enemy with this magic weapon, you gain GP equal to the creature's Challenge Rating (or level if it does not have a Challenge Rating). Creatures with a Challenge Rating less than 1 count as 0.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

Created through a gruesome process requiring the muscle tissue of a bugbear vampire, this graft melds to the flesh of a living creature who attunes to it. Your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. When you become attuned, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or your Constitution decreases by 2, to a minimum of 1.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This graft is cursed. Attuning to it curses you for 1 year or until you are targeted by __Remove Curse__ or a similar spell. Removing the graft fails to end the curse on you, and you cannot end the Attunement while the curse lasts. You develop a deep desire for rare meat and raw blood. At the end of each week, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or become a __Vampire Spawn__ with no progenitor.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This necklace allows you to absorb the life energy of creatures you slay. When you reduce a Small or larger enemy to 0 Hit Points, the necklace emits a faint glow and gains 1 charge. The necklace can have up to 3 charges and has 1d3 charges when found. You can expend 1 or more charges as a Bonus Action to magically turn death into life. You take **1d8** Necrotic damage for each expended charge, and another creature you can see within 30 feet of you regains Hit Points equal to twice the amount of Necrotic damage you took. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

If this damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, you have the Unconscious condition but are Stable. When this happens, the target regains Hit Points equal to twice the amount of Hit Points you had remaining before you took this damage.
The most infamous of mythos tomes, the Necronomicon contains within its pages untold secrets of the mythos.

description.name: Language:
description.value: Infernal (XPHB).

description.name: Attunement Check:
description.value: Intelligence (*Arcana*) DC 20. To end your Attunement to the Necronomicon, you must defeat a mythos deity in combat.

description.name: Benefits:
description.value: While attuned to the Necronomicon, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You double your Proficiency Bonus if it applies to an Intelligence check.
You can read and write Abyssal (XPHB), Celestial (XPHB), Draconic (XPHB), and Primordial (XPHB).
If you can cast spells, you always have __Evil Eye__, __Dread Curse of Azathoth__, __Dust of Suleiman__, and __Voorish Sign__ prepared.
__Ghouls__ and __Ghasts__ refuse to attack you unless you are first Hostile toward them.
__Skeletons__ and __Zombies__ obey your verbal commands.
A mythos deity attacks or otherwise attempts to harm you only if there are no other targets available for its attacks. You have Advantage on all Charisma checks to sway their attitude.
If you have the spellcasting class feature, you gain one additional spell slot for each level you can use. You regain these added spell slots as normal based on your spellcasting class feature.
The save DC of your spells gains a +2 bonus.

description.name: Drawbacks:
description.value: At midnight each day roll a d20. On a 10 or higher, you gain a Doom of the Necronomicon point. When you have 20 or more such points, you disappear into thin air, claimed by the inscrutable power that infuses this tome. The Necronomicon is the only possession you leave behind.

description.name: Insight-Compulsion to Annihilation (+20):
description.value: You are driven to meet and understand the deities of the Cthulhu Mythos. Such entities are fascinating. They are the true masters of reality, those who were and shall forever be. By understanding them, by coming in direct contact with them, you can unlock their secrets and match their power. All others failed because they were weak. I will be different. I will survive. You will see.

description.name: Lore:
description.value: The Necronomicon allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about the undead and all DC 20 or lower checks made to uncover information about the mythos in general.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the Commune with *Nature* spell, but your experience is filled with terror and dread. You must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, for the next 8 hours, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks while you can see a forest. You automatically succeed on the save if you have Immunity to the Frightened condition.
This bottle is carved from wood, with a green, leafy face adorning its surface. The liquid is a deep green streaked with shades of umber.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: You can learn all five facts from Commune with *Nature*.

Sewn from the plant creature known as maiden's hair, this sweet-smelling piece of headgear bestows lingering magical properties. While wearing the net on your head, you have Advantage on Charisma (*Persuasion*) checks. Additionally, you can take a Bonus Action to make an ability check to end the Grappled condition, and you have Advantage on ability checks to end the Grappled condition.
This twisted staff is created from the remains of a marra. It has 3 charges and regains its expended charges daily at dusk.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you damages you while you hold this staff, you can take a Reaction to expend **1** of the staff's charges to force the creature to make a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the creature sees a phantasm that causes it to have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. If the creature is already Frightened, it also takes **2d6** Psychic damage.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This studded Greatclub once belonged to a hungering oni who excelled at subterfuge. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Heavy property. When you hit a creature that has the Unconscious condition with this weapon, the target takes an extra **2d8** Psychic damage. In addition, when you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon, the target must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or magically have the Unconscious condition until the end of your next turn.

The condition ends on the target if it takes damage or someone takes an action to shake it out of the effect. Creatures that don't sleep, such as elves, or that have Immunity to the Exhaustion condition automatically succeed on saves against this effect.

The weapon has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the weapon, you can expend 1 charge as a Bonus Action to cast either Invisibility (targeting only yourself) or Sleep from it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
When you drink this potion, you have Darkvision out to 120 feet for the next 24 hours. During that time, you don't need to sleep, and if you take a Long Rest, you can remain conscious throughout.
This clay bottle with a waxed stopper is painted with the head of a great horned owl, and the liquid within is midnight blue

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: The duration increases to 72 hours.

This small mechanical device is a specialty of gnomish crafters. As a Utilize action, you can throw the Noisemaker into a space within 60 feet. When it lands, it makes a loud noise of some kind, depending on the whims of the creator: a musical clash, a whistling, a whirring, a buzzing, etc. This noise can be heard up to half a mile away.

A creature with an Intelligence score of 3 or less that is within 60 feet of the device when it goes off must succeed in a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has the Frightened condition for one minute. As an Influence action, another creature who the Frightened creature can see or hear can attempt a DC 20 Wisdom (*Animal Handling*) or Charisma (*Persuasion*) check. On a success, the Frightened condition ends on that creature.
This drab pouch contains 1d4 + 1 sticks of dull gray chalk. The chalk feels slightly tingly to the touch.

As a Magic action, you can touch one of the sticks of chalk to the ground, wall, or ceiling to magically create a line that is up to 50 feet long and 1 foot thick. The line extends from your location in the direction and shape of your choice. You can shape the line in any way you choose as long as it makes one continuous path along the surface or similar adjacent surfaces. Once a stick of chalk has been used in this way, it disintegrates into a pile of fine, nonmagical powder.

Magical effects can't cross this line. The line's effect extends 20 feet perpendicularly from the surface on which it is drawn. Targets have Total Cover against spells and other magical effects originating from the other side of the line. Magic items that cross the line become mundane and nonmagical for 1 round unless they're Artifacts.

The first time a Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead attempts to cross the line on a turn, that creature must make a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn, it's forced backward up to 10 feet away from the line, and it takes **2d8** Force damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only, and it passes through the line. If the line cuts through an affected creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the line (you choose which side).

This effect lasts for 8 hours or until a break of at least one foot is made in the line, which causes it to instantly lose all magical properties. A creature can spend 1 minute to smudge, smear, erase, or otherwise remove the line enough to disable its effects. When targeted by the __Dispel Magic__ spell, the line is treated as if it were a level 6 spell. If the line is dispelled in this way, its effects are disabled for 1 minute.

This raven-feathered mantle is almost iridescent. While wearing the mantle, you have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your rate of descent when falling slows to 60 feet per round, taking no damage from the fall when you land.

In addition, while wearing the mantle, you can cast the __Find Familiar__ spell from it as a Magic action instead of its normal casting time. When you do, the familiar takes the form of a Raven. If the familiar drops to 0 Hit Points, it can't be summoned again until the next dusk. Otherwise, the familiar remains as long as you are attuned to the mantle.

This red feather quill generates its own mundane ink and acts on its own as you speak to it. While holding the quill, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to activate it. While activated, the quill magically floats upright and writes the words you speak to it on whatever stationary, nonliving surface it's been placed on. When it reaches the edge of that surface, it begins a new line below before continuing. If the quill reaches the end of the surface, such as a piece of parchment, it taps against the surface expectantly until a new one is provided. You must be within 15 feet of the quill in order to speak to it. If the quill is behind Total Cover, it can't understand you. If you repeat the command word, even if you're not holding the quill, it deactivates and falls down. If the quill doesn't write anything for 1 minute, it deactivates on its own.

name: Ori Boots
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Passage__)

description.value: While you wear these boots, you can take a Bonus Action to click the boots' heels together. If you do, the boots double your Speed, and any creature that makes an Opportunity Attack against you has Disadvantage on the attack roll. If you click your heels together again, you end the effect.
When you've used the boots' property for a total of 10 minutes, the magic ceases to function for you until you finish a Long Rest.

This gruesome, magical otyugh pelt still holds some of its natural abilities. A single tendril bearing three eyes hangs from the back of the cloak's hood. While wearing the cloak, you can take a Magic action to telepathically communicate with a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can understand a language, sending either simple messages or images when you do. The receiving creature can't respond to these messages.

The tendril hanging from the hood is 3 feet long and offers some limited articulation. While wearing the cloak, you can take a Magic action to mentally control the tendril enough to perform a simple task within 5 feet of you, such as to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. The tendril can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

In addition, while wearing the hood, you can take a Bonus Action to close your eyes and magically see through the eyes of the tendril. When you do, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. You can control the tendril while looking through its eyes in this way. You return to your normal senses when you reopen your eyes or lower the hood.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you roll an 8 on the damage die for an attack made with this weapon, the target takes an extra **1d8** Poison damage. In addition, when you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon against a creature, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes **3d6** Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

While holding this large Shield, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. The bonus becomes +2 while you have at least 1 Temporary Hit Point. While you have Temporary Hit Points, the Shield emits a slight blue glow.
In addition, you can channel the heroic resolve within the Shield as a Magic action to gain 1d6 + 8 Temporary Hit Points. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This delicious gum comes in packs of five and can be blown into large, levitating bubbles 1 foot in diameter. You need to chew a piece of the gum for 1 minute before its magic can be used. Once it's been chewed for at least 1 minute, you can take a Magic action while the gum is in your mouth to blow a single bubble with it. When you do, you gain the effect of the __Levitate__ spell, as if you had cast it, provided the bubble stays attached to the gum in your mouth. While the effect doesn't require your *Concentration*, it does end early and cause you to fall if you take an action to pop it or if the bubble takes any damage; the bubble is a loose object for the purpose of any attack or effect that would target it. The effect ends on its own after 10 minutes, allowing you and the bubble to float gently down to the ground if you're still aloft. The gum becomes nonmagical, albeit still delicious, once this bubble's effect ends.

When you take the Magic action to blow this bubble, you can remove it from your mouth as part of the same action and stick it on another creature or loose object within 5 feet of you. When you do, the stuck target gains the effect of the __Levitate__ spell, instead of you, but you have no control over it; the effect otherwise functions as described above. An unwilling creature that succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw avoids having the bubble stuck to it.

This pair of golden rings play a sad, sad melody when you rub the two fingers wearing them together. Creatures that know the __Vicious Mockery__ cantrip can use this set of rings as a Somatic component for the spell instead of the normal Verbal component required by it.
This ammunition works like an Armor-Piercing Melee weapon, but you fire the ammunition as a projectile from a Ranged weapon.

When you hit with Blessed ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Radiant. Also, if the target is Fiend, Fey, or Undead, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Designed to open wide wounds, such as with a broad-bladed arrowhead, Brutal ammunition works like a __Brutal__ Melee weapon.

When you hit with Desecrated ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Necrotic. Also, if the target is Celestial, Humanoid, or Plant, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional **1d4** Fire damage.

This ancient set of armor, which includes boots, greaves, a cuirass, gauntlets, and a helm, fully encases you in a shell of imposing steel, such that no part of your body is visible. While wearing this armor, you have Immunity to the Unconscious condition. If you have 0 Hit Points, you must still make Death Saving Throws, but you can continue to move and act.
If you die while wearing this armor, you can continue to move and act within it for up to 1 minute, though you lose the ability to speak and to cast or concentrate on spells.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This armor is cursed, a fact revealed only when __Identify__ is cast on the armor or you attune to it. While attuned to the armor, it is impossible to remove. Additionally, you automatically fail all Death Saving Throws as the armor's magic puts an immense strain on your body.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

name: Parlor Gun

description.value: The smallest usable firearm, a Parlor Gun can be tucked into a stocking or hidden down a sleeve for two barrels of point-blank fire.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Disarming
description.value: A Disarming weapon can catch a foe's weapon, allowing you to remove it from their grasp. When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with a Disarming weapon, you can use your Bonus Action later on the same turn to disarm the target. Both you and the attacker must make opposed attack rolls, ignoring any sources of Advantage and Disadvantage. If your result is higher and the weapon is something the target can drop, the weapon falls from the target's grasp, landing in its space.

If your winning result on the opposed attack roll was a Critical Hit, you can choose for the weapon either to land in a space of your choice up to 15 feet from the target, or to land in your hand if you have a free hand.

name: Passage Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Passage__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Passage__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Passage Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Passage__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Passage__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Passage Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Passage__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Passage__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

This magic Quiver is made from the shell of an enormous oyster. Arrows you pull from it are magical and are coated with a pearlescent, hydrophobic coating. Ranged attack rolls made with these Arrows ignore the normal drawbacks of underwater combat. The Arrows become nonmagical once they hit a target or are held by a creature other than you.

description.name: Create Pearl
description.value: You can use a command word to cause the Quiver to create a magical pearl. You can hold onto this pearl or give it to another creature. When a creature with the pearl makes a Wisdom check or Wisdom saving throw, it can choose to make the check or save with Advantage. When it does, the pearl turns to dust. The pearl is visibly magical and disintegrates on its own after 24 hours if left unused. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.
This pelt cape is made from the fur of a Garmyr stitched carefully into the leathers of a ratling, decorated with the talons of a harpy, and polished to a shine with contaminated ichor.
While you are attuned to this pelt and are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, your allies have Advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Pelt of the Pack Lord requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Monstrosity Animus
**[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
**[Hair]**: Fur from a Garmyr
**[Hide]**: Skin from a Ratling
**[Natural Weapon]**: Claws from a Harpy

description.value: The jeweled pendant has 3 charges, which are replenished when you finish a Long Rest. When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, you can use a Reaction to expend 1 charge from the pendant to gain resistance to that damage type until the end of your next turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Pendant of Prismatic Protection requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus from an Elemental
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
**[Fluid]**: Any two Elemental Fluids from different Elementals

description.value: This magic silvered pendant glows with a simmering flame of rage trapped inside its clenched fist. Small sparks shoot out from between the pendant's metal fingers. The fiery anger from the pendant tightens your focus and allows you to shrug off some of the damage you take. If you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield while you wear this pendant, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by 3.

In addition, the pendant has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to ignite your hands in a magical flame, causing them to shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike while your hands are wreathed in this fire, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type, and it deals an extra **1d4** Fire damage on a hit. Your hands remain lit for 1 minute or until you take a Bonus Action to quench them.
Any flame created by the pendant, whether it be on your hands or on the pendant itself, is harmless to you.

While wearing this pendant, you know Thieves' Cant. In addition, you can more easily recognize the patterns used in linguistic codes, granting you a +5 bonus to Intelligence checks made to understand a written or spoken cipher.
These brass knuckles are made of gold and etched with a holy symbol over each knuckle. You gain a +1 to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon.
When you hit a Fiend or Undead with this weapon, that creature takes an extra **1d12** Radiant damage.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This hard, minty sugarbomb slowly dissolves in your mouth over the course of 1 hour. At any point, you can take a Bonus Action to crunch down and break the sugarbomb into tiny, painful shards. You take **1d6** Piercing damage from the shards but are temporarily enchanted by the candy. Whenever you hit a target with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike that deals Piercing or Slashing damage while you're enchanted in this way, the target takes an extra 2 damage. This enchantment fades after 1 minute.

description.name: Upset Stomach
description.value: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

This perfectly reflective charm magically helps you meditate and focus your mind. Whenever you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw while wearing the necklace, you can take a Reaction to reroll the save, and you must use the new roll.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This periapt is cursed, a fact that is only revealed when the curse extends to you due to rolling a 1 on a saving throw after using the periapt to reroll it. Until the curse ends, the mirrored surface of the necklace dulls into an ugly, flat gray while you wear it. The curse persists even if you aren't wearing the necklace, and you remain cursed until you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

While you're cursed, your reflection in any mirrored surface within 10 feet of you turns into an ugly, horrifying visage of your deepest insecurities. In addition, when you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (including the roll that reveals this curse), you take **1d8** Psychic damage.

This violet piece of parchment is smooth and pleasant to write on. You can take a Bonus Action and use either of the command words, "lock" or "unlock," to magically lock or unlock the parchment, respectively. While locked, the sheet can't be torn by hand, damaged by fire, or damaged by immersion in water, and any ink already on the page can't be removed, smeared, or otherwise changed without the use of magic. New ink added to a locked sheet of Permanent Parchment runs off the page like water. While unlocked, the parchment behaves like a nonmagical sheet of paper.
If the sheet is unlocked, you can use another command word, "clear," to cause any ink on the sheet of parchment to magically evaporate without leaving any marks behind.

This cape is made of colorful and aromatic petals. While wearing the cape, petals drift behind you as you walk and disappear before touching the ground. You can take a Bonus Action to magically change the color of these petals. While wearing the cape, you can cast the __Druidcraft__ cantrip from it, and Beasts and Plant creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

This hand-sized fleshy sapling has writhing tentacles for branches and bulbous yellow eyes studding its trunk. You can take an action to plant it in the ground in your space, at which point it begins whispering telepathically to you. While the sprout is planted and within 30 feet of you, you have truesight with a range of 30 feet.

Anyone in the sprout's space can take an action to uproot it. If left in the ground for 1 minute, the sprout experiences a growth surge, uproots itself, and becomes a __Roper__ that is Hostile to you and your allies.

This crystalline Battleaxe seems to be almost transparent when looking at the bladed head from different angles. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. The first time on your turn when you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the axe, you can force another creature within 10 feet of the target to make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, that creature takes **1d8** Force damage.

If you can see the axe and are within 60 feet of it, you can take a Bonus Action to magically return the axe to your outstretched hand. When you do, the weapon phases through any obstacle in its path that isn't more than 5 feet thick or made of lead.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
This thick glass bottle holds viscous, white, fizzing liquid. Tied around the bottle's neck is a worn tag that once listed the ingredients and stated dose.

For 1 hour after drinking this potion, when you take bludgeoning damage, reduce the total damage taken by 1d4. Your Strength and Constitution scores both increase by 2 until the potion's effects wear off.

This strong, flexible armor made from the hide of ogre swine is surprisingly supple. It is considered light armor rather than medium armor. When a Critical Hit is scored on you, roll 1d20. On a 17-20, you treat it as a hit instead.
However, while wearing the armor, you snore uncontrollably while sleeping, and your food intake doubles.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding this Pike, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: __Mirror Image__ (1 charge), __Phantom Steed__ (1 charge), __Speak with Dead__ (1 charge), or __Spirit Guardians__ (2 charges).

description.name: Spectral Warrior
description.value: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this Pike, you can choose to summon a spectral warrior from it. Until the start of your next turn, the target is haunted by this warrior, causing it to have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. This property has no effect against Undead creatures.

description.name: Haunting Phalanx
description.value: You can take a Magic action while holding this Pike to expend 3 charges and point it forward commandingly. Five spectral, Pike-wielding warriors appear before you and march in a 25-foot-wide, 50-foot-long Line in a direction you choose. Any creature within the area must make a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw; Undead creatures automatically succeed on the save. On a failed save, a target takes **3d10** Necrotic damage and **3d10** Psychic damage and is affected by the weapon's Spectral Warrior property. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
The earliest type of one-handed firearm, a Pistol operates as a miniature Musket, loading and firing a single heavy projectile with deadly results.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This birdlike mask's blend of magic and science is as unique as it is helpful. While wearing it, you can easily lift it above your face to eat or speak more clearly. The mask's beak is lined with magical flowers that react to and purify airborne toxins before they pass through it. While wearing the mask, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition as well as the effects of magical contagions if they came from an airborne source, and you have Resistance to any Poison damage that those effects might deal.

In addition, the flowers have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn as new flowers bloom. As a Magic action, you can hold the beak's nostrils closed with a free hand and expend 1 charge to exhale a 15-foot Cone of thick pollen in front of you. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes **2d8** Poison damage, and its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn unless it has Immunity to the Poisoned condition. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

This thin blade seems to toe the line between planes of existence, occasionally allowing it to bend the planes to extend beyond its normal reach. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Rapier has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. When you make a melee attack roll with the Rapier, you can expend 1 charge to extend the weapon, increasing its reach for the attack by 5 feet.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge immediately after making a melee attack roll with the Rapier against a target within 5 feet of you, causing the weapon to extend and pierce through the original target. Make an additional melee attack roll with the Rapier against a second target 5 feet behind the original one; the second target must be within 10 feet of you. This additional attack is made as part of the initial attack, and the second target doesn't benefit from using the original one as cover.
Whenever you expend a charge from this weapon, the planes around the extended blade begin to tear, causing the target to take an extra **2d8** Force damage on a hit.
After the attack with the extended blade, it returns to its normal size.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

name: Planchette of Adela Druskenvald (Legendary)

description.value: A small, heart-shaped silver pointer hangs from a silver necklace. It is inscribed with occult symbols. When placed on an open book or other assortment of letters, the air nearby feels heavy and cold.

While wearing the planchette, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence and Wisdom ability checks determined by the planchette's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Sense the Unseen (Rare+)
description.value: The planchette has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. You can expend charges to cast the following spells from it: __Detect Magic__ (1 charge), __Locate Object__ (2 charges), __See Invisibility__ (2 charges).

description.name: Starlight Ward (Rare+)
description.value: You have Resistance to Radiant damage. When you take Radiant damage, for the next minute, the star-sigils on the planchette shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

description.name: Vision Beyond (Very Rare+)
description.value: The planchette now has 9 charges and regains 1d8 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. You can also cast __Find Traps__ (2 charges) and __Sending__ (3 charges) from it.

description.name: Spirit Ward (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you fail a saving throw against the __Magic Jar__ spell or possession (such as by a __ghost__), you can expend 3 charges to succeed instead.

description.name: Third Eye Opened (Legendary)
description.value: The planchette now has 13 charges and regains 1d12 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. You can also cast __Divination__ (4 charges), __Contact Other Plane__ (5 charges), and __Etherealness__ (7 charges) from it.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.
