properties: each fabled heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. the rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [heirloom rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. an heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. the heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: The Pnakotic Manuscripts originate from a long-lost species that once walked the world, long before the rise of humans, elves, and other intelligences. These creatures communed with the Cthulhu Mythos and were perhaps their servitors. This strange tome was written before time began its proper flow and grants insights into its workings. By reading it, you learn to move between time's beats.

description.name: Language:
description.value: Primordial (XPHB).

description.name: Attunement Check:
description.value: Intelligence (*Religion*) DC 15. To end your Attunement to the Pnakotic Manuscripts, you must be the target of a __Remove Curse__ spell.

description.name: Benefits:
description.value: While attuned to the Pnakotic Manuscripts, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You double your bonus to Initiative.
You gain a +10 bonus to Speed.
You have Advantage on all Dexterity saving throws.
You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Once per turn while moving, you can teleport back to any spot you occupied during your current move.

description.name: Drawbacks:
description.value: You age at an accelerated rate. After one week, you age an additional week. After two weeks, you age an additional four weeks. After three weeks, you age an additional six weeks, and so on. If you remove your Attunement to this item and later attune to it again, you preserve this drawback's progress.

description.name: Insight-No Time to Tarry (+15):
description.value: You hate any activity that takes more than a few moments. You grow impatient as your attention fades and you seek something new to do, leaving critical work unattended as you start a new project or seek out something new to do.

description.name: Lore:
description.value: The Pnakotic Manuscript allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about time and its nature.

name: Polearm

description.name: Hafted
description.value: A Hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. After you use the Attack action to attack with a Hafted weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to make a melee attack with the haft. The haft deals **1d6** Bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Set
description.value: Weapons with the Set property allow you to prepare for an oncoming attack. If a target enters your reach while you wield a weapon with this property, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack with the weapon against that target.

properties: a hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. after you use the attack action to attack with a hafted weapon, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the haft. the haft deals **1d6** bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.value: This canister of waxy pomade has magical properties, allowing you to change your hair's color, style, thickness, and length (up to 1 foot longer or shorter per use). The canister steadily replenishes its pomade over time. It can hold up to 4 uses at a time and regains 1d4 expended uses daily at dawn. Applying 1 use of the pomade takes 1 minute.

Once you've used this product in your hair, it returns to its normal appearance after you finish a Long Rest. Hair produced by the pomade that's been cut off turns to dust after 24 hours. If you use the pomade every day for 7 days to make the same changes, the changes become permanent.
This bag contains twenty iron balls, each measuring one inch in diameter and weighing 1/4 of a pound. When poured out of their bag as a Utilize action, the balls function as Ball Bearings.

As a Bonus Action, you can speak the command word, which causes a number of the balls that you choose to expand into full-size cannonballs weighing 10 pounds each, suitable for firing from a cannon. A creature in the path of one or more cannonballs rolling downhill must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take **2d10** Bludgeoning damage and have the Prone condition if it is Large or smaller.

Each iron ball can also be used as a Sling Bullet or a Firearm Bullet. As a Bonus Action when you make an attack with an iron ball as ammunition, you can expand it in midair. On a hit, this attack deals Bludgeoning damage equal to 2d12 plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll instead of the weapon's normal damage.

This sickly-looking potion contains a writhing mass of tentacles that animate and uncomfortably crawl down the imbiber's throat when consumed. The taste is pungent and fishy, and results in the sudden outbreak of random, but temporary, mutations.

When you consume this potion, you gain the effects of one randomly determined Mutation until you start a Short or Long Rest. You can roll on the [Mutations](https://5e.tools/tables.html#mutations_monstersofdrakkenheim) table twice, choosing which mutation manifests. You don't gain any Contamination levels as a result of this Mutation. When the effect ends, your body returns to normal.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Potion of Controlled Mutation requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from an Aberration
**[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
**[Organs]**: Any two Organs from an Aberration

description.value: Drinking this potion grants you a brief surge of draconic power. Once within the next minute, you can replace one of your attacks when you take the Attack action with an exhalation of magical energy, which has the same effects as the Dragonborn's Breath Weapon trait. The damage type for the exhalation is randomly determined from the Draconic Ancestors table in the Dragonborn species description when this potion is created. The amount of damage the exhalation deals and its save DC are determined by the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below.

When crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath, you can use the harvested stomach and gizzard of a fallen dragon in place of the raw materials normally needed to craft a magic item. If you do, the exhalation's damage type is determined by the kind of dragon the materials were sourced from, and the potion's rarity is determined by the dragon's age category: Uncommon (young dragon), Rare (adult dragon), or Very Rare (ancient dragon). Once you start crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath in this way, if you don't spend at least 2 hours working to craft it on a given day before finishing it, roll 1d20. On a 1, the harvested materials are destroyed, and the potion spoils.

This brew is made from the ground horns of keppmirs. When consumed, this potion allows you to breathe underwater for 1 hour, during which time you have Resistance to Cold damage. It tastes salty and gives off a slight warmth.
This concoction is the result of a failed attempt to make a Potion of Heal. It is indistinguishable from that potion without using divination magic of level 3 or higher.

When you imbibe this potion, roll 1d4. That becomes your new Hit Point total. If the Potion of Harm is given to a creature with 0 Hit Points, they instantly suffer a Death Saving Throw failure and begin dying if they are Stable.
This ebon liquid is made from the remains of a downcast vampire. When you imbibe this potion, you regain all your Hit Points.

This shimmering liquid changes colors constantly within its vial. Made from the acid glands of the dreaded wolfentroika, this potion allows you to share your life force with others. After drinking this potion, you can take a Bonus Action to choose a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see or hear. That creature regains 4d6 Hit Points, and you take an equal amount of Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. The effect ends after 1 minute, at which point you gain 1 level of Exhaustion.

This brew is made from the spore sacs of three grippers. When consumed, this potion causes the imbiber to give off spores that anger enemies within 10 feet. Those enemies must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw, or they must target the imbiber with their attacks for 1 minute. All weapon attacks are made with Disadvantage.

This viscous potion is made from quoxxarie blood. After drinking this potion, when you are reduced to 0 Hit Points you can expend a Hit Point Dice (no action required) and set your Hit Points to 1. This effect lasts for 1 minute, at the end of which you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of Exhaustion for each Hit Die spent during the potion's duration.
When you drink this potion, you recover expended spell slots of your choice of levels 1-5. The spell slots must have a combined level that is less than or equal to 1d3 + 3.
For 1 minute after you drink this potion, you gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Unarmed Strikes.
This potion is thick and dark brown topped with a cream colored froth.

This magic coral staff was first found within the Great Reef of the Elemental Plane of Water. Its origins beyond that are entirely unknown, with some suggesting it was made by the plane itself rather than forged or crafted by a mere creature's hands. Attuning to the staff bestows some of its planar powers to you, allowing you to breathe underwater and ignore any of the drawbacks caused by a deep, underwater environment. In addition, while holding the staff, you have Resistance to Cold damage.
This staff has 15 charges, which are used to power its various properties. The staff regains 1d8 + 7 expended charges daily at dawn.

description.name: State Change
description.value: The staff has a powerful control over the various states of water. As a Bonus Action while holding the staff, you can mentally command the staff's ever-present bounty of water to magically change its state into a gas, liquid, or solid. The properties of each state are detailed below. Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge as a Reaction when you are targeted by an attack or spell to force the staff to change its state more rapidly.

When you do, the staff's change is immediate, potentially affecting the outcome of the incoming attack or spell. You take this Reaction when you know you are the target of the attack or spell, but before knowing the result of the roll.

description.name: Gas
description.value: When the staff enters its gaseous state, the water surrounding it becomes a fine mist. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You have Resistance to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage.
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.
You can move through the space of any creature, regardless of its size, and another creature's space isn't difficult terrain for you.
Opportunity Attacks against you are made with Disadvantage.

description.name: Gas Spells
description.value: While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: __Cloudkill__ (5 charges), __Fog Cloud__ (1 charge), __Gaseous Form__ (3 charges), __Misty Step__ (2 charges), or __Wind Walk__ (6 charges).

description.name: Tailwind
description.value: While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 2 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to grant additional benefits to you and nearby allies. Until the end of your next turn, you and your allies within 30 feet of you can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action and don't provoke Opportunity Attacks by moving.

description.name: Liquid
description.value: When the staff enters its liquid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a swirling torrent. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You have Resistance to Bludgeoning and Slashing damage.
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
You have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
You can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground.

When an enemy that you can see misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a Reaction to force that creature to repeat the same attack against a different creature of your choice (other than itself).

description.name: Liquid Spells
description.value: While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: __Blur__ (2 charges), __Control Water__ (4 charges), __Create or Destroy Water__ (1 charge), __Mirror Image__ (2 charges), or __Water Breathing__ (3 charges).

description.name: Tide Turner
description.value: While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 3 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to send out a wave of ethereal water to buffet and push your enemies. Each enemy of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes **4d8** Bludgeoning damage and is pushed either 20 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

description.name: Solid
description.value: When the staff enters its solid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a frozen shell. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You have Resistance to Piercing and Slashing damage.
Your Speed is reduced to 5 feet.
You have a +3 bonus to Armor Class.
If you're pushed against your will, the distance you are pushed is halved.
You gain 10 Temporary Hit Points at the start of each of your turns, which vanish if the staff changes state.

description.name: Solid Spells
description.value: While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend some charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18; +10 attack bonus) from it: __Cone of Cold__ (5 charges), __Ice Storm__ (4 charges), __Ray of Frost__ (0 charges, or 1 charge to cast at level 5), or __Wall of Ice__ (6 charges).

description.name: Deep Freeze
description.value: While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend 4 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to send out a chilling blast to freeze your foes. Enemies of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes **4d8** Cold damage, and its Speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much Cold damage, and its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn instead.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: Precipit, the Formless has the following random properties:

entries: 2 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) properties
2 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) properties

description.name: Destroying the Staff
description.value: The only way to destroy the staff is to keep it untouched by water for 100 years while on the Elemental Plane of Water, at which point it crumbles to dust. Any amount or precipitation (such as a puff of misty air, a drip of water, or the touch of ice) during that time reinvigorates the staff's bounty of water.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This dark crystal Javelin has a prismatic head that can refract light into beautiful displays of color. Immediately after you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the Javelin, it disappears in a small burst of light before reappearing in your open hand.

As a Magic action, you can throw the Javelin at a point you can see within 120 feet of you and use a command word. The Javelin erupts at that point in a dazzling display of color and light, casting painful Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. Each creature of your choice within the Bright Light that isn't behind Total Cover must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. For each target, roll 1d6 to determine which beam of light affects it, consulting the table below. On a failed save, a target takes **2d10** damage of the type corresponding to the beam's color for each beam of light it is struck by. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

rows: The creature is struck by two beams of light. Roll twice, rerolling any 6.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This charm is a charred feather harvested from a fallen angel, wrapped in silver wire. While you wear this charm, your creature type appears to be Humanoid for the purpose of __Detect Evil and Good__ and similar effects.

This cloth mask converts the words that pass through it into vile obscenities. While wearing the mask over your mouth, your words are heard as angry insults and swears instead of the ones you intend. You don't hear these words. If a creature takes a Study action to examine the words, the creature can determine that they aren't your own with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check. Verbal spell components, command words, and actual obscenities you say are unaffected by the mask's magic and are heard normally by creatures within earshot.

name: Prospector's Wand
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Finding__)

description.value: This Y-shaped wand, bearing the emblem of the __Mark of Finding__, has 5 charges. While holding the wand, you can use any of its properties:

description.name: Finding
description.value: You can expend 2 charges to cast __Locate Creature__ from it.

description.name: Location
description.value: You can expend 1 charge to cast __Locate Object__ from it.

description.name: Prospecting
description.value: You can expend 1 charge to cast __Locate Animals or Plants__ from it, with the following benefits.
You can describe or name a specific kind of mineral and locate it instead of a Beast or Plant.

You can specify the minimum quantity of that Beast, Plant, or mineral that you wish the spell to find within a 30-foot-radius sphere, such as "at least 3 pounds of Eberron dragonshards" or "at least five deer." You learn the direction and distance to the closest occurrence in that *Concentration*, if any are present.

description.name: Regaining Charges
description.value: The wand regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with Grievous Wounds, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through Prosthetics.
When a creature with a Grievous Wound uses a Prosthetic, they ignore the penalties imposed by the Grievous Wound while wearing a Prosthetic that replaces the lost or wounded body part.
Some Prosthetics can be enchanted with magic, giving them even further powers. Rules for Magical Prosthetics can be found in the *Grim Hollow Campaign Guide*.

name: Pump Shotgun

description.value: The Pump Shotgun's namesake is a distinctive sliding grip on the barrel which can be "pumped" to chamber a new round.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Recoil
description.value: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Scatter
description.value: Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls with this weapon.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.
after you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

name: Punching Dagger

description.name: Armor-Piercing
description.value: An Armor-Piercing weapon is a Melee weapon designed to punch through armor or thick hide. When you make an attack roll using an Armor-Piercing weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll if your target is wearing armor or has an Armor Class of 18 or higher.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Defending
description.value: A Defending weapon is either made for parrying, has advanced techniques for use in parrying, or both. When wielding a Defending weapon, you may use your Reaction when you are hit by a melee attack roll. Roll 1d4 and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack.

properties: an armor-piercing weapon is a melee weapon designed to punch through armor or thick hide. when you make an attack roll using an armor-piercing weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack roll if your target is wearing armor or has an armor class of 18 or higher.

description.value: This chiseled wooden Dagger is a relic crafted from the bough of a holy tree and is always miraculously sharp. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d4** Radiant damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to 2d4 when you hit an Undead with the Dagger, causing blue tongues of holy flame to flash along the weapon's edge.

When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon against an Undead, you can choose to plunge the blade into the target's body and leave it there. When you do, the Dagger emits Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet. The light is sunlight. While the blade is lodged in a target in this way, that target takes **3d4** Radiant damage at the start of each of its turns, and the Dagger continues to emit sunlight. To end this effect, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 16 Strength (*Athletics*) check, removing the Dagger on a success. Once removed, the blade vanishes and reappears on the ground at your feet or in your free hand (your choice each time).

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

name: Purity Spear
type: legendary (requires attunement by a Creature of Good Alignment)

description.value: This beautiful Spear has a long handle carved of ivory and is tipped with the spiraling horn of a unicorn. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While attuned to the Spear, you have Immunity to Poison damage and the Poisoned condition. In addition, you have Advantage on Constitution and Wisdom saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

The Spear has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Spear, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: __Calm Emotions__ (2 charges), __Detect Evil and Good__ (1 charge), __Dispel Evil and Good__ (5 charges), __Greater Restoration__ (5 charges), __Misty Step__ (2 charges), or __Purify Food and Drink__ (1 charge). In addition, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge to touch a creature with the Spear. The target regains 2d8 + 2 Hit Points, and the Poisoned condition ends on it if it had that condition.

description.name: Charge
description.value: If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack roll using the Spear, the target takes an extra **2d8** Piercing damage.

description.name: Curse Breaker
description.value: While attuned to the Spear, you are immune to being cursed by spells and other effects. If you are already affected by a curse when you attune to the Spear or are attuned to a cursed item, the effects of the curse are suppressed for you as long as you remain attuned to the Spear.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This ceramic piglet figurine is glazed with a friendly pink coating that's soft to the touch, and it has a hole in the top that can be stoppered with a cork. When you drop a coin in the piglet and stopper it, the figurine animates and imprints on you, considering you its owner. As the piglet's owner, you can magically learn how much money is inside it by holding and gently shaking it, causing it to oink happily.

Once animate, the piglet happily eats any coin handed to it, storing it inside. The piglet will spit out exact change when you or an ally asks for it, even converting the coins within it into larger or smaller denominations. The figurine can only hold coins and will spit or sneeze out anything else you place inside it. The piglet squeals with glee and prances about excitedly when you deposit or feed it coins. The piglet can eat up to 1,000 coins of any denomination every hour it spends eating them; it will eat Electrum Pieces with less enthusiasm. The piglet remains the same size regardless of how many coins are inside it.

The piglet is exceptionally loyal and will listen to commands given by you and allies you designate. It walks beside you or the nearest designated ally in their space as best it can, but it vanishes into a pocket dimension if neither you nor a designated ally is within 30 feet of it. The figurine can be magically summoned to you or a designated ally as a Bonus Action by using the command words, "Come home, little piggy." You or a designated ally can tell the figurine to return to its pocket dimension by taking a Bonus Action to use the command words, "Go to market, little piggy."

When asking for 10 percent or more of its total stockpile, the piglet looks disappointed before carrying out the request. The piglet can eject its own stopper and roll over on its back to empty itself of coins when it's asked for a large amount, but it will always retain at least one Copper Piece unless you physically remove it. The figurine returns to its inanimate form when there are no more coins inside it.

The piglet is a Tiny object and can be attacked while it is animate. It has AC 10, HP 5, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability to Bludgeoning damage. If the piglet drops to 0 Hit Points, it cries out and shatters into hundreds of ceramic pieces, causing the coins inside it to scatter. The piglet rematerializes before you again after 1d4 days. If you die, the piglet becomes distraught and empties itself of all its coins, returning to its inanimate ceramic form atop whatever coins were inside it.

Placing the piglet inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. When this happens, the piglet is permanently destroyed, and its contents are lost. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Total Cover is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way and can't be reopened.

name: Puzzle Ring of Vitality, Life, and Power

description.value: This ring is blessed by a god of life and healing. While wearing the ring, you can use your Lay On Hands on a creature up to 10 feet away from you instead of needing to touch it.

description.name: The Outer Ring
description.value: The inner, golden ring is covered by a silver puzzle ring that grants various benefits. The puzzle ring is made up of three distinct bands. As the bands are fitted together in an elaborate and ever-changing puzzle, you radiate an aura that heals and supports you and your allies. As a Study action while holding or wearing the ring, you can attempt to solve one band of the puzzle, which must each be attempted within a set amount of time and in a fixed order:

entries: The first band slides into place with a successful DC 5 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check. Once solved, you begin to radiate an aura in a 30-foot Emanation, which lasts for 1 minute. When you create the aura and at the start of each of your turns while it persists, you can restore 2d6 Hit Points to one creature in it.

The second band can then be solved with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check. When it slides into place, the aura's power increases. While in the aura, you and your allies have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximums can't be reduced. If an ally with 0 Hit Points starts its turn in the aura, that ally regains 1 Hit Point.

After that, the third and final band can be solved with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check. When the band fits into place to complete the puzzle, the aura's power is maximized. While in the aura, you and your allies have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. When an affected creature makes a saving throw against a spell or magical effect that allows a save to take only half damage, it takes no damage if it succeeds on the save.

description.value: The aura ends early if you take off the ring or drop to 0 Hit Points. Once the aura ends, this property can't be used again until 1 day has passed for each band that you solved. If you solve all three bands, roll 1d3 when the aura ends. On a 1 or 2, the number of days that must pass before this property can be used again is reduced by the number rolled. On a 3, this property can be used again immediately.

This old, withered hammer seemingly belongs in a swamp. Regardless of the conditions the hammer is kept in, it is always damp and smells of bog water. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The hammer has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Magic action, you can expend 1 or more charges and slam the hammer into the ground at a point within 5 feet of you. The area in a 5-foot-radius circle centered on that point transforms into a sickly, swamp that lasts for 1 minute. This area is Difficult Terrain. For each charge you expend after the first, the circle's radius increases by 5 feet. While you're holding the hammer, you can traverse the magical swamp as if it were normal terrain.
If you expend the last charge from the hammer, roll 1d20. On a 1, the hammer turns into viscous muck in your hands and is destroyed.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

As a Magic action, you can smash the hammer into the ground at a point within 5 feet of you or throw it at a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, sending out intense tremors in a 10-foot-radius circle centered on that point. Each creature in the area other than you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **2d6** Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
Fashioned from the scales of a quake drake, this armor rumbles softly with the sound of thunder during storms. While wearing it, you have Resistance to Thunder damage.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

This humble acorn is one of the mightiest gifts a Faerie queen can bestow upon her subjects. While holding the acorn, you can cast the __Wish__ spell. After using the acorn in this way, it immediately teleports back to the queen who bestowed it.

If the __Wish__ spell is used in a way that the queen would perceive as a threat to herself or her realm, the spell does not work. Instead, the creature who made the wish immediately transforms into an oak tree. Only a __Wish__ spell cast with the Queen's Token can return a creature transformed in this way to its original state.

This curious contraption is in fact a small, surreptitious Hand Crossbow that can be worn on a wrist or forearm without requiring a free hand to use it. In order to use the crossbow, you must also wear two special rings on adjacent fingers on the arm the weapon is attached to. One ring carries a thin but flexible string that connects to the firing mechanism of the crossbow. The other ring is equipped with a very small but functional blade that's used to sever the first ring's string. When the string is severed, the crossbow fires. It takes 1 minute to reload the crossbow and reset its rings.

While the rings are set and the crossbow is loaded, you can take a Bonus Action to make a ranged attack roll with it. Alternatively, you can make this attack roll as a Reaction at the start of your first turn of a combat.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This small orb of silver, watery liquid is strangely dry to the touch. While holding the 1-inch-diameter metallic sphere in the palm of your hand, you can mentally control the form that it takes as a Magic action. The liquid stretches and turns into the imagined shape and remains centered in your hand.

Regardless of the form, it can be no larger than the palm of your hand and is always a liquid. You can cause the liquid to revert to its natural orb state at any time (no action required). It immediately reverts if it leaves your hand. Consuming the liquid is harmless, but it takes 1d4 days to exit the body.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose one of the following damage types: Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The first time each turn that you hit a target with a weapon attack using ammunition drawn from this quiver, the attack deals an extra **1d6** damage of the chosen type.
This Maul has a narrow Shield covering its handle that can be rotated to protect the wielder's grip. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While wielding the guarded Maul, taking the Dodge action also gives you a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll while you're benefiting from the Dodge action, you can take a Reaction to make a melee attack with the Maul against that creature. On a hit, the attack deals an extra **1d8** Radiant damage. Once you take this Reaction, you lose the Maul's bonus to AC until you take the Dodge action again.

This punch knife style weapon is carved from a single chunk of superconductive dark violet metal that binds to the fist and forearm with black leather straps.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you score a Critical Hit against a creature with this magic weapon, that creature takes an extra **2d6** Lightning damage. Additionally, while you are attuned to this magical weapon, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and you can cast __Jump__ on yourself.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

When you hit with an attack as part of an Attack action using this magic dagger and apply your Sneak Attack to the damage roll, you can make an additional attack using this dagger as part of the same action. If that attack hits and meets the criteria for your Sneak Attack, you can apply half your Sneak Attack dice (rounded down) to the attack's damage.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Rat Tooth Dagger requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Fluid]**: Venom
**[Hide]**: Bark
**[Natural Weapons]**: Claws from a Ratling

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

These pungent weapons are made of leather of dubious origin with clumps of fur still attached. The leather grip fits snugly over the knuckles, with rat teeth and bits of bone sticking out the outward facing side. It gives off an unpleasant odor.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with these magic weapons. While you are attuned to these weapons, you have Immunity to magical contagions. Any creature who takes damage from this Constitution saving throw or contract Sewer Plague. When you score a Critical Hit against a creature with these magic weapons, it takes an extra **2d4** Necrotic damage and has Disadvantage on saving throws against magical contagions for seven days.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This sticky paste is fashioned from the powdered bone armor of a bone trader. After you treat a weapon, Shield, or other item that can be wielded in one or two hands with the paste, you can take a Bonus Action to summon and equip it, as long as the item is within 30 feet of you. After using this effect three times, it loses its potency.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Force damage on a hit instead of Piercing. While attuned to the weapon, you can cast the __Mending__ cantrip from it.

A special, needle-like Bolt is magically bound to the crossbow. When fired, this Bolt leaves a faint thread of arcane energy behind it. The Bolt returns to the crossbow and loads itself after each attack made with it, allowing you to ignore the crossbow's Loading property.

The crossbow has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with this crossbow's special Bolt, you can expend 1 charge to tether the target to a point on the ground within 5 feet of it. If the target attempts to move more than 10 feet away from that point before the end of its next turn, it must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target's Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

If the special Bolt is somehow destroyed or lost, it reappears loaded in the crossbow after 24 hours. The weapon functions like a nonmagical crossbow while separated from the Bolt for longer than 1 minute.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you must make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw whenever you attempt to begin a Short or Long Rest. On a failed save, you are overcome with the urge to craft and are forced to sew, knit, crochet, or cross-stitch feverishly for at least 1 hour before being able to rest.

description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

When you drink this potion, you are filled with intense and violent vigor, gaining 3d8 Temporary Hit Points. For 1 minute, when one of your enemies dies within 30 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to regain 1d8 Hit Points.
The base of this glass potion bottle is shaped like a skull, and the images of scythes run up its neck.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: For 1 minute after drinking this potion, when you hit a *Bloodied* creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, the creature takes an extra **1d8** Necrotic damage.
This dragon scale robe is miraculously insulated and comfortable. While wearing the robe, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You can tolerate temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower without any additional protection.
Your Constitution increases by 2, to a maximum of 22.
You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.
You have Resistance to Fire damage.
You can stand on and move across molten rock, unharmed, as if it were solid ground.

description.value: The hem of this robe glimmers with slowly shifting embers. While wearing the robe, your steps leave behind small motes of harmless fire and scorched earth that disappear after 1 second.

This magic shield is formed from the shell of an Anomollusk combined with leather from an aberration as its handle. It's fused together and coated in contaminated ichor and inset with a rare animus. Once complete, the shell gives off an otherworldly hue that shimmers in kaleidoscopic patterns. The shield can reflect attacks and magic.

When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, you can use your Reaction to cause the creature to take the same damage (you still take the damage).

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Reflector Shield requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
**[Hide]**: Shell from an Anomollusk
**[Hide]**: Skin from an Aberration

description.value: When you drink this bright purple potion, you immediately gain the benefits of a short rest.
After you consume a Rejuvenation Potion, you can't benefit from consuming another until you finish a 1d4 Long Rests.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Rejuvenation Potion requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Dust]**: Fey Dust
**[Fluid]**: Any Elemental Fluid
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Dragon
**[Organ]**: Heart from a Fiend

name: Relentless Bulwark
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Cleric or Paladin)

description.value: This hefty metal Shield is virtually impenetrable. The Shield has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Shield, you can expend 1 charge to cast the __Shield of Faith__ spell from it. Whenever you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain *Concentration* on the spell, you can take a Reaction and expend another charge to succeed on the save instead. You can only take this Reaction if you're holding the Shield.

name: Repeater Crossbow

description.name: Magazine
description.value: A weapon with the Magazine property also has a number and an ammunition type. The weapon holds that amount and type of ammunition, which you can expend before needing to reload the weapon. As a Bonus Action, you may remove a Magazine and then reload it with a new Magazine. A Magazine weapon comes with two empty magazines included in the weapon's cost and weight. An additional empty magazine for a Magazine weapon costs 25 GP. Loading an empty Magazine with ammunition takes 1 minute.

description.name: Repeater
description.value: Repeater weapons can fire ammo in quick succession, using multiple barrels or quick-reloading mechanisms. When you take the Attack action with a Repeater weapon, you can shoot multiple times if you have features that let you attack more than once as part of that action, such as Extra Attack. After taking the Attack action you can use a Bonus Action to attack once with the same weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the Bonus Action's attack, unless that modifier is negative.

description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Repeater
description.value: Repeater weapons can fire ammo in quick succession, using multiple barrels or quick-reloading mechanisms. When you take the Attack action with a Repeater weapon, you can shoot multiple times if you have features that let you attack more than once as part of that action, such as Extra Attack. After taking the Attack action you can use a Bonus Action to attack once with the same weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the Bonus Action's attack, unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Magazine

A Magazine weapon comes with two empty magazines included in the weapon's cost and weight. An additional empty magazine for a Magazine weapon costs 25 GP. description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

description.value: This foul-smelling concoction is made from the remains of stinking sludge. As an action, you can throw the vial up to 10 feet, where it breaks and releases a noxious vapor that fills a 30-foot-radius Sphere. Each creature in the area with the Incapacitated, Stunned, or Unconscious condition ends those conditions. Each dying creature in the area has Advantage on its next Death Saving Throw. Each creature that was not dying and did not have any of those conditions must instead succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

This steel Shield hides a slim chamber in its center where magical flora grow, accumulating toxic pollen. The chamber is covered with an intricate, interlocking series of metal plates and flaps that can be released, unfurling to a shape that resembles a flower.

While holding the Shield with its plates collapsed, you can take a Reaction when a Large or smaller creature you can see within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll to release the interlocked plates and fire the accumulated pollen at the attacker. When you do, that creature must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes **3d10** Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk when the flowers accumulate another wave of pollen.

Curious, whirring mechanisms inside the Shield automatically retract the chamber's unfurled metallic plates at dusk. Alternatively, you can manually collapse the Shield's plates over the course of 1 minute.

This Shield has a hidden compartment inside it that can fire thick squid ink at attacking creatures. When a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to press a button on the Shield's handle, spraying ink from the front of the Shield. The attacker must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Blinded condition until the start of its next turn.

If the Shield is filled with a Vial of squid ink (worth 20+ GP), the effect uses a save DC of 13. If it's filled with a bottle of common Ink (worth 10 GP), it uses a save DC of 10 instead. The Shield can be used in this way up to three times before its ink needs to be refilled, which takes 1 minute.

This Shield is a mechanical item whose purpose and functionality can be discerned by taking a Study action to make a DC 12 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check. On a success, you understand what the Shield does, how to use it, and how to take care of it. You also understand that filling the Shield with other volatile or sticky liquids (such as acid, poison, grog, or oil) or any solid material (such as sand) will damage the machinery inside and take 8 hours of work to repair.

These boots are crafted from the flesh and scales of a dragon and decorated with Harpy feathers and the webbed membranes of flying creatures. The soles are injected with goopy ooze, allowing their wearer to jump back in time and space.

You can use a Bonus Action on your turn to click the heels of these boots together. When you do, you teleport to the space you occupied at the start of your turn so long as it is currently unoccupied.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Retracer Boots requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Fluid]**: Goopy Ooze
**[Hide]**: Scales from a Dragon
**[Hide]**: Webbed Membrane
**[Hair]**: Feathers from a Harpy
**[Organ]**: Flesh from a Dragon

description.value: This mechanized shield retracts into a bracer worn on the forearm. With a quick motion, it can be expanded just as an opponent believes they've snuck a blow.

You can wear the Retractable Shield as a bracer on your forearm, and it does not count as having that hand occupied while the shield is retracted. As a Reaction to an attack hitting you, you can extend the shield, giving you a bonus to your Armor Class equal to your Proficiency Bonus against that attack. If this changes the attack from a hit into a miss, you may make one melee attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against the provoking creature if they are within reach. The shield remains extended until the start of your next turn.
As a free interaction with an object on your turn, you can either extend or retract the shield. While the shield is extended, it occupies your hand and confers a +2 bonus to your Armor Class.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Returning
description.value: A Returning weapon allows you to hurl the weapon in such a way that it returns to you. When you make a ranged attack with a Returning weapon, the weapon returns to you immediately after hitting or missing the target. You can catch the weapon if you have a hand free to do so.

name: Revelry Suit

description.value: This bulky suit is made from natural materials, including fur, canvas, and straw. Its mask is exceptionally oversized and shaped into a sun, smiling in an unsettling way. While you wear this armor, you gain a +2 bonus to AC, and it grants the following properties.

description.name: Dancing Dodge
description.value: When you fail a Dexterity saving throw, if your Speed isn't 0, you can use this property to succeed instead. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Wild Steps
description.value: As a Bonus Action, you can move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

description.name: Dancing Curse
description.value: When you roll Initiative, you must make a DC 0 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you gain the Incapacitated condition, and your Speed is 0 until the start of your next turn as you perform a folk dance. When you use the Dancing Dodge or Wild Steps properties, the DC of the saving throw increases by 2. The DC of this curse can't increase again until you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

name: Revolver

description.value: An iconic handgun, the Revolver stores six bullets in a rotating cylinder. This weapon is favored by Gunslingers for its reliability and stopping-power.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Recoil
description.value: After you make an attack with this weapon, you can't make ranged attacks beyond the weapon's normal range until the end of the current turn.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.
