description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Swift
description.value: Swift weapons help you recover quickly from missed attacks. When you miss with a Swift weapon, you have Advantage on the first attack roll you make with the weapon against the same target before the end of your next turn. If that attack hits, it also deals an extra **1d4** damage of the weapon's normal damage type.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of a __Detect Magic__ spell (no *Concentration* required) for 10 minutes, and during that time, you have Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) checks to discern hidden motives or deception.
This potion is stored in a round glass flask. An iron band wraps around the bottle, ornamented with a goat's skull.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: For the duration, you also gain the effect of the __See Invisibility__ spell.

name: Signet Rings of Blindness, Deafness, and Silence

description.value: Each of these three signets is decorated with the carving of a skull and a pair of skeletal hands that cover either its eyes (blindness), ears (deafness), or mouth (in an area of silence). Each ring has 1 charge, which it regains daily at dawn. If you are wearing the corresponding signet when you have the Blinded or Deafened condition or are in an area of magical silence, you can expend that ring's charge (no action required) to end that condition or speak a word or phrase (such as a spell's Verbal component) that can be heard through magical silence. Wearing the rings together as a set combines their collective charges, potentially allowing you to use one ring's property multiple times.

name: Signet Rings of the Fey Court
type: very rare (requires attunement by an Elf or Fey Creature)

description.value: This set of wooden rings once belonged to a powerful Fey who ruled over a domain on the Feywild. You must be wearing all four rings in order to attune to them and use their magic. While wearing the rings, you know the __Druidcraft__ cantrip. In addition, you gain the Elf's Trance trait if you don't already have it.

Each ring has an associated season: autumn, spring, summer, or winter. The four rings each contain 2 charges and regain all expended charges when you finish a Long Rest. Once a ring has no remaining charges, the small landscape adorning the top of it withers until it regains its charges.

description.name: Season's Resistance
description.value: You can expend 1 of a particular ring's charges as a Reaction when you take damage of the type corresponding to that ring: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold). When you do, you have Resistance to that damage type until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering damage.

description.name: Magic Resistance
description.value: You can expend any 2 charges from the rings as a Reaction when an enemy targets you with a spell or other magical effect. When you do, you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering spell or effect. The 2 charges don't need to be from the same ring.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the __Silence__ spell (no *Concentration* required) as a 20-foot Emanation originating from you for 10 minutes, and for the duration, squid tentacles emerge from your mouth.
This sculpted clay jar is painted in a deep blue and adorned with squid tentacles. Uncorking it reduces all noise in the area as if you are underwater, and the liquid within is a coppery blue-green.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: For the duration, you can spit ink from your mouth as a Bonus Action. One creature within 30 feet of you makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target gains the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target is immune to this property for the next 24 hours.

This pair of magic, smooth socks are iridescent and oily to the touch. While wearing both socks on your feet, you can use them to cast the __Grease__ spell (save DC 13) centered on a point within 5 feet of you. The magical oil runs off the socks to the ground at your feet, causing the ground to become slick. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This small silver bell exudes Divination magic, especially while under a full moon. While hung, the bell rings a unique, magical melody if a Lycanthrope passes within 15 feet of it, or within 60 feet of it during a full moon. The melody sounds quiet but is nevertheless audible out to 100 feet. Different kinds of Lycanthropes cause the bell to emit a different melodies.

While this pewter stein holds at least a sip's worth of potable alcohol, the face adorning it comes alive to sing songs based on the kind of drink it contains (examples are shown in the table below). If there are multiple kinds of alcohol within the stein, it either alternates between song types or does its best to combine their various lyrics. The stein isn't sentient, but it does have a pleasant singing voice. If there are multiple Singing Steins in the same room, they can sing together in harmony if they have the same kind of drink within them.

If the drink inside the stein is poisoned, it sings songs slightly out of key, which can be discerned by a creature that takes a Search action to make a successful Wisdom (*Perception*) check. The DC for this check is determined by the GM.
You can place this golden ear cuff over your ear as a Magic action. While wearing the cuff, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition.
Tapping the ear cuff twice (no action required) causes you to have the Deafened condition, although you can still faintly hear the sound of the ocean. Doing so again ends this effect on you.

Created from the ichor in a potbelly's stomach-pot, this volatile concoction is effective at damaging inorganic substances. As a Magic action, you can hurl the serum at a Construct or an object that you can see within 30 feet of you. The target makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking **10d6** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.name: Acid
description.value: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.
Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.name: Alchemist's Fire
description.value: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.
This ammunition works like an Armor-Piercing Melee weapon, but you fire the ammunition as a projectile from a Ranged weapon.

When you hit with Blessed ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Radiant. Also, if the target is Fiend, Fey, or Undead, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Designed to open wide wounds, such as with a broad-bladed arrowhead, Brutal ammunition works like a __Brutal__ Melee weapon.

When you hit with Desecrated ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Necrotic. Also, if the target is Celestial, Humanoid, or Plant, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.name: Holy Water
description.value: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.
When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional **1d4** Fire damage.

Advanced Ammunition named after a damage type deals that damage type. Arrows and bolts can have wide heads that deal Slashing damage or blunt tips that deal Bludgeoning damage. A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.
Advanced Ammunition that has the Ranging property is lighter and better made than common counterparts. When you fire Ranging ammo, you can increase your weapon's normal range by 50 percent.
Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

description.name: War Oil
description.value: A target hit by a piece of Alchemical Ammunition packed with War Oil takes damage as normal for the ammunition, then becomes coated in War Oil for up to 1 minute. Alternatively, you can target a point, such as the ground or a wall, and on an attack roll against AC 10, cause the War Oil to spill out of the ammunition, creating a circular patch of the viscous substance with a 10-foot radius.

War Oil is slick and highly flammable. An area coated in War Oil counts as Difficult Terrain, and a creature that starting its turn in a coated area or enters the coated area for the first time on a turn must succeed a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or gain the Prone condition and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the end of its turn. Additionally, if a creature or area coated with War

Oil is exposed to an open flame or some other source of Fire damage, the oil ignites. The ignited oil burns for two rounds, dealing **2d4** Fire damage to any creature or object who comes in contact with it, and an additional **2d4** Fire damage to any creature that ends its turn while in contact with it. An ignited creature can douse the flames by using an action.
After burning for two rounds, being doused, or remaining unlit for 1 minute, War Oil dries up and ceases to be slippery or flammable.

Ammunition with the Whistling property creates a high-pitched sound after firing. This sound is audible out to 300 feet from the ammo as it flies. Whistling ammo isn't heavier, but it catches the air with intricate baffles to create its sound, so its maximum range is half normal. Whistling ammo deals Bludgeoning damage.

This wicked Sling is devastating against foes larger than yourself. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the Sling, the target takes an extra **1d4** Force damage for each size larger than you that it is, to a maximum of 3d4.

In addition, when you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this Sling, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away from you and have the Prone condition. If the target is Large or larger, it has Disadvantage on the save.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This hearty root vegetable is grown by the Clerics and champions of a god of war and combat, whose strength is said to make its way to the Material Plane through their gardens. If you eat one of these vaguely fist-shaped potatoes, your hands itch for the thrill of combat for 1 hour. For the duration, you can roll 1d4 in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strikes, provided you make the attack with one of your hands. Each additional Smash Potato you eat extends the duration by 1 hour. You can eat up to three of these potatoes before needing to finish a Long Rest to benefit from them again.

As a Utilize action, you can throw this smoky glass vial to a space up to 30 feet away. When the vial breaks, the concoction creates a 10-foot-radius Sphere of smoke. The area is Heavily Obscured. The smoke lasts for 1d4 + 2 rounds, or half as long in a windy area.

name: Sniper Rifle

description.value: An instrument of ranged precision, the Sniper Rifle can take shots from distant, nearly invisible ranges.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Loading
description.value: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Sighted
description.value: Attacking at long range with this weapon doesn't impose Disadvantage on your attack rolls. When you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon at long range, you can reroll any of the damage dice and must use the new roll.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.value: This dark metal Sickle was forged with an unusually harsh angle and has a unique power over light and shadow. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d6** Psychic damage on a hit.

While holding the weapon, you can use a command word as a Magic action to extinguish nonmagical flames within 60 feet of you. Any area of Bright Light or Dim Light within 60 feet of you that was created by a spell is also dispelled as if it were targeted by __Dispel Magic__ (+4 spellcasting ability modifier). Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

As a Magic action, you can draw your hand over the Sickle's handle to extend it downward, turning the Sickle into the form of a scythe wreathed in shadow. While in this form, the weapon has the Two-Handed and Reach properties, and the extra Psychic damage it deals on a hit increases to 2d6.
As a Bonus Action while holding the scythe, you can magically return it to its Sickle form.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

When a creature regains Hit Points at the end of a Short Rest by spending one or more of its Hit Point Dice, that creature magically regains extra Hit Points if it spent the Short Rest snuggling with one of these enchanted toys. The rare dragon variant of the snugglebeast restores 3d6 Hit Points.

A creature can only benefit from one Snugglebeast at a time. Once this property of the Snugglebeast is used by a creature, that creature can't benefit from the same Snugglebeast's magic again until it finishes a Long Rest.

When a creature regains Hit Points at the end of a Short Rest by spending one or more of its Hit Point Dice, that creature magically regains extra Hit Points if it spent the Short Rest snuggling with one of these enchanted toys. The common owlbear variant of the snugglebeast restores 1d6 Hit Points.

A creature can only benefit from one Snugglebeast at a time. Once this property of the Snugglebeast is used by a creature, that creature can't benefit from the same Snugglebeast's magic again until it finishes a Long Rest.

When a creature regains Hit Points at the end of a Short Rest by spending one or more of its Hit Point Dice, that creature magically regains extra Hit Points if it spent the Short Rest snuggling with one of these enchanted toys. The very rare tarrasque variant of the snugglebeast restores 4d6 Hit Points.

A creature can only benefit from one Snugglebeast at a time. Once this property of the Snugglebeast is used by a creature, that creature can't benefit from the same Snugglebeast's magic again until it finishes a Long Rest.

When a creature regains Hit Points at the end of a Short Rest by spending one or more of its Hit Point Dice, that creature magically regains extra Hit Points if it spent the Short Rest snuggling with one of these enchanted toys. The uncommon unicorn variant of the snugglebeast restores 2d6 Hit Points.

A creature can only benefit from one Snugglebeast at a time. Once this property of the Snugglebeast is used by a creature, that creature can't benefit from the same Snugglebeast's magic again until it finishes a Long Rest.
Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

entries: Snugglebeast (Owlbear)
Snugglebeast (Unicorn)
Snugglebeast (Dragon)
Snugglebeast (Tarrasque)

description.value: A soarsled is a crystalline disk 5 feet in diameter. It can carry a passenger through the air, using the same principles as the buttresses that sustain the towers of Sharn.

While within Sharn or another Syranian manifest zone, you can stand on the sled and take a Magic action to mentally activate it, causing it to hover beneath you. Once per turn, you can mentally command the hovering sled to move up to 30 feet in any direction. The sled can carry up to 400 pounds, and stops hovering when you step off it.
Each turn, you can take a Magic action to make a DC 12 Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check, moving the sled up to an additional 60 feet on a success.

While outside a Syranian manifest zone, the plane's energies rapidly fade, and the Soarsled can only be activated once, by taking a Magic action. When it has been used to fly for a total of 10 minutes, or when you deactivate it by stepping off it, it loses its energy and can't be used again until it spends at least 8 hours in a Syranian manifest zone.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest while wearing these comfortable enchanted socks, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Constitution modifier. You must be wearing both socks on your feet in order to gain this benefit.

This smooth and weighty stone has a dusk-colored gem embedded in its center. When pressed to the chest of a creature who has been dead for less than one minute, the stone captures a fragment of the dead creature's soul for later use.

The Soulbond Stone has 3 charges. While holding the stone, you can expend 1 charge to cast __Speak With Dead__ with the stone, as if the trapped soul's corpse was the target of the spell. When the last charge is expended, the stone shatters and the soul fragment returns to its rightful place.

This small oval stone is engraved with Fernian glyphs. While you are holding the stone, you can take a Bonus Action to touch a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar object, instantly igniting it into flame.

These scarab-like symbionts, bred by the daelkyr Valaara, have brilliant, iridescent shells. To attune to it, you must place it on your head; during the process of Attunement, it burrows through your skull, establishing a psychic connection with you. While it lacks human consciousness, it possesses a strange alien sentience that responds to your desires. There are tales of rare Spellburrows that possess greater knowledge and sentience; such stories sometimes end with the Spellburrow consuming the brain of the wizard who pushed it too far—but these are surely just fanciful stories!

A Spellburrow knows one cantrip of the DM's choice drawn from the Sorcerer or Warlock spell list, and you can cast this cantrip as if you know it. In addition, a Spellburrow knows one level 1 spell and one level 2 spell from the same spell list its cantrip is from. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic class feature, you can cast these spells as if you had prepared them, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You can choose to use either your Intelligence modifier, or a spellcasting ability modifier you have gained from another source, for these spells.

description.name: Symbiotic Nature
description.value: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

This robe is spun from special, magic-sensitive threads, causing arcane glyphs to appear on it whenever you cast a spell. While wearing the robe and not wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 10 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

In addition, whenever you cast a level 1+ spell while wearing the robe, you can change its apparent style, color, and material. Regardless of its appearance, it is always a robe and its weight remains the same.

This pair of Daggers is made using the harvested fangs of a large, venomous spider. When you hit the same creature on your turn with both Daggers, that creature must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take an extra **2d4** Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This large tree seed is 1 foot long and is surrounded by a protective cone. If you're attuned to the seed and plant it and its cone in soil, it immediately takes root and begins to grow rapidly, becoming fully grown after 30 days. The stem of the seed's cone is vaguely key-shaped, and it breaks off in your hand when planted. While you're attuned to the seed, the stem magically remains on your person at all times.

Once planted, no other creature can attune to the seed. Your attunement to the seed doesn't end as a result of being more than 100 feet away from it for at least 24 hours, but rather only after being on a different plane of existence than it for at least 24 hours. It also doesn't end as a result of you dying, but rather only after you've been dead for more than 1 minute. If your attunement ends after the seed has begun to grow but before it becomes fully grown, the tree dies and the seed is destroyed.

Once fully grown, the spire tree is 300 feet tall and 40 feet in diameter at its base, which tapers gently inward toward the top of the tree. Its canopy extends out in a 30-foot Emanation around the tree. Soil beneath the tree's canopy is exceptionally rich and fertile.

At the base of this magic tree is a door large enough for Medium creatures to enter. The door is guarded by a Dryad who is loyal to you and allies you designate. The dryad accepts the seed's stem as proof of ownership and uses it as a key to open the door. If your attunement to the seed ends before the dryad first opens the door, the stem disintegrates and the door can't be opened. Once opened, your attunement to the seed ends, and the tree belongs to you. You and your designated allies can freely enter and leave the tree.

Inside the tree are ten floors. You choose how to distribute the floors throughout the tree. A wooden spiral staircase climbs upward through the center of the tree and its floors. Each floor has ten small windows that can't be seen from outside the tree. In addition, the interior of the tree can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through magical scrying sensors, and it can't be entered using teleportation or interplanar travel.

The tree has AC 20; HP 500; Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage except that which is dealt by siege equipment, magic items, spells, or other magical effects; and Resistance to all other damage. The door has AC 15, HP 100, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. The tree regains 1d6 Hit Points daily at dawn. If a part of the tree, such as the door, is destroyed, that part regrows after 7 days.

If the tree is attacked, it immediately creates a Treant at its base to defend it. The treant isn't under your control and acts in accordance with its normal disposition and alignment, doing its best to defend the tree. The treant disappears at dawn or when it drops to 0 Hit Points. Once the tree creates a treant in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

Neither the treant nor the dryad can move farther than 1 mile away from the tree. If the dryad drops to 0 Hit Points, it vanishes, reappearing at the base of the tree at the next dawn. If you or one of your allies kills the dryad, it doesn't reappear, and the tree becomes nonmagical. The tree is still hollow inside with the floors you'd chosen, but its windows and all its magical properties are lost.
The tree creates another Spire Seed once every 100 years.

If you're not proficient with Pikes, you are nevertheless proficient with this weapon while you're attuned to it. When you cast the __Spiritual Weapon__ spell while holding the Pike, you can cause it to dissolve into the air to make the spell's spectral weapon take the form of the Spirit Pike. On a hit, with the spectral weapon, the target takes Force damage equal to 1d10 plus your spellcasting ability modifier instead of the spell's normal damage. If you cast __Spiritual Weapon__ using a higher-level spell slot, the spell's damage still increases by 1d8 for every slot level above 2.
Your hands are left free when you dissolve the Pike in this way. When the spell ends, the Pike reappears in your hand or on the ground at your feet if your hands are full.

In addition, the weapon has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with an attack roll using the Pike as either a physical or spectral weapon, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra **1d8** Radiant damage to the target.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This Shortbow can cause an Arrow to shatter and unleash a devastating spray of magical shrapnel. As a Magic action, you can use a command word to destroy one nonmagical Arrow you have nocked in the bow and send splintering shards of arcane energy out in front of you. When you do, each creature in a 15-foot Cone must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **2d6** Piercing damage, or **3d6** Piercing damage if the creature was within 5 feet of you.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This Halberd's haft is made of rough, dark wood and is miraculously easy to heft. The bladed end of the Halberd looks like a hatchet that's been absorbed by the hewn wood. While holding the Halberd with two hands, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action to magically split the weapon into its more basic components.

When you do, the Halberd deconstructs in your hands, leaving you with a Handaxe in one hand and Quarterstaff in the other. Both the Handaxe and Quarterstaff have the Light property. You can combine the two weapons to reform the Halberd by repeating the command word as a Bonus Action while you're holding both the Handaxe and the Quarterstaff.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If the weapon is split into the Handaxe and Quarterstaff, the bonus is a +1 with each weapon instead.

description.name: Halberd
description.value: If you hit a creature with the Halberd and roll a 10 on the damage die, that creature's energy is sapped. Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and your Speed increases by 10 feet for the same duration.

description.name: Handaxe and Quarterstaff
description.value: If you're wielding the Handaxe and Quarterstaff in different hands, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class, and when you make an extra attack as a result of using these weapons' Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage. The Quarterstaff deals Necrotic damage on a hit, and it deals maximum damage to plants and Plant creatures. Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the Handaxe, it flies back to your hand.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This enormous squash is strangely durable and makes for a functional magic weapon. Druids wielding this weapon can use their Wisdom modifier instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of melee attacks using it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

This wooden staff is made from the harvested claws of a braerog. It has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and cause thorn-covered rose vines to sprout up, covering a 20-foot square centered on a point within 5 feet of you. This area becomes Difficult Terrain.
Once created, the briars are non-magical. They grow (or wither) as appropriate for the environment, just as a normal plant would.
The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff turns into rose petals and is lost forever.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

name: Staff of Farryn of the Greenwood (Legendary)

description.value: This twisted wooden staff is crowned by a trinket-adorned deer's skull. It was fashioned by Farryn before she delved into the dark lore of Gorthos. Soft, fragrant moss and earthy mushrooms grow along the staff's length.

While holding the staff, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the staff's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Living Ward (Rare+)
description.value: You have Resistance to Necrotic damage.

description.name: Servant of the Cycle (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Cure Wounds__ (level 3 version) from the staff. When you do so, the next time you hit with an attack before the end of your next turn, the target takes an extra **1d10** Necrotic damage. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Cycle's Balance (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Revivify__ from the staff. When you do so, the next time a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast in the next hour, it and creatures of your choice within 20 feet of it take **4d10** Necrotic damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Sacrifice of Flesh (Very Rare+)
description.value: When a spell you cast restores Hit Points, you can take Necrotic damage up to twice the level of the spell that can't be reduced or prevented in any way. If you do so, the target regains additional Hit Points equal to three times the damage you take.

description.name: Death Blossom (Legendary)
description.value: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you dies, you can take a Reaction to make flowers bloom around them. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of the dead creature regain 4d8 Hit Points and gain 2d8 Temporary Hit Points. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

name: Staff of Favorable Winds
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard)

description.value: While holding this staff, Difficult Terrain caused by wind doesn't cost you extra movement. The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: __Cone of Cold__ (5 charges), __Feather Fall__ (1 charge), __Gust of Wind__ (2 charges), or __Wind Wall__ (3 charges).

In addition, while holding the staff, you can take a Magic action to create a harmless sensory effect using the air around you. For example, you can cause leaves to rustle, slam shutters closed in a sudden gust, or cause your clothing to billow dramatically.
The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff turns to dust and is blown away by a sudden flurry of wind.

name: Staff of the Four Seasons
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard)

description.value: This staff's form changes with the seasons. It has 10 charges and can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. As long as the staff has at least 1 charge, your melee attacks with it deal an extra **1d8** damage on a hit. This extra damage's type is based on the staff's season: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold).
Over the course of 10 minutes, you can focus on the staff to change its form to a different season. It remains in this form for 8 hours before reverting to the current season again.

While holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spell attack modifier. The spells you can cast from the staff in this way are determined by its season, as shown in the table below.
The staff regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff loses all foliage and vitality, becoming a gnarled, nonmagical Quarterstaff.

rows: Guiding Bolt (1 charge), Moonbeam (2 charges), Plant Growth (3 charges)
Burning Hands (1 charge), Spike Growth (2 charges), Fireball (3 charges)
Inflict Wounds (1 charge), Pass Without Trace (2 charges), Vampiric Touch (3 charges)
Color Spray (1 charge), Darkvision (2 charges), Sleet Storm (3 charges)

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This magic stone staff weighs 10 pounds and has the bust of a magpie at its top. While holding the staff, you gain a +1 bonus to Wisdom (*Perception*) checks you make to search for treasure or a specific item you're looking for.

The staff has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can expend some charges to cast either Fly (3 charges) or Locate Object (2 charges) from it. The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff becomes a nonmagical Quarterstaff as the magpie springs to life and flies away.

description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
This staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff vanishes and is lost.

description.name: Spells
description.value: You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC; you gain a +2 bonus to your spell save DC when casting a spell in this way: __Disguise Self__ (1 charge), __Hallucinatory Terrain__ (4 charges), __Invisibility__ (2 charges), __Mirror Image__ (2 charges), __Mislead__ (5 charges), or __Silent Image__ (1 charge).

description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This dark wooden staff is carved in the shape of a majestic stallion. The staff has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can expend 1 charge to cast the __Phantom Steed__ spell from it. In addition, you can use a command word while holding the staff and expend 1 charge to take the Dash action as a Bonus Action.

The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff breaks in two as if bitten and is destroyed. When this happens, the sound of hooves can be heard galloping away in an indiscernible direction.
