description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This staff was made as a means of worship rather than war by a retired warrior using the weapons he'd once wielded. The staff is adorned with blades and channels the inner focus of a warrior. This staff can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. Even if you aren't attuned to the staff, attacks with it can deal either Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage on a hit (your choice each time).

This staff has 10 charges. While attuned to the staff, you know the __True Strike__ cantrip. When you cast this spell while holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to enhance the spell in one or more of the following ways:
You can expend 2 charges to cast the spell as a Bonus Action.
You can expend 1 charge to cause the next attack roll made against the target before the end of your next turn to have Advantage.
On a hit, you can expend 1 charge to cause the attack to deal an extra **1d6** Radiant damage.

The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff becomes a nonmagical Quarterstaff, but attacks with it can still deal either Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This ebony staff bears a bronze spear tip and additional blades carved to depict a winged scarab. The staff can be wielded as a magic spear that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. You are considered proficient with this weapon while you are attuned to it, even if you aren't proficient with spears. While holding the staff, you gain these benefits:

entries: **Spell Power**: You gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls.
**Cull Subjects**: Humanoids have a -2 penalty to saving throws against your spells.
**Spell Shield**: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells that target only you.

description.name: Cursed
description.value: This staff is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with __Remove Curse__ or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the staff, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls made with weapons other than this one.

While cursed, you must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw each day at midnight. On a failed save, your Hit Point maximum is reduced by 10 unless you are Undead. Your Hit Point maximum can only be restored by a __Wish__ spell. If your Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0 while cursed, you die and immediately rise as a __Wight__.

This magic Spear is made of dark, polished granite and has a large ruby set in its head. Though it is made of stone, it weighs no more than a normal Spear and is enchanted to prevent it from shattering. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Spear has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. While you're within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a Magic action and expend 1 charge to plunge the Spear into that surface. The Spear vanishes into the stone or earth and emerges as a sharp stone spike, 1 foot wide and 10 feet long, from another stone or earthen surface that you can see within 60 feet of you, such as the ground or a cave wall. The spike erupts perpendicularly from that surface and forces any creature in a 5-foot-wide, 10-foot-long Line in that direction to make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **4d6** Piercing damage and is pushed up to 5 feet away from the spike. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

While you're within 60 feet of the stone spike and within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to magically recall the Spear. The stone spike crumbles, and the Spear inside vanishes back into the surface it erupted from before reemerging from the surface next to you into your open hand. If you don't have an open hand, it falls to the ground at your feet.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This ocular organ, harvested from a living Aberration, melds with the skull of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your scalp during the Attunement process. At the end of this time, the stalk burrows into your skull and bonds with your brain. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Stalk Symbiote.
While attuned to this item, you gain the following benefits:

entries: **Symbiotic Senses**: You have Advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks, and you do not have Disadvantage on Initiative rolls when surprised.
**Aberrant Power**: If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, you have blindsight with a range of 10 feet.

**Symbiote Link**: You cannot voluntarily end your Attunement to the Stalk Symbiote. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in 1d4 hours unless you receive a __Remove Curse__ spell before it grows back (which also ends your Attunement).

description.value: This heavy steel ring is set with a chunk of shimmering star metal. While wearing this ring, your appendages are crusted with iridescent star metal. Your Unarmed Strikes are considered magical and deal Force damage.

This glowing Morningstar sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet while you hold it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d4** Radiant damage on a hit. In addition, you can cast the __Daylight__ spell using the weapon. Once the weapon has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This roughly crafted metal ring seems to have an otherworldly pull on other metallic items. While touching an object with the hand that bears this ring, you can spend 1 hour forging a magical bond between the ring and the object, provided the object weighs no more than 25 pounds and is at least 50 percent metal. Only one object can be bound to the ring in this way at a time.

While wearing the ring, you can take a Bonus Action on your turn to magically pull its bound object up to 20 feet toward you, provided the object is within 40 feet of you and isn't behind Total Cover. The pulled object bounces harmlessly off of creatures and other objects in its path. If you pull the object into your space, you can catch it in your free hand if you have one. Otherwise, it falls to the ground at your feet.

This open metal Shield hovers above its paired gauntlet, protecting you but leaving your hand free. While wearing the gauntlet, you are considered to be wielding the Shield, but you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class instead of a Shield's normal bonus to AC. Whenever you're targeted by an attack roll made with a metal weapon or projectile, this bonus becomes +3 instead.

description.name: Shooting Star
description.value: While wearing the gauntlet, you can take a Magic action to throw the Shield, bouncing it between clustered targets before it returns to your arm. Choose up to three creatures, objects, or points. The first target must be within 30 feet of you, and any additional targets the Shield bounces toward must be within 10 feet of the target before it. You can't select the same target more than once each time you throw the Shield.

Make a ranged attack roll against each target. The targets gain no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover for the attack. You are proficient with these attacks and add either your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) to their attack rolls and damage rolls. On a hit, the target takes **2d8** Slashing damage. The Shield flies back to the gauntlet after reaching its final target. It bounces harmlessly off of any other creatures or objects in its path.

This magic weapon is forged using iron from the stars. While you're attuned to this weapon, you can call upon its latent stellar energy to catalyze change within the metal, creating endothermic and exothermic reactions. The weapon can be fissioned into two separated Battleaxes or fused back into a Greataxe. It has the following properties based on its current state.

description.name: Fused State (Greataxe)
description.value: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **2d6** Fire damage on a hit. While holding the axe, flames erupt from its edges and a small star burns in its center. These flames shed Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. The light is sunlight.

description.name: Fissioned State (Battleaxes)
description.value: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with each of these magic weapons, which deal an extra **1d6** Cold damage on a hit. The axes orbit you slowly while they aren't being held or stowed. You can equip an orbiting Battleaxe as if it were sheathed. In addition, if you take the Attack action on your turn, you can take a Bonus Action to make one melee attack with an orbiting Battleaxe against a target you can see within 20 feet of you.

description.name: State Change
description.value: This weapon can change between its two states using the following properties:

description.name: Fission
description.value: While holding the fused Greataxe, you can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to magically split it apart into its fissioned state. When you do, electrical energy is released, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes **3d6** Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

description.name: Fusion
description.value: While holding both fissioned Battleaxes, you can take a Bonus Action and use another command word to magically recombine the weapon into its fused state. When you do, the sudden generation of heat creates a wave of fire around you, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes **3d6** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This Light Hammer was forged using the remains of a comet and is cold to the touch. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra **1d4** Cold damage on a hit. The hammer leaves behind a crackling mist when thrown, and it flies back to your hand immediately after making a ranged attack with it.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

These shoes allow you to freely change the sound of your steps while wearing them. Changing the sound of your steps doesn't change their volume but can make them sound as though the shoes are made of a different material. For example, your steps can sound like a beggar's bare feet, a dancer's sharp heels, or an approaching guard's metal boots.

This black iron needle easily pierces the skin. If a creature's mouth is sewn shut with a Stitching Needle, it loses the ability to speak and cast spells with verbal components. The creature gains the ability to communicate with Telepathy out to a range of 60 feet.
Stitching the mouth of a willing, Unconscious, or Incapacitated creature takes 10 minutes. Removing the stitches takes 1 minute.

name: Storm Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Storm__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Storm__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Storm Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Storm__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Storm__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Storm Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Storm__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Storm__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

This Sickle sparks with electricity as beads of water form and drip from its blade. The weapon can be used to make special ranged attacks by slashing it through the air to send out blades of storming wind.

You're proficient with these attacks, which have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, use your Strength modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls, and deal **1d4** Slashing damage on a hit.
Attacks with this magic Sickle deal an extra **1d4** Lightning damage on a hit, regardless of whether you attack with the weapon itself or use its special ranged attack.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

You have a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you make a ranged attack with the Trident, it deals an extra **1d8** Lightning damage on a hit. Immediately after hitting or missing, you can use the chain attached to the weapon's handle to pull it back to your hand as a Bonus Action.

In addition, this Trident acts as a conduit for the sky's ferocious power. Immediately after hitting a creature with the Trident, you can call down a bolt of lightning upon the target, provided it's unobstructed from the sky. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking **6d10** Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that is submerged in water or wearing metal armor has Disadvantage on the save, and you have Immunity to the Lightning damage dealt by this effect. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Impale
description.value: As a Magic action, you can try to impale and pull a creature toward you. If the target is no more than one size larger than you, make a ranged attack against it using the Trident. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet toward you.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

name: Storm's Embrace
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Storm__)

description.value: When you fall while wearing this ring, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

This wooden Quarterstaff has been scarred by lightning, and an amplifying crystal is embedded at its head. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1 Lightning damage on a hit.

Whenever the Quarterstaff takes Lightning damage or you take Lightning damage while holding it (from a source other than the Quarterstaff itself), the crystal glows brilliantly and pulses with electrical energy for 1 minute. It also glows in this way while under the effect of the __Shillelagh__ spell. While the crystal is glowing in this way, it emits Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet, and the extra Lightning damage the Quarterstaff deals on a hit increases to 1d6.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This stained grey jacket has long arms reaching the floor and contains dozens of restraining straps. This magical jacket takes 10 minutes to don or doff. While wearing this item and not wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you add your Intelligence modifier to your Armor Class. Also, you can cast spells without using Somatic or Material components that don't have a GP value listed. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Aberrant Horror Transformation, you may roll twice whenever rolling on the [Unstable Form table](https://5e.tools/tables.html#unstable%20form_grimhollowpg24) and choose either result.

name: Submachine Gun

description.value: Firing lighter, easier to control rounds, the Submachine Gun is an effective alternative to larger automatic weapons.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Automatic
description.value: When you make an attack with this weapon, you can choose to make two attacks instead. These attacks are always made with Disadvantage, regardless of circumstance. You can't replace these attacks. If this weapon has Ammunition, these attacks use twice the normal amount of ammunition.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.value: This suit of comfortable woolen clothes, made from the wool of the rare and dangerous poffer, includes a shirt, trousers or a kilt, and thick socks. While wearing the suit, you have Resistance to Lightning damage, and you don't suffer effects from extreme cold weather.

These black leather goggles are set with cloudy glass that completely obscures the eyes of the wearer. You can take an action to don or doff these goggles. While wearing these goggles, you ignore your Sunlight Sensitivity, as well as any other ill effects you would suffer due to exposure to sunlight. The goggles also block your Darkvision, preventing you from seeing in the dark.

This gelatinous Net is made with the enchanted remains of a gray ooze. A creature takes **1d6** Acid damage when it gains the Restrained condition from the Net, and it takes that damage again at the end of each of its turns until that condition ends. If the creature is wearing nonmagical metal armor, its armor is partly corroded and takes a cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers whenever it takes Acid damage at the end of one of its turns. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10. The penalty can be removed by casting the __Mending__ spell on the armor. A creature other than you who touches the Net takes **1d6** Acid damage.

The Net's sticky composition makes it more difficult to escape from than a mundane one. To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. Destroying the Net (AC 10; 5 HP; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage; Resistance to all other damage) also frees the target, ending the effect and tearing the Net apart.

The torn Net is harmless. If more than half of the Net can be salvaged and stored within a container large enough to hold 5 gallons of liquid for 12 hours, the Net is repaired and can be used once more. Your attunement to the Net ends if the Net remains torn for longer than 48 hours.

You have Immunity to damage from the Net while you're attuned to it. Picking up the Net after throwing it renders it harmless until the next time you throw it. The Net deals no Acid damage if there isn't a creature attuned to it.
This gnarled, oak staff ends in a crook reminiscent of a swan's neck. It is clearly ancient, and was only recently uncovered from deep within an elven ruin.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Once a day, if the wielder is reduced to 0 Hit Points, the Swansong Staff immediately animates (using the stats of an __Animated Broom__) to protect them. The weapon acts on the wielder's initiative. If the animated weapon is reduced to 0 Hit Points or if its wielder regains consciousness, it becomes inanimate once more.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
While wearing these supple leather boots, Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Swashbuckler's Boots requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any
**[Dust]**: Fey Dust
**[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
**[Hide]**: Any

name: Switch
type: very rare (requires attunement by a Druid)

description.value: This simple, springy rod is made of twisting vines and twigs. While holding the rod, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature as a Bonus Action to activate it, magically transforming it into a weapon. It can take the form of any kind of Simple or Martial weapon of your choice that deals Bludgeoning or Piercing damage and lacks the Loading and Reach properties. If you transform the rod into a weapon with the Ammunition property, it magically creates its own ammunition when you make a ranged attack with it.

Regardless of the weapon's form, you're proficient with it and can use your Wisdom modifier for its attack and damage rolls instead of Strength or Dexterity. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra **1d8** damage of its normal type.

While holding the weapon, you can take a Bonus Action to transform it into another qualifying weapon or temporarily back into its rod form until you transform it into a weapon again. Alternatively, you can expend a second use of your Wild Shape feature as a Magic action to extend the bark of the activated rod or weapon to your body, covering yourself in treelike armor. When you do, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to four times your Druid level, and until the rod deactivates, you have an Armor Class of 17 if your AC is lower than that.

The rod deactivates after a number of hours equal to half your Druid level (round down), immediately reverting to its rod form if it's still a weapon. It deactivates early if you drop to 0 Hit Points or choose to deactivate it as a Bonus Action.

This peculiar brass Longsword is hollow and has lute strings that run along its blade, allowing you to use it as a Musical Instrument and Spellcasting Focus. You are proficient with the Sword of Resonance as both an instrument and Longsword while you're attuned to it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Finesse property.

In addition, the sword's hollow metal blade magically amplifies the music made when using it to inspire allies. Whenever you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration while holding the sword, it begins to reverberate with thunderous energy. The next time you hit a target with an attack using the sword before the end of your next turn, that target takes an extra **1d6** Thunder damage from the attack.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

name: Sword of the Crimson Abbot (Legendary)

description.value: This powerful, fiendish sword was once wielded by the Crimson Abbot. While it was created as a gift that brought evil and malice to the corrupted former knight, it has lost its connections to the Crimson Rose. However, its evil origins still linger within. The sword is sleek and polished, with a blade that absorbs light. A blood-red ruby on the hilt is fitted within a setting of thorns and roses.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by the sword's rarity. While holding the sword, you can use the following properties.

description.name: Blood Drain (Rare+)
description.value: When you hit a creature with the sword, it takes an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage.

description.name: Irresistible Hunger (Very Rare+)
description.value: Necrotic damage you deal ignores Resistance.

description.name: Vampiric Charm (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Charm Person__ (save DC = 16 + the sword's bonus, no *Concentration* required) from the sword. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Embrace of the Duchess (Legendary)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can touch the sword to the body of a Humanoid that has been dead for 1 minute or less. The creature must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma saving throw (as if it were alive) or become a __Vampire Spawn__ that dies again at dawn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Stolen Life (Legendary)
description.value: When you deal Necrotic damage with the Blood Drain property, you can expend and roll one Hit Points Die. You regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus the Necrotic damage dealt.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: This sword seems to absorb any light that touches it, making it appear darker than the deepest midnight. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the sword, you treat any magical light or Darkness within 30 feet of you as if it were nonmagical, and you can breathe normally in any environment.

In addition, this sword has 2 charges and regains 1d2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the sword, you can expend 1 charge to cast __Counterspell__ from it. When cast in this way, the target automatically fails its saving throw if the triggering spell is level 5 or lower, and it automatically succeeds if the spell is level 6 or higher. If you successfully interrupt a spell in this way, you can choose to absorb it into the sword instead of allowing it to dissipate. The absorbed spell must have a casting time of an action or a Bonus Action. The sword can have only one absorbed spell at a time.

While holding the sword, you can release its absorbed spell. Doing so requires you to take a Magic action or Bonus Action (as determined by the spell's normal casting time), and it uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell.
The interrupted spell remains absorbed by the sword for 8 hours or until it's released. Absorbing a new spell replaces the one stored within the sword.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

The dreadful talisman is crafted from the skull at the center of a gore elemental. When you kill a creature with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike while you wear the talisman, you gain 10 Temporary Hit Points for 1 minute.
While you have any of these Temporary Hit Points, your melee weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes deal an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage on a hit.

While you are holding this wand, your voice and other sounds you produce are three times as loud as normal. House Phiarlan makes use of a similar device, the Thunderous Amulet, that leaves the wearer's hands free.

These leather gloves are outfitted with the talons of fallen beasts and stitched together with the arcane stitching of apothecary creations. The gloves are then empowered by elemental magic, reinforced with bone, and powered by an animus.
While wearing these gloves, you gain Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and your Unarmed Strikes deal an additional **1d6** Piercing damage on a hit.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Talon Gloves requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
**[Hair]**: Stitches
**[Hide]**: Skin
**[Natural Weapons]**: Claws

name: Talyard the Great's Wand of Power

description.value: This normal-looking spruce stick is actually the wand of a famous drunkard. A drunken creature that sees the stick perceives it as a magnificent, colorful wand that radiates with an awesome power.

This wand has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dusk. While you're drunk and are holding the wand, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (+3 spellcasting ability modifier) from it: __Heroism__ (1 charge), __Lesser Restoration__ (2 charges), or __Thaumaturgy__ (0 charges).

As a Magic action, you can crush this small, green gem underfoot to activate its magic. When you do, plants in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you instantaneously become healthy and full. Fruit and vegetable-bearing plants in the area grow their produce, which become ripe over the course of 1 hour. If there are no plants within range or you crush the gem against an inorganic material, fertile topsoil 1 inch deep spreads across the area. Healthy green grass immediately grows from the new soil.

This magical set of stone gauntlets imbues your fists with the power of the Elemental Plane of Earth. While wearing the gauntlets, your Unarmed Strikes with your fists deal **1d8** Bludgeoning damage instead of the usual Bludgeoning damage (unless it's already higher), and they deal double damage to objects and structures. In addition, these gauntlets have 15 charges and regain 1d10 + 5 expended charges daily at dawn. When you make an Unarmed Strike using your fists, you can expend up to 5 charges to extend your fist's reach by 5 feet for each expended charge.

description.name: Powerglove
description.value: When you hit a target with an Unarmed Strike, you can expend up to 3 charges to deal an extra **1d8** Bludgeoning damage for each charge spent. If you spend any charges in this way, the target must also succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet away from you.

description.name: Geomancy
description.value: You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from them: __Earthquake__ (8 charges), __Move Earth__ (6 charges), __Shatter__ (2 charges), __Spike Growth__ (2 charges, with stone projections), or __Wall of Stone__ (5 charges).

description.name: Tectonic Plate Armor
description.value: As a Magic action, you can cause rocks to envelop and protect your body. For 1 hour, you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, your Speed is halved, and you have Disadvantage on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws. You can end this property early as a Bonus Action. While enveloped in this way, you can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone using a Burrow Speed of 30 feet. While doing so, you don't disturb the material you move through. If you end this property while burrowed in this way, you're shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take **1d10** Force damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

description.name: Curse
description.value: These gauntlets are cursed. Your mind and body become sluggish once you attune to the gauntlets. The gauntlets become one with your flesh and prevent you from removing them. Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, and your Intelligence score is reduced by 4 (to a minimum of 7) while cursed. The curse remains even if the attunement ends but can be undone by any effect that removes a curse such as a __Greater Restoration__ or __Remove Curse__ spell, allowing you to remove the gauntlets and end the curse on you.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: The gauntlets have the following random properties:

entries: 1 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) property
1 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property

description.name: Destroying the Gauntlets
description.value: The gauntlets can only be destroyed in the depths of the crystalline mines of Durhun on the Elemental Plane of Earth where they were first created.

You can take a Bonus Action on your turn to extend or retract this mechanical weapon by twisting its handle. The weapon is a normal Lance while it's extended. If the Lance is retracted, the end of the weapon rests inside the wider, bladed base, and it is treated as a Greatsword instead. This Greatsword deals **1d10** Slashing damage on a hit instead of 2d6.

While using the weapon as a Greatsword, you can choose to extend it as a Bonus Action immediately after hitting a target with an attack. If you do so and the target is a Large or smaller creature, it's pushed 5 feet away from you.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This cherry-sized bloodstone heart is the beating center of a poppet. While the stone is on your person, when you gain the Frightened condition, you can make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you end the Frightened condition.

Also, when you make an Intelligence ability check while holding the stone, you can listen to it, gaining unusual insight or access to esoteric lore. If you do so, you gain Advantage on that Intelligence check. The Telltale Heart can't be used this way again until the next dawn.
While wearing this cape, you have Resistance to Lightning damage, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws against spells and other effects that deal Lightning damage.

While wearing the cape, you can take a Magic action and use a command word to transform into a bolt of lightning. When you do, choose an unoccupied space that you can see within 120 feet of you. You immediately travel in your lightning form to the chosen space without provoking Opportunity Attacks, filling a 5-foot-wide Line in your path. Other creatures in the Line or within 5 feet of either your old or new location must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking **3d10** Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This whip is made from the tentacles and guts of aberrant creatures, stitched to the webbed membranes of winged beasts and fused to the bark of a plant creature. Once the animus is placed, the tentacles begin to writhe and wriggle and the whip can latch and drag creatures along the ground with uncanny strength.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic whip, which has a reach of 20 feet.
Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with an attack using this weapon, you can pull it 10 feet towards you.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Tentacle Whip requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Hair]**: Stitches
**[Hide]**: Bark
**[Hide]**: Webbed Membrane
**[Natural Weapons]**: Tentacles from an Aberration

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This seemingly overgrown Quiver keeps a large plant magically concealed inside it, and it can hold up to 20 Arrows or Bolts. When you draw an Arrow or Bolt from the Quiver, you can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to magically connect the end of the ammunition to the plant inside the Quiver. The plant is a ropelike vine that flies effortless behind its connected piece of ammunition when fired. It becomes taut and climbable if the ammunition hits an object or surface, able to hold up to 250 pounds before bursting.

While wearing the Quiver, you can take a Bonus Action to magically retract the vine and its connected ammunition up to 60 feet back into the Quiver. If the connected ammunition hit an object that weighs less than 25 pounds, that object is also pulled back toward the Quiver when the vine is retracted in this way.

If you hit a creature with a piece of ammunition that was connected to the vine, the vine magically disconnects itself from the ammunition and falls. You can disconnect the vine from its connected ammunition by taking a Bonus Action to repeat the command word or sever the vine from the Quiver.

The vine grows up to 120 feet long, and a connected piece of ammunition can't be fired longer than the vine's current length. If any portion of the vine is severed, it regrows up to 30 feet of length daily at dawn. A severed portion of vine becomes a mundane length of Rope.

name: The Bag

description.value: This weathered old satchel has three tarnished silver buckles that hold it shut. There are faint bloodstains on the inside of the flap, and the bag occasionally ripples as if something inside is moving. The bag functions as a Bag of Holding and has the following additional properties.

description.name: Inhabitant
description.value: A __Lurker in the Dark__ lives in the bag's extradimensional space. If reduced to 0 Hit Points, the lurker vanishes and reappears in the bag at the next midnight. The lurker only dies if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points by a creature holding a toy or stuffed animal once owned by a child. If the lurker is killed, the bag loses its magic, and anything in it appears in unoccupied spaces closest to the bag.

description.name: The Bag's Claw
description.value: While holding the bag, you can take a Bonus Action to have the lurker in the dark lash out with its claw at a creature within 5 feet of you. Make a melee attack roll with a +7 bonus. On a hit, the claw deals **1d10 + 4** Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from the claw, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Lurker's Curse
description.value: When you finish a Long Rest, roll 1d6. On a 1, the lurker slipped out of the bag during the rest and caused mayhem in a nearby area, such as attacking people, causing livestock to sicken, or spoiling provisions.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

description.value: These leather bags have the stylized face of a griffon on their front and appear across the multiverse in strange locations. One may be found in the belly of a dragon, while another in the limbs of a great tree. Regardless of where it's found, a Griffon's Saddlebag is typically discovered by an adventurer with a destiny.

The saddlebags are made by a great, six-armed griffon on the Astral Plane named Criir. Believed by some to be a demigod of pocket dimensions and craftsmen everywhere, Criir is a patron of artificers and creators across the multiverse.

The griffon creates magic items in its great forge using materials collected from various planes of existence to add to their collection. While no one knows exactly how to contact Criir, the astral griffon has a knack for knowing what items are needed by whom.

description.name: Superior Holding
description.value: This 1-foot-wide bag always weighs 3 pounds, regardless of what's inside it. It functions as a Bag of Holding that can only be pierced by another Artifact. Placing a Bag of Holding, Heward's Handy Haversack , Portable Hole, or similar item inside the extradimensional space created by the saddlebag, or vice versa, destroys the other extradimensional item but leaves the saddlebag unharmed. Any item stored within the other extradimensional space is magically moved to the space within the saddlebag instead. If doing so overloads the bag, random contents from either space are scattered in the Astral Plane until the bag isn't overloaded.

description.name: Magic Courier
description.value: At the GM's discretion, the saddlebag's beak opens up to reveal a letter. The magical script can be read by any creature with an Intelligence of 4 or higher. The note is a delivery request or similar task that includes the name of an item as well as either specific or vague descriptions of a person or place. At the bottom of the letter is a price listed in coins or other form of payment as well as a date or time depending on the task's urgency.

If the saddlebag is brought to the described person or place within the allotted time, it dispenses the magic item into the hand of the appropriate recipient. If the payment isn't received by the bag within 1 hour of dispensing the magic item, the item vanishes and is lost. After receiving the payment for an item in this way, the bag's beak reopens to dispense a reward for the courier.

description.name: Sell Magic Items
description.value: The saddlebag has a connection to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane. Depending on the magic item, you can sell a magic item to the saddlebag for half the cost of its base price.

description.name: Spells
description.value: The saddlebag has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the saddlebag, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it: __Detect Magic__ (1 charge), __Identify__ (1 charge), or __Legend Lore__ (5 charges).

description.name: Additional Spells
description.value: At the GM's discretion, such as after reaching certain milestones or completing Magic Courier quests, the saddlebag may offer one or more of the following additional spells that can be cast from it: __Blink__ (3 charges), __Dimension Door__ (4 charges), Divination (4 charges), __Etherealness__ (7 charges), __Fly__ (3 charges), __Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion__ (7 charges), __Plane Shift__ (7 charges), or __Leomund's Secret Chest__ (4 charges).

description.name: Sentience
description.value: The saddlebag is a sentient Chaotic Neutral item with an Intelligence of 13, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and normal vision with a range of 60 feet.

The bag knows Common. When in the presence of only creatures it trusts, the bag can speak audibly, its beak moving as it speaks. Otherwise, the bag communicates telepathically with its wearer. The bag can also speak and communicate with griffons.

description.name: Personality
description.value: The bag's purpose is to carry, collect, and deliver magic items. Different bags have different personalities, but they are for the most part largely pleasant to talk to. Their voices are birdlike and are filled with occasional coos and squawks, and their stitched eyes widen, squint, and move expressively.

If the wearer or its allies fail to fulfill the bag's Magic Courier quests, it may stop offering its magic to them. If it does, their items may be lost or inaccessible within the bag or potentially spat out. While the bag provides the names of item recipients and delivery locations, it doesn't know any more information than what was provided to it by the astral griffon. Regardless, it does its best to help its wearer and allies find the specified person or location on the letter.

description.name: Destroying the Griffon's Saddlebag
description.value: While there is no way to permanently destroy the saddlebag, piercing it with an Artifact returns it to its place of origin for repair before it's returned to the multiverse in a new location. Placing a Griffon's Saddlebag inside the extradimensional space created by another Griffon's Saddlebag returns both items to their place of origin and sends all the items stored within them to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane.

A thin, leather-bound volume, The King in Yellow contains a dreamlike play that compels a reader to obsess over the text. They read the play again and again, slowly coming to believe that the disconnected scenes and strange vistas it describes are real.

description.name: Language:
description.value: Common (XPHB).

description.name: Attunement Check:
description.value: Charisma (*Performance*) DC 15. Unlike other tomes, you are compelled to make this check when inspecting The King in Yellow. If you succeed, you attune to the book. To end your Attunement to the King in Yellow, you must meet Hastur.

description.name: Benefits:
description.value: While attuned to The King in Yellow, you gain the following benefits:

entries: You gain Advantage on all Charisma (*Performance*) checks.
You gain Advantage on all Charisma (*Deception*) checks as long as your lie involves characters, scenes, and locations drawn from The King in Yellow.

You can cast __Contact Deity__. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. When you cast that spell using this item, you always contact Hastur.

Each time you finish a Long Rest, roll a d20. On a 1 you can cast __Call Deity__ to summon Hastur. You lose access to this benefit if you finish a Long Rest without using it. If you do not use the spell, you gain a level of Exhaustion that cannot be removed while you are attuned to this item.

description.name: Drawbacks:
description.value: You have Disadvantage on all Wisdom (*Perception*), Wisdom (*Insight*), and Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks, as images of Carcosa dance in your mind, distracting you from the increasing unreal world around you.

description.name: Insight-Lost Carcosa (+20):
description.value: You must find lost Carcosa and gaze upon forgotten Lake Hali. There, in that dreadful realm, you will finally find peace. No matter the cost, you must find the path there. You see omens and signs of Carcosa in the strangest places. The depths of ancient dungeons. The entrails of a slain enemy. Every sign points you back to Carcosa, again and again.

description.name: Lore:
description.value: The King in Yellow allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about Hastur and elements associated with it.

This silver Rapier has a rose adorning its crossguard and pommel and has thorns lining its hilt. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If you make an attack with the weapon against a Fey or a creature that is shape-shifted, the target takes an extra **1d8** Radiant damage on a hit.

description.name: Field of Roses
description.value: As a Magic action, you can use a command word and touch the Rapier's point to the ground at your feet. When you do, silver rosebushes sprout from the ground in a 25-foot square centered on your location. The area becomes Difficult Terrain until the rosebushes disappear. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes **2d4** Piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels. While holding the Rapier, this Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement, and you don't take damage from moving into or within the area. The rosebushes disappear after 1 minute or when you dismiss them as a Bonus Action. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

This magical spying device, designed by gnome engineers on behalf of the Ebon Syndicate, is composed of two crystal orbs. The Emitter Orb is marble-sized, making it easy to slip into your target's purse or pocket. The Receiver Orb is fist-sized.

You can take a Magic action and touch the two orbs together to activate them for 7 days. Once activated, the Emitter Orb begins capturing thoughts within a 5-foot Sphere centered on it. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, that creature is immune to the effect for 24 hours. On a failed save, the holder of the Received Orb becomes immediately aware of that creature's surface thoughts for 1 minute, even if it leaves the area.

This ornate hand mirror, made of carved iron and adorned with images of grasping hands, can be used to contact other planes. As a Magic action, you can speak the true name of an extraplanar being, such as a Fey, Fiend, or Celestial, into the mirror three times. This summons the named creature in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mirror.

A creature summoned this way retains its free will, and there is no guarantee it views you as an ally. It cannot leave this plane for 1 minute, after which time it automatically returns to its home plane unless it has the means to travel between planes on its own, in which case it can choose to stay.

Bred by the daelkyr Valaara, this bizarre symbiont burrows into the palm of its host, secreting razor-sharp chitin blades that can also be used as throwing weapons. When you attune to the scarab, it fuses with one of your hands, visible only as an iridescent, chitinous growth on your palm.

For every attack you make as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can extrude a shard of razor-sharp chitin from the symbiont into your empty hand, using it for the attack. The shard counts as a magical Simple Melee weapon with which you are proficient. It has the Finesse, Light, and Thrown properties with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. On a hit, it deals **1d4** Piercing damage and **1d4** Acid damage. The shard dissolves as soon as it hits or misses its target.

description.name: Symbiotic Nature
description.value: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

This Flail has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As long as the Flail has at least 1 charge, you deal an extra **1d6** Lightning damage to the first target you hit with it on each of your turns.

While holding the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to cast the __Thunderwave__ spell (save DC 15) from the ball of the Flail. Alternatively, if you make a melee attack using the Flail, you can immediately expend 1 charge to cast __Thunderwave__ as a Bonus Action in the direction of the attack's target.

The ball of the Flail is attached to its chain with a powerful magnetic connection that can be released at will. The Flail can be used to make special ranged attacks by releasing the ball mid-swing. You're proficient with these attacks, which have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, use your Strength modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls, and deal **1d8** Bludgeoning damage on a hit. While the ball is within 60 feet of you, you can magically pull it up to 20 feet toward you as a Bonus Action. It bounces harmlessly off of creatures and other objects in its path. The ball magically reattaches itself to the chain when it enters your space.

While the ball is detached, you can still use the Flail to cast __Thunderwave__. When you do, the spell originates from the ball, affecting creatures in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the ball instead of the spell having its normal area of effect.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

name: Thuranni Cloak
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Shadow__)

description.value: While you wear this cloak, it magically projects an illusion that makes you appear to be standing in a place near your actual location, causing any creature to have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. If you take damage, the property ceases to function until the start of your next turn. This property is suppressed while your Speed is 0.

This rod is a magical Musical Instrument developed by the gnomes of Zilargo. While holding the rod, you can take a Magic action to produce auditory illusions that unerringly replicate the sound of any instrument with which you're proficient, with an effect similar to the __Minor Illusion__ spell, with the sound emanating from the rod. To determine the quality of the performance, make a Charisma check with the Musical Instrument you're replicating. If you are proficient with the Thurimbar Rod, you can produce unearthly music unlike any natural instrument.

description.name: Tool (Musical Instrument)
description.value: If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

This festive Quarterstaff is decorated with ribbons and other glittering elements. It is perfectly balanced and seems to be made to perform with. This magic Quarterstaff has the Finesse property. In addition, you have a +1 bonus to Charisma (*Performance*) checks you make in order to put on an entertaining performance using the Quarterstaff.

description.name: Punishing Parry
description.value: This Quarterstaff has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Quarterstaff, you can expend 1 charge as a Reaction when a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack. When you do, roll 1d6. You gain a bonus to Armor Class equal to the number rolled against that attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss. If the attack misses you as a result of this bonus to AC, you can immediately make one attack with the Quarterstaff against the attacking creature as part of the same Reaction. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to the number rolled on the d6.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

This magical axe is imbued with a destructive force that builds with each consecutive strike. You have a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon equal to the number of charges it currently has. The Handaxe gains 1 charge each time you hit a target with it, up to a maximum of 3 charges. When Timber gains its third charge, the built-up energy immediately explodes; it loses all charges, and the target takes an extra **3d6** Force damage, or **6d6** Force damage if it's made of wood. When this happens, if the target is no more than one size larger than you, you can choose to push it up to 10 feet away from you.
Timber's charges last for up to 1 minute. It loses all charges if you miss with an attack using it, make an attack against a different target, or make an attack using a different weapon.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

The inner workings of this clockwork device are formed from gears forged from magical constructs gathered around a focusing lens, held together carefully by the needles of magical creatures. The animus used harnesses the energy of The Algorithm, a being of order and consequence, whose control over time and space ripples from the strange clockworks of the medallion.
This medallion has 3 charges. It crumbles to dust when you expend the final charge.

You can expend 1 charge from the medallion to take an extra action on your turn. Each time you do, you can roll 1d6. On a 1, at the end of your turn, you become unstuck in time and space as the medallion casts the __Maze__ spell on you. On a 6, the medallion regains 1d3 charges.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating the Time Dilation medallion requires a Legendary Workshop and the following Legendary Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from The Algorithm*
**[Hide]**: Plates from a Construct
**[Natural Weapon]**: Any Needles
**[Organ]**: Eye from a Construct

description.value: ** At the Game Master's discretion, the animus could be any other Legendary Construct instead.*

This item appears to be a sword hilt that has a small hole on either end of it. The hilt is made of clear quartz and contains an hourglass with sand inside it. Despite the holes on the hilt, the sand never seems to flow out of the hourglass. You can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to cause it to magically form a thin blade of sand. The hourglass spills sand from the bottom of the hilt that circulates up and around to form the blade and guard of a Rapier before returning to the hourglass again through the hole at the top. You can take a Bonus Action and repeat the command word to cause all the sand to return to the hourglass. While the Rapier is formed, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While holding the hilt, you can cast either the Haste or __Slow__ spell (save DC 16) from it. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain *Concentration* on a spell cast in this way. While *Concentrating* on such a spell, the sands in the hourglass move quickly if you cast __Haste__ or more slowly if you cast __Slow__. Once the hilt has been used to cast one of these spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

If a Large or smaller creature hits you with a melee attack while you're wearing this cloak, you can take a Reaction to cause time to briefly warp around you. After taking the damage from the attack, you can immediately move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and the attacker's Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

When you drink this potion, you weep with inexpressible sorrow for 1 hour. During that time, you have Immunity to the Charmed condition, but your continued wailing prevents you from being silent. If you are Charmed when you drink the potion, the condition is suppressed for the duration. This glass bottle is topped with a small crypt angel carved from stone. The fluid within has the taste and consistency of tears and the colors of a rain cloud.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: Creatures within 10 feet of you that are Friendly to you also gain Immunity to the Charmed condition.

This small jade carving of a frog dangles from a simple cord of leather to be worn as a necklace. While you wear it, you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed and can hold your breath for up to 1 hour. In addition, you can cast the __Jump__ spell using the necklace, targeting only yourself. Once the necklace has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dusk.

description.name: Curse
description.value: This necklace is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you're targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic. Removing the necklace fails to end the curse on you. While you're cursed, your skin is perpetually slightly wet and clammy, and you have only an appetite for insects and other grubs instead of the foods you would normally enjoy eating.
This carbonated liquid, a potent distillation of faerie magic, is bright fuchsia and tastes of autumn rain. A Humanoid who drinks a Toadstool Toddy has Immunity to Fire and Cold damage for 1 hour.

This beautifully embossed book is full of gripping short stories. You can read a story from the book in 10 minutes. The underlying nature of each story is unclear, leaving your subconscious mind to slowly process and unpack its deeper meanings over the course of your next Long Rest.

The next time you finish a Long Rest after reading a story from the book, roll 1d20. On a roll of 10 or lower, you take **2d4** Psychic damage as your mind is plagued with intense terrors from the story you read. On a roll of 11 or higher, you gain 2d4 Temporary Hit Points as your mind is filled with joy and courage instead. If you start a story but don't finish reading it, nothing happens the next time you finish a Long Rest.

This coil of muscle terminates in a sharp barb. When you attune to it, this daelkyr-bred worm attaches to your throat and nestles under your tongue. You can take a Bonus Action to make an Unarmed Strike with the worm, using your choice of Strength or Dexterity for the attack. On a hit, you deal Piercing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike. In addition, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Symbiotic Nature
description.value: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a __Remove Curse__ spell or similar magic.

name: Tooth of the Jinxed Leviathan (Legendary)

description.value: This tooth is razor sharp and can be wielded as a Dagger. Its "hilt" is wrapped in alligator hide, and the flat of its blade flickers with magenta hex magic in carved glyphs.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the tooth, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Jinx of Dire Fortune (Rare+)
description.value: As a Bonus Action, you can force one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to make a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the tooth's bonus). On a failed save, the target is jinxed for 1 minute. While jinxed, when the target makes a D20 Test and rolls an even number on the d20, it must reroll the d20 and take the new roll. On a successful save, you must make the same saving throw, becoming jinxed for 1 minute on a failure. This property can't be used again while another creature is jinxed by it.

description.name: Exposed Weak Spot (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you make an attack roll with the tooth, you score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

description.name: Steal Unluck (Very Rare+)
description.value: When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of you makes a D20 Test with Advantage, you can take a Reaction to negate their Advantage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until a creature you can see makes a D20 Test and rolls a 1 on the d20, or until the next dusk.

description.name: Strange Fortunes (Legendary)
description.value: Each time you score a Critical Hit with the tooth against an enemy, the tooth gains a cumulative +3 bonus to damage rolls. This bonus is in addition to the bonus based on the tooth's rarity. When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll with the tooth, you take Force damage equal to the accumulated bonus. This property's damage bonus returns to +0 when you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [Heirloom Rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

properties: each fabled heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. the rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the [heirloom rarity](https://5e.tools/tables.html#heirloom%20rarity_crookedmoon24) table. an heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. the heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.
